example: Hello! How are you?
examplePt: Olá! Como você está?
tip: The most common way to greet someone. Used worldwide in English.

example: Hi, my name is Ana.
examplePt: Oi, meu nome é Ana.
tip: Shorter and more casual than 'Hello'. Used between friends.

example: Good morning, teacher!
examplePt: Bom dia, professor(a)!
tip: Two words. Said before noon, when the day is just starting.

example: Good afternoon, everyone.
examplePt: Boa tarde, todos.
tip: Two words. Said after noon, when the sun starts going down.

example: Good night, sleep well.
examplePt: Boa noite, durma bem.
tip: Said when parting at night or before going to sleep.

example: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
examplePt: Tchau, te vejo amanhã!
tip: A more formal farewell. Originated from 'God be with you'.

example: Bye! Have a nice day!
examplePt: Tchau! Tenha um bom dia!
tip: A quick, informal farewell. Very common among friends.

example: Can you help me, please?
examplePt: Você pode me ajudar, por favor?
tip: The magic word of politeness. Always makes a request sound nicer.

example: Thank you for your help.
examplePt: Obrigado(a) pela sua ajuda.
tip: 'Thanks' is the shorter version. The reply is 'You're welcome'.

example: Sorry, I'm late.
examplePt: Desculpa, estou atrasado(a).
tip: Said when you make a mistake or bump into someone accidentally.

example: Yes, I understand.
examplePt: Sim, eu entendo.
tip: Positive answer. The opposite is 'no'.

example: No, thank you.
examplePt: Não, obrigado(a).
tip: Negative answer. The opposite is 'yes'. Always polite to add 'thank you' after.

example: Welcome to my house!
examplePt: Bem-vindo(a) à minha casa!
tip: Also used in 'You're welcome' as a reply when someone thanks you.

example: Hi! How are you today?
examplePt: Oi! Como você está hoje?
tip: A classic conversation opener. The expected reply is 'Fine, thanks!'

example: I'm fine, thank you!
examplePt: Estou bem, obrigado(a)!
tip: The standard reply to 'How are you?'. 'I'm' is short for 'I am'.

example: Zero comes before one.
examplePt: Zero vem antes de um.
tip: The number before 1. On a thermometer, it means very cold! The word also means 'nothing' in English.

example: I have one brother.
examplePt: Eu tenho um irmão.
tip: The first whole number. Sounds like 'won' (past of win). Be careful!

example: She has two cats.
examplePt: Ela tem dois gatos.
tip: Sounds the same as 'too' (also) and 'to' (preposition). Three words, one sound!

example: There are three chairs.
examplePt: Há três cadeiras.
tip: The 'th' sound requires you to put your tongue between your teeth.

example: I have four friends.
examplePt: Eu tenho quatro amigos.
tip: Sounds like 'for' (purpose word). A table has this many legs.

example: Give me five minutes.
examplePt: Me dê cinco minutos.
tip: You have this many fingers on one hand. 'High ___!' means let's celebrate!

example: I wake up at six.
examplePt: Eu acordo às seis.
tip: Half of twelve. A cube (die) has this many faces.

example: There are seven days in a week.
examplePt: Há sete dias na semana.
tip: Considered a lucky number in many cultures. One week has this many days.

example: School starts at eight.
examplePt: A escola começa às oito.
tip: The 'gh' is completely silent. A spider has this many legs.

example: I go to bed at nine.
examplePt: Eu vou dormir às nove.
tip: One less than ten. Cats are said to have this many lives.

example: Count to ten.
examplePt: Conte até dez.
tip: The base of our number system. You have this many fingers on both hands.

example: Pick a lucky number.
examplePt: Escolha um número da sorte.
tip: The word for any digit or value, like 1, 5 or 100. We use numbers to count, measure, and tell the time.

example: I like red roses.
examplePt: Eu gosto de rosas vermelhas.
tip: The color of fire and stop signs. Also used to say you feel embarrassed ('turn red').

example: The sky is blue.
examplePt: O céu é azul.
tip: The color of the sky and ocean. 'Feeling blue' means feeling sad.

example: The grass is green.
examplePt: A grama é verde.
tip: The color of plants and nature. Traffic lights use it to say 'go'.

example: The sun is yellow.
examplePt: O sol é amarelo.
tip: The color of the sun and bananas. Used on caution signs.

example: I have a black cat.
examplePt: Eu tenho um gato preto.
tip: The absence of light. The opposite of white.

example: Snow is white.
examplePt: A neve é branca.
tip: The combination of all light colors. The opposite of black. Snow is this.

example: I like orange juice.
examplePt: Eu gosto de suco de laranja.
tip: Both a color AND a fruit! The color was actually named after the fruit.

example: She likes pink flowers.
examplePt: Ela gosta de flores rosas.
tip: A lighter, softer shade of red. Flamingos are famous for being this color.

example: Grapes are purple.
examplePt: Uvas são roxas.
tip: A mix of red and blue. Historically worn by kings and queens.

example: The dog is brown.
examplePt: O cachorro é marrom.
tip: The color of soil and wood. Chocolate and coffee are this color.

example: The clouds are gray.
examplePt: As nuvens estão cinzas.
tip: A mix of black and white. Clouds on a rainy day are this color.

example: I have three dogs.
examplePt: Eu tenho três cachorros.
tip: It has been our loyal companion for 15,000 years. A single sniff tells it more about you than any ID card.

example: The cat is sleeping.
examplePt: O gato está dormindo.
tip: Ancient Egyptians once worshipped it as divine. It can right itself in midair and always lands the same way.

example: The bird is singing.
examplePt: O pássaro está cantando.
tip: Most creatures in its class rule the skies, though two famous ones — the penguin and ostrich — never leave the ground.

example: The fish is in the water.
examplePt: O peixe está na água.
tip: It lives its entire life breathing something other creatures drown in. Its plural is identical to its singular.

example: The horse is running.
examplePt: O cavalo está correndo.
tip: Before engines existed, its name became the unit used to measure how powerful they were.

example: The cow gives milk.
examplePt: A vaca dá leite.
tip: Its stomach has four chambers and it chews for up to eight hours a day. Entire civilizations built their wealth around it.

example: The pig is pink.
examplePt: O porco é rosa.
tip: Contrary to its reputation, it is one of the cleanest farm animals. Rolling in mud is simply how it regulates its temperature.

example: I like fried chicken.
examplePt: Eu gosto de frango frito.
tip: It crossed the road long before anyone asked why. Both its egg form and its adult form star in famous English phrases.

example: The duck is in the lake.
examplePt: O pato está no lago.
tip: Its feathers shed water as if waxed. The phrase 'like water off a ___'s back' means criticism that simply doesn't stick.

example: The rabbit is fast.
examplePt: O coelho é rápido.
tip: It appears in magicians' hats and Easter traditions. In fiction, it once led a girl to a fantastical underground world.

example: The lion is strong.
examplePt: O leão é forte.
tip: Despite being called royalty of the wild, it actually avoids jungles. It prefers open savanna — and the females do most of the hunting.

example: The elephant is big.
examplePt: O elefante é grande.
tip: The largest land creature on Earth. It is the only animal known to mourn its dead, standing silently over their remains.

example: The monkey likes bananas.
examplePt: O macaco gosta de bananas.
tip: Darwin's most famous relative. It can peel its favourite food from the bottom end — the side that avoids the stringy bits.

example: The bear is big and strong.
examplePt: O urso é grande e forte.
tip: It sleeps for months without eating, yet wakes up fine. Children keep a stuffed version named after an American president.

example: The snake is long.
examplePt: A cobra é comprida.
tip: It has no eyelids and cannot blink. In the Garden of Eden story, it changed everything with one fateful conversation.

example: The frog jumps high.
examplePt: O sapo pula alto.
tip: It spends its early life breathing underwater as a completely different creature. Its skin is a living barometer of environmental health.

example: The butterfly is beautiful.
examplePt: A borboleta é bonita.
tip: Inside its cocoon, it completely dissolves into liquid before rebuilding itself into something entirely different. A miracle of biological reinvention.

example: The turtle is slow.
examplePt: A tartaruga é lenta.
tip: It carries its home everywhere — and its skeleton is fused to that home. Some of its kind outlive their human caretakers by a century.

example: The spider built a web.
examplePt: A aranha construiu uma teia.
tip: An eight-legged creature that spins silk webs to catch insects. It’s an arachnid, not an insect!

example: A bat flies at night.
examplePt: Um morcego voa à noite.
tip: The only mammal that truly flies! It sleeps upside-down during the day and uses sound to 'see' in the dark.

example: An owl watches from the tree.
examplePt: Uma coruja observa da árvore.
tip: A bird that hunts at night with huge eyes to see in the dark. It makes a 'hoot' sound and can turn its head almost all the way around!

example: The bee makes honey.
examplePt: A abelha faz mel.
tip: A flying insect that makes honey and pollinates flowers. It lives in a hive with thousands of other bees. Its sting hurts!

example: An ant works hard.
examplePt: Uma formiga trabalha duro.
tip: It has no lungs and breathes through tiny holes in its body. A single colony can move tonnes of soil to build a hidden city beneath your feet.

example: The chameleon changes color.
examplePt: O camaleão muda de cor.
tip: A lizard famous for changing its skin color to hide or communicate. It also has eyes that move independently of each other!

example: I eat rice every day.
examplePt: Eu como arroz todo dia.
tip: A small white grain. The staple food of more than half the world's population.

example: I want bread with butter.
examplePt: Eu quero pão com manteiga.
tip: A baked food made from flour. Toast is a browned, crunchy version of it.

example: I eat eggs for breakfast.
examplePt: Eu como ovos no café da manhã.
tip: Comes from a bird. Can be fried, boiled, scrambled, or poached for breakfast.

example: Do you like meat?
examplePt: Você gosta de carne?
tip: Sounds identical to 'meet' (to encounter someone). Be careful in writing!

example: I love pizza!
examplePt: Eu amo pizza!
tip: Spelled the same as in Portuguese! Originated in Italy. Round with toppings.

example: An apple a day keeps the doctor away.
examplePt: Uma maçã por dia mantém o médico longe.
tip: A round fruit that can be red or green. Has seeds inside. Grows on trees.

example: Monkeys like bananas.
examplePt: Macacos gostam de bananas.
tip: Spelled the same as in Portuguese! A yellow curved fruit. Monkeys love them.

example: I like cheese on my sandwich.
examplePt: Eu gosto de queijo no meu sanduíche.
tip: Made from milk. Photographers say 'Say ___!' to make people smile.

example: The cake is delicious.
examplePt: O bolo é delicioso.
tip: A sweet baked dessert. Served with candles on it at birthday parties.

example: Kids love candy.
examplePt: Crianças amam doces.
tip: A small, sweet treat. Children collect it going door-to-door on Halloween.

example: Eat more fruit.
examplePt: Coma mais frutas.
tip: A natural sweet food that grows on trees or plants. Usually contains seeds.

example: I want a salad, please.
examplePt: Eu quero uma salada, por favor.
tip: A cold dish made with raw vegetables. Often served with dressing on top.

example: The soup is hot.
examplePt: A sopa está quente.
tip: A warm liquid food cooked in a pot. Often eaten when sick or cold outside.

example: I made a sandwich.
examplePt: Eu fiz um sanduíche.
tip: Two slices of bread with a filling between them. Named after an English earl.

example: I want chocolate ice cream.
examplePt: Eu quero sorvete de chocolate.
tip: A frozen sweet treat. Made with milk and sugar. Melts fast in hot weather.

example: I need water.
examplePt: Eu preciso de água.
tip: The most essential drink. Covers 71% of the Earth's surface.

example: I drink milk every morning.
examplePt: Eu bebo leite toda manhã.
tip: A white drink produced by mammals. Used to make cheese, butter, and yogurt.

example: I want coffee, please.
examplePt: Eu quero café, por favor.
tip: A hot drink made from roasted beans. Contains caffeine. Very popular worldwide.

example: Do you want tea?
examplePt: Você quer chá?
tip: A hot drink made by soaking leaves in hot water. Very popular in England.

example: Orange juice is my favorite.
examplePt: Suco de laranja é meu favorito.
tip: A drink made by squeezing fruit. Orange ___ is the most popular kind.

example: I don't drink soda.
examplePt: Eu não bebo refrigerante.
tip: A sweet, fizzy drink. Also called 'pop' in parts of the USA.

example: My mother is beautiful.
examplePt: Minha mãe é bonita.
tip: The informal version is 'mom'. The woman who raised you.

example: My father works a lot.
examplePt: Meu pai trabalha muito.
tip: The informal version is 'dad'. The male parent in your family.

example: I have one brother.
examplePt: Eu tenho um irmão.
tip: A male sibling. Someone who grew up in the same house with the same parents.

example: My sister is ten years old.
examplePt: Minha irmã tem dez anos.
tip: A female sibling. Someone who grew up in the same house with the same parents.

example: He is my son.
examplePt: Ele é meu filho.
tip: Sounds exactly like 'sun' (the star in the sky). Your male child.

example: She is my daughter.
examplePt: Ela é minha filha.
tip: The 'gh' is completely silent. Your female child.

example: The baby is sleeping.
examplePt: O bebê está dormindo.
tip: A very young child who cannot walk or talk yet. Cries a lot and needs milk.

example: I love my family.
examplePt: Eu amo minha família.
tip: A group of people related by blood or marriage. Your closest circle.

example: My grandmother makes great cake.
examplePt: Minha avó faz ótimo bolo.
tip: Informal: 'grandma'. Your mother's or father's mother.

example: My grandfather is 80 years old.
examplePt: Meu avô tem 80 anos.
tip: Informal: 'grandpa'. Your mother's or father's father.

example: She loves her husband.
examplePt: Ela ama seu marido.
tip: The male partner in a marriage. The opposite of 'wife'.

example: He loves his wife.
examplePt: Ele ama sua esposa.
tip: The female partner in a marriage. The opposite of 'husband'.

example: My uncle lives in São Paulo.
examplePt: Meu tio mora em São Paulo.
tip: Your parent's brother, or your aunt's husband.

example: My aunt is a teacher.
examplePt: Minha tia é professora.
tip: Your parent's sister, or your uncle's wife. Sometimes spelled 'auntie' informally.

example: My cousin is my best friend.
examplePt: Meu(minha) primo(a) é meu(minha) melhor amigo(a).
tip: The child of your uncle or aunt. Not a sibling, but still family!

example: I live in a big house.
examplePt: Eu moro em uma casa grande.
tip: A building where people live. Different from 'home', which is more emotional.

example: Please close the door.
examplePt: Por favor, feche a porta.
tip: Everyone passes through it, yet few think about it. In English, one word tells you whether to push or pull — but often the sign is missing.

example: Open the window.
examplePt: Abra a janela.
tip: It lets in the world without letting in the weather. One tech company named its most-used operating system after it.

example: I cook in the kitchen.
examplePt: Eu cozinho na cozinha.
tip: The room where raw things become meals. Its name comes from the Latin word for 'to cook'.

example: My bedroom is clean.
examplePt: Meu quarto está limpo.
tip: Made of two words: 'bed' + 'room'. The room where you sleep.

example: Where is the bathroom?
examplePt: Onde fica o banheiro?
tip: Has a shower, sink, and toilet. In public places it is called 'restroom'.

example: The book is on the table.
examplePt: O livro está na mesa.
tip: A flat piece of furniture with legs. Used for eating, working, or studying.

example: Please sit on the chair.
examplePt: Por favor, sente na cadeira.
tip: It has four legs but cannot walk. It holds humans upright, yet is always empty when doing so feels most comfortable.

example: I go to bed at ten.
examplePt: Eu vou para a cama às dez.
tip: You spend about a third of your entire life in one. Its name spells the same shape as the letter that looks like it.

example: I sit on the sofa.
examplePt: Eu sento no sofá.
tip: A large, comfortable seat for two or more people. Also called 'couch'.

example: I watch TV at night.
examplePt: Eu assisto TV à noite.
tip: Short for 'television'. The screen in the living room that shows movies and shows.

example: Look at the clock.
examplePt: Olhe o relógio.
tip: A device that shows the time. Hangs on the wall. A 'watch' is worn on the wrist.

example: Where is my key?
examplePt: Onde está minha chave?
tip: It has teeth but cannot bite. The right one opens everything; the wrong one opens nothing. Music has them too.

example: Turn on the lamp.
examplePt: Ligue a lâmpada.
tip: A portable light source. In the story of Aladdin, a magic one had a genie inside.

example: I have a beautiful garden.
examplePt: Eu tenho um jardim bonito.
tip: An outdoor area with plants, flowers, and grass. Common behind houses.

example: Rain falls on the roof.
examplePt: A chuva cai no telhado.
tip: It is the first thing a storm hits and the last thing people repair. Raising one is an ancient celebration of a new building.

example: Hang a picture on the wall.
examplePt: Pendure um quadro na parede.
tip: It divides a space without moving. History's most famous one in Berlin fell in 1989. Another in China was said to be visible from space.

example: Walk up the staircase.
examplePt: Suba pela escadaria.
tip: It connects two worlds separated by height. Escalators replaced many of them, but they're still the only option when the power goes out.

example: Strike with a hammer.
examplePt: Bata com um martelo.
tip: It has one job. One proverb says: 'To someone who only has one of these, every problem looks like a nail.'

example: Cut with a knife.
examplePt: Corte com uma faca.
tip: The sharpest tool in the kitchen drawer. It is used in the name of a famous fictional villain — Jack the Ripper's preferred instrument.

example: Sew with a needle.
examplePt: Costure com uma agulha.
tip: It is the thinnest object with an eye. Finding one in a haystack is the English way of saying something is nearly impossible to find.

example: Trim with scissors.
examplePt: Apare com uma tesoura.
tip: Always plural — you can never have just one. It wins one round in a classic three-way hand game, but loses to the other two.

example: Climb the ladder.
examplePt: Suba a escada de mão.
tip: Climb it and you go up in the world — or so the saying goes. In a classic board game, a snake always sends you back down.

example: Eat with a spoon.
examplePt: Coma com uma colher.
tip: 'There is no ___,' says the Oracle in The Matrix. Mary Poppins insisted a spoonful of sugar helps the medicine go down.

example: Secure the lock.
examplePt: Tranque o cadeado.
tip: It keeps secrets without knowing any. Its counterpart — the object that opens it — rhymes with the sound of a clock ticking.

example: Draw with a drawing compass.
examplePt: Desenhe com um compasso.
tip: A technical drawing instrument consisting of two articulated legs, used for inscribing precise circles or measuring spatial distances on a two-dimensional surface.

example: Kick the ball.
examplePt: Chute a bola.
tip: Round, bouncy, and present in almost every sport. Its shape is mathematically perfect — every point on its surface is exactly equidistant from the center.

example: Play chess.
examplePt: Jogue xadrez.
tip: Two players, 64 squares, 32 pieces — and more possible games than atoms in the observable universe. The queen is its most powerful piece.

example: Score a goal.
examplePt: Marque um gol.
tip: It is the difference between cheering and silence. In sports it means a point scored — in life, it means what you are working toward.

example: Roll the dice.
examplePt: Jogue os dados.
tip: Shake, roll, and fate decides. Julius Caesar said 'the ___ is cast' before crossing the Rubicon, committing to a decision with no return.

example: Blow the whistle.
examplePt: Apite o apito.
tip: A referee's best friend and a dog's worst enemy. You can make one with just your lips — no tool required.

example: The true champion.
examplePt: O verdadeiro campeão.
tip: There is only one per competition. Queen wrote a famous song with this word as its central lyric: 'We are the ___s!'

example: Go for a running session.
examplePt: Vá para uma sessão de corrida.
tip: The oldest sport in history. Your body was literally shaped by evolution to do this for hours — an ability most animals cannot match.

example: Enjoy swimming.
examplePt: Aproveite a natação.
tip: Michael Phelps earned more Olympic gold medals in this sport than any athlete in any sport in history.

example: Work as a team.
examplePt: Trabalhe como uma equipe.
tip: There is no 'I' in this word — and coaches love to point that out. Two or more people working toward the same goal.

example: Draw a red card.
examplePt: Tire um cartão vermelho.
tip: In soccer, a red one ends your game. In poker, five good ones can win you everything. It fits perfectly in a wallet.

example: Catch the thief.
examplePt: Pegue o ladrão.
tip: Takes without asking. Robin Hood was a famous one — though he stole from the rich to give to the poor.

example: Lethal poison.
examplePt: Veneno letal.
tip: Tiny amounts can kill; even tinier ones can cure — some medicines are this in controlled doses. Cleopatra is said to have ended her life with its help.

example: Conceal a weapon.
examplePt: Esconder uma arma.
tip: The second most important invention in human conflict, right after the idea of having a conflict at all.

example: Locked in prison.
examplePt: Trancado na prisão.
tip: Four walls, a locked door, and time. Nelson Mandela spent 27 years in one before becoming president of South Africa.

example: Find the missing clue.
examplePt: Encontre a pista que falta.
tip: The key to every mystery. A famous board game about a fictional murder — Colonel Mustard in the library? — shares its name with this word.

example: Verify his alibi.
examplePt: Verifique o álibi dele.
tip: A Latin word meaning 'elsewhere'. In crime fiction, it is the first thing a suspect needs to establish to prove innocence.

example: Scan the fingerprint.
examplePt: Escaneie a impressão digital.
tip: No two humans share the same one — not even identical twins. It became the foundation of modern criminal investigation in the 1890s.

example: Investigate a murder.
examplePt: Investigue um assassinato.
tip: The most serious crime in the law books. Interestingly, a group of crows is also called this — for unknown reasons.

example: Question the witness.
examplePt: Interrogue a testemunha.
tip: The courtroom's most important voice. 'Eyewitness' is the compound form — it means you saw the event with your own eyes.

example: Set up a trap.
examplePt: Arme uma armadilha.
tip: It only works when the target doesn't see it coming. The cartoon version always uses cheese as bait — real ones are far more varied.

example: Fresh paint dries.
examplePt: Tinta fresca seca.
tip: Before cameras existed, it was the only way to preserve a face forever. Michelangelo spent four years lying on his back applying it to a ceiling.

example: Go to the theater.
examplePt: Vá ao teatro.
tip: The oldest form of public storytelling. In London's Globe, audiences once stood in the rain to watch Shakespeare — and loved it.

example: Write a poem.
examplePt: Escreva um poema.
tip: Words arranged to be felt, not just read. Some rhyme; others don't — but all choose each word with unusual care.

example: Turn on radio.
examplePt: Ligue o rádio.
tip: For decades, it was the internet — news, music, and stories beamed invisibly into homes. No screen required.

example: Carve a sculpture.
examplePt: Esculpa uma escultura.
tip: Michelangelo said he just removed everything that wasn't David. It is art you can walk around.

example: Enjoy the dance.
examplePt: Aproveite a dança.
tip: The only art form where your body is both the brush and the canvas. Every culture on Earth has developed its own version.

example: Mail a letter.
examplePt: Envie uma carta.
tip: It can mean a single character in an alphabet or an entire written message. One changes a word; the other can change a life.

example: I go to school every day.
examplePt: Eu vou à escola todo dia.
tip: You spend roughly 15,000 hours of your childhood in one. The word comes from the Greek for 'leisure' — which seems ironic.

example: My teacher is nice.
examplePt: Meu(minha) professor(a) é legal.
tip: The person who explains lessons and evaluates students in a classroom.

example: I am a student.
examplePt: Eu sou um(a) estudante.
tip: A person who studies. If you are using this app, that is you!

example: I read a book every week.
examplePt: Eu leio um livro toda semana.
tip: Seneca said 'show me your ___shelf and I'll tell you who you are.' Thousands of years later, still true.

example: Give me a pen, please.
examplePt: Me dê uma caneta, por favor.
tip: Mightier than the sword, according to one famous saying. The word also refers to a small enclosure for animals.

example: I need a pencil.
examplePt: Eu preciso de um lápis.
tip: A writing tool with a gray graphite core. Can be erased with a rubber.

example: Write on the paper.
examplePt: Escreva no papel.
tip: It starts as a tree. China invented it. Without it, there would be no money, no books, and no office jobs.

example: Open your notebook.
examplePt: Abra seu caderno.
tip: Made of two words: 'note' + 'book'. Many blank pages for writing notes.

example: The classroom is big.
examplePt: A sala de aula é grande.
tip: Made of two words: 'class' + 'room'. Where lessons take place at school.

example: I need to do my homework.
examplePt: Eu preciso fazer minha lição de casa.
tip: Made of two words: 'home' + 'work'. School tasks done outside of class.

example: I have a test tomorrow.
examplePt: Eu tenho uma prova amanhã.
tip: An evaluation that measures how much you know. Can make students nervous!

example: I use the computer.
examplePt: Eu uso o computador.
tip: An electronic machine that processes information. A 'laptop' is the portable version.

example: I work from Monday to Friday.
examplePt: Eu trabalho de segunda a sexta.
tip: Can be a noun ('I have work to do') or a verb ('I work every day'). Very flexible!

example: I go to the office every day.
examplePt: Eu vou ao escritório todo dia.
tip: A room or building where professional work happens. Has desks and computers.

example: My boss is friendly.
examplePt: Meu chefe é amigável.
tip: The person in charge at work. Everyone reports to this person.

example: I have a good job.
examplePt: Eu tenho um bom emprego.
tip: A paid occupation. 'What is your ___?' is a common question when meeting someone.

example: I need to save money.
examplePt: Eu preciso economizar dinheiro.
tip: It makes the world go round — or so the song says. It holds no value on its own; only collective human agreement gives it power.

example: I have a meeting at two.
examplePt: Eu tenho uma reunião às duas.
tip: A gathering where people discuss topics together. Very common in offices.

example: Where is my phone?
examplePt: Onde está meu celular?
tip: A device for communication. A 'smartphone' is the modern pocket version.

example: I will send you an email.

example: It's cold, wear a jacket.

example: I need clean socks.
examplePt: Eu preciso de meias limpas.
tip: Soft fabric worn on feet inside shoes. Always sold in pairs.

examplePt: Ela usa um anel de prata.

examplePt: Coloque uma máscara facial.

examplePt: Aperte seu cinto de couro.

examplePt: Olhe no espelho.

examplePt: Use luvas quentes.

tip: The top part of the body where the brain, face, and hair are located.

examplePt: Ela tem olhos azuis.

examplePt: Lave suas mãos.

examplePt: Ela tem cabelo longo.

examplePt: Eu amo a praia.

examplePt: Ela vai à igreja no domingo.

examplePt: Eu vou ao banco.
tip: A financial institution where people save and withdraw money.

examplePt: A rua está movimentada.
tip: A public road in a city with buildings on both sides. Has sidewalks for walking.

examplePt: Eu moro em uma cidade grande.

examplePt: O Brasil é um país grande.
tip: Can mean a nation OR a rural area ('the countryside'). The context decides which!

examplePt: Cruze a ponte de pedra.
tip: A structural span engineered to provide continuous passage over a physical obstacle, such as a chasm, watercourse, or thoroughfare.

example: I go by car.
examplePt: Eu vou de carro.

examplePt: Eu pego ônibus para a escola.
tip: A large vehicle that carries many passengers along a fixed route. Public transport.

examplePt: Eu ando de bicicleta.
tip: A two-wheeled vehicle powered by pedaling. The informal version is 'bike'.

examplePt: O trem é rápido.
tip: A series of connected cars that travel on metal rails. Faster than buses.

example: I fly by airplane.
examplePt: Eu viajo de avião.
tip: Made of 'air' + 'plane'. A winged machine that flies through the sky.

example: The boat is on the water.
examplePt: O barco está na água.
tip: A watercraft used on rivers and lakes. Smaller than a 'ship'.

example: Let's take a taxi.
examplePt: Vamos pegar um táxi.
tip: A car driven by a professional that takes you places for a fee.

example: I am happy.
examplePt: Eu estou feliz.
tip: The most important verb in English. Its forms are: am, is, are, was, were.

example: I have a dog.
examplePt: Eu tenho um cachorro.
tip: Expresses possession. Also used in perfect tenses: 'I have finished'.

example: I go to school.
examplePt: Eu vou à escola.
tip: An irregular verb. Its past tense is 'went', which looks completely different!

example: I eat breakfast at seven.
examplePt: Eu como café da manhã às sete.
tip: The action of consuming food. Its past tense is 'ate'.

example: I drink water.
examplePt: Eu bebo água.
tip: To consume a liquid. Its past tense is 'drank'.

example: I sleep eight hours.
examplePt: Eu durmo oito horas.
tip: To rest with your eyes closed. Its past tense is 'slept'.

example: I read books.
examplePt: Eu leio livros.
tip: Tricky! Present and past are spelled the same ('read'), but they sound different: 'reed' vs 'red'.

examplePt: Eu escrevo no meu caderno.
tip: The 'w' is completely silent! Its past tense is 'wrote'.

example: I speak Portuguese.
examplePt: Eu falo português.
tip: To use your voice to communicate. Its past tense is 'spoke'.

example: Listen to the music.
examplePt: Escute a música.
tip: Active attention to a sound. Unlike 'to hear', which happens without effort.

examplePt: Eu vejo as estrelas.
tip: Passive visual perception. 'To look' means you are actively choosing to direct your eyes.

examplePt: Eu gosto de pizza.
tip: To find something pleasant. Weaker than 'to love'. Also used on social media buttons!

examplePt: Eu amo minha família.
tip: A complex neurobiological and psychological state characterized by intense oxytocin release, deep attachment, and altruistic behavioral tendencies toward another entity.

example: I want coffee.
examplePt: Eu quero café.
tip: To desire something. Different from 'to need' — wanting is a wish, needing is essential.

examplePt: Eu preciso de ajuda.

example: I know the answer.
examplePt: Eu sei a resposta.
tip: The 'k' is completely silent! To have knowledge about something.

example: I make breakfast.
examplePt: Eu faço o café da manhã.
tip: To create or produce something. Its past tense is 'made'.

example: Come here, please.
examplePt: Venha aqui, por favor.
tip: The opposite of 'to go'. Moving toward the speaker. Its past tense is 'came'.

example: I play soccer.
examplePt: Eu jogo futebol.
tip: Has three meanings: to play a sport, a game, OR a musical instrument. Context is key!

example: I run every morning.
examplePt: Eu corro toda manhã.
tip: To move fast on foot. Its past tense is 'ran'. Also means to operate something.

example: I walk to school.
examplePt: Eu ando até a escola.
tip: The 'l' is completely silent! To move at a normal pace on foot. Slower than 'to run'.

example: Open the door.
examplePt: Abra a porta.
tip: The opposite of 'to close'. To make something accessible.

example: Close the window.
examplePt: Feche a janela.
tip: The opposite of 'to open'. To shut something.

example: I want to buy a book.
examplePt: Eu quero comprar um livro.
tip: To get something by paying money. Its past tense is 'bought'.

example: Can you help me?
examplePt: Você pode me ajudar?
tip: To assist someone in need. 'Can you ___ me?' is a very common request.

examplePt: Eu estudo inglês todo dia.
tip: To learn by reading and practicing. That is exactly what you are doing right now!

examplePt: Eu cozinho o jantar.
tip: To prepare food using heat. A 'cook' is also a noun for a person who does this.

examplePt: Me dê o livro.
tip: To hand something to another person. Its past tense is 'gave'.

examplePt: Leve seu guarda-chuva.

examplePt: Eu tive um sonho.
tip: A endogenous hallucinatory state occurring during specific neural cycles, creating a temporary, immersive reality that collapses upon waking.

example: Chaos reigns.
examplePt: O caos reina.
tip: A state of utter confusion or randomness, though in physics it describes systems highly sensitive to initial conditions, making long-term prediction impossible.

example: A space vacuum.
examplePt: Um vácuo do espaço.
tip: A volume of space that is entirely devoid of matter, where the gaseous pressure is significantly lower than atmospheric pressure.

example: Evolution of life.
examplePt: Evolução da vida.
tip: The gradual, non-teleological process of change in the heritable characteristics of biological populations over successive generations.

example: Speak a new language.
examplePt: Fale um novo idioma.
tip: An institutionalized, highly structured system of arbitrary vocal signs or graphic symbols used by human cohorts to transmit abstract thoughts.

example: Water reflection.
examplePt: Reflexão da água.
tip: The abrupt change in direction of a wavefront at an interface between two different media, returning it to its original medium.

example: Into the void.
examplePt: Para dentro do vazio.
tip: A localized spatial region containing zero atoms or particles, maintaining an absolute pressure of zero pascals.

example: At the very end.
examplePt: Bem no final.
tip: The terminal threshold or final boundary condition where a continuous chronological sequence or structural process permanently ceases.

example: I am very happy today.
examplePt: Eu estou muito feliz hoje.
tip: Feeling joy and pleasure. The opposite is 'sad'. 'Happy birthday!' uses this word.

example: She is sad.
examplePt: Ela está triste.
tip: Feeling sorrow or unhappiness. The opposite is 'happy'. Crying is a sign of this.

example: He is angry.
examplePt: Ele está com raiva.
tip: An intense emotional response involving a strong uncomfortable and hostile response to a perceived provocation, hurt, or threat.

example: Overcome your fear.
examplePt: Supere seu medo.
tip: An evolutionary survival mechanism triggered by a perceived threat, causing an immediate amygdala response and a cascade of adrenaline for a fight-or-flight reaction.

example: Express your sadness.
examplePt: Expresse sua tristeza.
tip: An emotional pain associated with, or characterized by, feelings of disadvantage, loss, despair, grief, helplessness, and disappointment.

example: Avoid jealousy.
examplePt: Evite o ciúme.
tip: A complex negative emotion encompassing feelings ranging from suspicion to rage, triggered by the perceived threat of losing a valued relationship or status to a rival.

example: Feel pride in work.
examplePt: Sinta orgulho no trabalho.
tip: An inwardly directed emotion that carries an inflated appraisal of one's own country, group, achievements, or personal worth.

example: No shame in trying.
examplePt: Sem vergonha de tentar.
tip: A painful, socially self-conscious emotion that arises from the comparison of one's actions or state with social standards or internal ideals.

example: A fond memory.
examplePt: Uma memória querida.
tip: The cognitive faculty and neurobiological apparatus by which information, experiences, and learned behaviors are encoded, stored, and subsequently retrieved.

example: High intelligence.
examplePt: Alta inteligência.
tip: The abstract capacity to acquire, process, synthesize, and apply knowledge to solve novel problems and adapt to changing environments.

example: I am hungry.
examplePt: Eu estou com fome.
tip: The feeling when your body needs food. Your stomach may make noise when you feel this.

example: Satisfy your hunger.
examplePt: Satisfaça sua fome.
tip: A physiological sensation signaling a critical depletion of caloric reserves, mediated by the hormone ghrelin acting upon the hypothalamus.

example: I am thirsty.
examplePt: Eu estou com sede.
tip: The urge to drink liquid. Your throat and mouth feel dry when you feel this.

example: I am scared of snakes.
examplePt: Eu tenho medo de cobras.
tip: Feeling fear. Something frightening caused this feeling. Haunted houses make people feel this.

example: I am sick today.
examplePt: Eu estou doente hoje.
tip: Not feeling well due to illness. 'Call in sick' means telling work you cannot come.

example: I am cold.
examplePt: Eu estou com frio.
tip: Feeling a low temperature. Can describe the weather or how your body feels.

example: It is very hot today.
examplePt: Está muito quente hoje.
tip: Feeling high temperature. The opposite of cold. Summer days can feel this way.

example: I am excited about the trip.
examplePt: Eu estou empolgado(a) com a viagem.
tip: Feeling great enthusiasm and eagerness. You feel this before something you have been looking forward to.

example: I am nervous about the test.
examplePt: Eu estou nervoso(a) com a prova.
tip: Feeling anxiety before something important. Your hands might shake and your heart beats faster.

example: I am surprised!
examplePt: Eu estou surpreso(a)!
tip: A sudden feeling caused by something unexpected. Birthday parties often cause this feeling!

example: I am bored.
examplePt: Eu estou entediado(a).
tip: Feeling weary with nothing interesting to do. Long waits or dull classes cause this.

example: I am proud of you.
examplePt: Eu estou orgulhoso(a) de você.
tip: Deep satisfaction from an achievement. Parents feel this when their child does something great.

example: What is your name?
examplePt: Qual é o seu nome?
tip: Asks about things or information. 'What is that?' is a very common question.

example: Where do you live?
examplePt: Onde você mora?
tip: Asks about location. 'Where are you from?' and 'Where is the bathroom?' are classics.

example: When is your birthday?
examplePt: Quando é seu aniversário?
tip: Asks about time or the moment an event happens.

example: Who is your teacher?
examplePt: Quem é seu(sua) professor(a)?
tip: Asks about a person's identity. 'Whodunit?' is a classic mystery question.

example: Why are you sad?
examplePt: Por que você está triste?
tip: Asks for a reason or cause. The answer almost always starts with 'because'.

example: How are you?
examplePt: Como você está?
tip: Asks about manner or condition. 'How are you?' is the most common greeting question.

example: How much is this?
examplePt: Quanto custa isso?
tip: Used for prices and uncountable things. 'How many?' is used for countable things.

example: How many brothers do you have?
examplePt: Quantos irmãos você tem?
tip: Used for things you can count individually. 'How much?' is for things you cannot count.

example: What time is it?
examplePt: Que horas são?
tip: Asks about the current hour or when something is scheduled to happen.

example: Do you like chocolate?
examplePt: Você gosta de chocolate?
tip: A yes/no question about preferences. 'Would you like?' is used when offering something.

example: Can you help me?
examplePt: Você pode me ajudar?
tip: Asks about ability or makes a polite request. 'Could you?' is more formal.

example: I don't know the answer.
examplePt: Eu não sei a resposta.
tip: 'Don't' is a contraction of 'do not'. An honest response when you lack information.

example: I don't understand this word.
examplePt: Eu não entendo esta palavra.
tip: A key phrase for language learners! Use it to ask for clarification politely.

example: Can you repeat, please?
examplePt: Pode repetir, por favor?
tip: A polite request to hear something again. Very useful in real conversations!

example: I'm learning English at home.
examplePt: Estou aprendendo inglês em casa.
tip: Uses the present continuous tense: 'I'm' + verb+ing. This is exactly what you are doing!

example: Hi! Nice to meet you.
examplePt: Oi! Prazer em conhecê-lo(a).
tip: Said when meeting someone for the first time. Reply with 'Nice to meet you too!'

example: Bye! See you later.
examplePt: Tchau! Até mais tarde.
tip: An informal goodbye. Implies you will see the person again soon. 'Later!' is even shorter.

example: Goodbye! Have a nice day!
examplePt: Tchau! Tenha um bom dia!
tip: A friendly farewell wish. Cashiers and service workers say it all the time.

example: It's late, I'm going home.
examplePt: Está tarde, estou indo para casa.
tip: Uses present continuous (I'm + going) to describe an action happening right now.

example: Hey! What are you doing?
examplePt: Ei! O que você está fazendo?
tip: A present continuous question. Uses 'are + you + verb+ing'. Very natural in everyday speech.

example: This is good, I like it.
examplePt: Isso é bom, eu gosto disso.
tip: 'It' replaces the object already mentioned. A natural way to express approval.

example: Let's go to the park!
examplePt: Vamos ao parque!
tip: Short for 'let us go'. Suggests doing something together. A great motivational phrase!

example: I'm sorry for being late.
examplePt: Me desculpe por estar atrasado(a).
tip: More sincere than just 'sorry'. The full phrase shows deeper regret.

example: Excuse me, where is the bathroom?
examplePt: Com licença, onde fica o banheiro?
tip: Used to politely get attention or pass by someone in a crowd.

example: Can you help me? Of course!
examplePt: Pode me ajudar? Claro!
tip: A confident, positive response. Stronger than simply saying 'yes'.

example: Is it going to rain? I think so.
examplePt: Vai chover? Eu acho que sim.
tip: Expresses uncertainty. Means you believe something but are not 100% sure.

example: Wait a moment, please.
examplePt: Espere um momento, por favor.
tip: Asking someone to pause briefly. 'Hold on' is a common informal alternative.

example: You passed the test? That's great!
examplePt: Você passou na prova? Que ótimo!
tip: An enthusiastic response to good news. 'That's' is a contraction of 'that is'.

example: Thank you! No problem!
examplePt: Obrigado(a)! Sem problema!
tip: A casual reply to 'thank you' or 'sorry'. Shows no inconvenience was caused.

example: I need help with my homework.
examplePt: Eu preciso de ajuda com minha lição.
tip: Uses 'need' + noun. A direct and polite way to ask for assistance.

example: It's late, it's time to go.
examplePt: Está tarde, é hora de ir.
tip: 'It's time to' + verb. Signals that you need to leave or start something.

example: Don't worry, take it easy.
examplePt: Não se preocupe, vai com calma.
tip: A friendly way to say relax or don't stress. Often used as a casual goodbye too.

example: Bye! See you tomorrow.
examplePt: Tchau! Até amanhã.
tip: A specific farewell for when you know exactly when you'll meet again.

example: See you soon, take care!
examplePt: Até logo, se cuida!
tip: Used when you're not sure exactly when, but you expect to meet again soon.

example: Hey! What's up?
examplePt: Ei! E aí?
tip: A very casual greeting between friends, not a real question about the sky!

example: Goodbye, take care!
examplePt: Tchau, se cuida!
tip: A warm way to say goodbye, showing you care about the other person.

example: Good luck on your test!
examplePt: Boa sorte na sua prova!
tip: Said before something important happens, like a test or a big decision.

example: Congratulations on your new job!
examplePt: Parabéns pelo seu novo emprego!
tip: Said to celebrate someone's achievement. Often shortened to 'Congrats!'

example: I am eleven years old.
examplePt: Eu tenho onze anos.
tip: The first 'teen'-range number that doesn't actually end in '-teen'.

example: There are twelve months in a year.
examplePt: Há doze meses em um ano.
tip: A dozen eggs means twelve eggs!

example: She is twenty years old.
examplePt: Ela tem vinte anos.
tip: The first number formed by combining a 'ty' ending with a digit.

example: The bus arrives in thirty minutes.
examplePt: O ônibus chega em trinta minutos.
tip: Half an hour has this many minutes.

example: He has fifty dollars.
examplePt: Ele tem cinquenta dólares.
tip: Halfway to one hundred.

example: I have one hundred stars.
examplePt: Eu tenho cem estrelas.
tip: Always follows 'a' or 'one': 'a hundred', not just 'hundred'.

example: The city has a thousand shops.
examplePt: A cidade tem mil lojas.
tip: One thousand is written as 1,000 in English, with a comma, not a period.

example: She has a silver necklace.
examplePt: Ela tem um colar prateado.
tip: The color of the metal used in coins and jewelry.

example: The walls are cream.
examplePt: As paredes são cor de creme.
tip: A soft, warm shade of white, like the color of fresh cream.

example: He wears a beige coat.
examplePt: Ele usa um casaco bege.
tip: A pale sandy-brown color, popular for walls and furniture.

example: The sea looks turquoise here.
examplePt: O mar parece turquesa aqui.
tip: Named after the blue-green gemstone. A mix of blue and green.

example: The flower is violet.
examplePt: A flor é violeta.
tip: A deep purple, like the color of the violet flower.

example: I painted my room light blue.
examplePt: Eu pintei meu quarto de azul claro.
tip: Two words. Add 'light' or 'dark' before any color to describe its shade.

example: The tiger has orange stripes.
examplePt: O tigre tem listras laranjas.
tip: The largest wild cat in the world, known for its striped coat.

example: The wolf howls at night.
examplePt: O lobo uiva à noite.
tip: A wild relative of the dog that lives and hunts in packs.

example: The fox is clever.
examplePt: A raposa é esperta.
tip: Known in stories worldwide for being clever and sneaky.

example: The deer ran into the forest.
examplePt: O cervo correu para a floresta.
tip: Plural is also 'deer' — no extra 's' needed!

example: The sheep gives us wool.
examplePt: A ovelha nos dá lã.
tip: Singular and plural are the same word: one sheep, two sheep.

example: The goat eats grass.
examplePt: A cabra come grama.
tip: A farm animal known for eating almost anything and climbing well.

example: The mouse is very small.
examplePt: O rato é muito pequeno.
tip: Plural is 'mice', not 'mouses' — an irregular plural!

example: The shark swims in the ocean.
examplePt: O tubarão nada no oceano.
tip: A powerful ocean predator with rows of sharp teeth.

example: I put butter on my bread.
examplePt: Eu passo manteiga no meu pão.
tip: Made from cream. Spread it on toast for breakfast.

example: She baked a chocolate cookie.
examplePt: Ela assou um biscoito de chocolate.
tip: In British English, a similar sweet snack is often called a 'biscuit'.

example: I love chocolate cake.
examplePt: Eu amo bolo de chocolate.
tip: Made from cacao beans. One of the most popular flavors in the world.

example: Carrots are a healthy vegetable.
examplePt: Cenouras são um legume saudável.
tip: A general word for edible plants like carrots, potatoes, and lettuce.

example: I like fried potatoes.
examplePt: Eu gosto de batatas fritas.
tip: Plural is 'potatoes', with an 'es' — an exception to the usual rule.

example: The tomato is red.
examplePt: O tomate é vermelho.
tip: Botanically a fruit, but used as a vegetable in cooking.

example: This soup has onion in it.
examplePt: Essa sopa tem cebola nela.
tip: Cutting one often makes people cry because of the gases it releases.

example: Garlic gives great flavor to food.
examplePt: O alho dá um ótimo sabor à comida.
tip: A strong-smelling ingredient used in cooking all over the world.

example: They drank wine at dinner.
examplePt: Eles beberam vinho no jantar.
tip: Made from fermented grapes. Comes in red, white, and rosé.

example: He ordered a cold beer.
examplePt: Ele pediu uma cerveja gelada.
tip: One of the oldest and most popular alcoholic drinks in the world.

example: We made lemonade in summer.
examplePt: Fizemos limonada no verão.
tip: A refreshing drink made from lemon juice, water, and sugar.

example: She drinks a banana smoothie.
examplePt: Ela toma uma vitamina de banana.
tip: A thick drink made by blending fruit, similar to a Brazilian 'vitamina'.

example: I drink hot chocolate in winter.
examplePt: Eu bebo chocolate quente no inverno.
tip: Two words. A warm, sweet drink perfect for cold days.

example: Coconut water is refreshing.
examplePt: Água de coco é refrescante.
tip: A natural drink that comes straight from a young coconut.

example: I visit my grandparents every week.
examplePt: Eu visito meus avós toda semana.
tip: A general word for grandmother and grandfather together.

example: My nephew is very funny.
examplePt: Meu sobrinho é muito engraçado.
tip: The son of your brother or sister.

example: My niece loves to sing.
examplePt: Minha sobrinha ama cantar.
tip: The daughter of your brother or sister.

example: My stepfather is very kind.
examplePt: Meu padrasto é muito gentil.
tip: 'Step-' before a family word means it's through marriage, not blood.

example: Her stepmother cooks well.
examplePt: A madrasta dela cozinha bem.
tip: Not always the villain from fairy tales — just a mother by marriage!

example: She has a twin sister.
examplePt: Ela tem uma irmã gêmea.
tip: Twins are born on the same day, from the same pregnancy.

example: All my relatives came to the party.
examplePt: Todos os meus parentes vieram à festa.
tip: A general word for anyone in your family, close or distant.

example: I like to sit on the balcony.
examplePt: Eu gosto de sentar na varanda.
tip: A small outdoor platform attached to an upper floor of a house.

example: The kids play in the backyard.
examplePt: As crianças brincam no quintal.
tip: One word. The outdoor area behind a house.

example: There is a fence around the garden.
examplePt: Há uma cerca ao redor do jardim.
tip: A structure that marks the border of a property.

example: The lamp hangs from the ceiling.
examplePt: A luminária pende do teto.
tip: The inside top surface of a room — don't confuse with 'roof', the outside!

example: The cat sleeps on the floor.
examplePt: O gato dorme no chão.
tip: Also means a level of a building, like 'first floor'.

example: I take a shower every morning.
examplePt: Eu tomo banho de chuveiro toda manhã.
tip: Also a word for light rain, like 'a shower of rain'.

example: Put the milk in the refrigerator.
examplePt: Coloque o leite na geladeira.
tip: Often shortened to 'fridge' in everyday conversation.

example: He used a wrench to fix the pipe.
examplePt: Ele usou uma chave inglesa para consertar o cano.
tip: In British English, this tool is usually called a 'spanner'.

example: I need a screwdriver to open this.
examplePt: Eu preciso de uma chave de fenda para abrir isso.
tip: Used to turn screws — literally 'a driver of screws'.

example: He cut the wood with a saw.
examplePt: Ele cortou a madeira com uma serra.
tip: Also the past tense of 'see' — context tells them apart!

example: She used a drill to make a hole.
examplePt: Ela usou uma furadeira para fazer um buraco.
tip: Also means practicing something repeatedly, like a 'fire drill'.

example: He swept the floor with a broom.
examplePt: Ele varreu o chão com uma vassoura.
tip: The tool witches are famously shown flying on!

example: Fill the bucket with water.
examplePt: Encha o balde com água.
tip: 'Bucket list' means a list of things to do before you die.

example: He hit the nail with a hammer.
examplePt: Ele bateu no prego com um martelo.
tip: This word also means the hard part at the tip of your finger!

example: I know all the words to this song.
examplePt: Eu sei todas as palavras dessa música.
tip: A piece of music with lyrics, meant to be sung.

example: We watched a movie last night.
examplePt: Nós assistimos a um filme ontem à noite.
tip: 'Film' is the more common word in British English.

example: She took a beautiful photograph.
examplePt: Ela tirou uma fotografia linda.
tip: Often shortened to 'photo' or 'pic' in everyday speech.

example: We visited an art museum.
examplePt: Nós visitamos um museu de arte.
tip: A building where historical or artistic objects are kept and shown.

example: He plays the guitar every day.
examplePt: Ele toca violão todos os dias.
tip: One of the most popular instruments in music around the world.

example: She learned to play the piano.
examplePt: Ela aprendeu a tocar piano.
tip: Short for 'pianoforte', meaning it can play both soft and loud.

example: The child made a drawing of a house.
examplePt: A criança fez um desenho de uma casa.
tip: Comes from the verb 'draw'. A picture made with pencil or pen.

example: I use a ruler to draw straight lines.
examplePt: Eu uso uma régua para desenhar linhas retas.
tip: Also means someone who governs a country — context makes the meaning clear.

example: Can I borrow your eraser?
examplePt: Posso pegar sua borracha emprestada?
tip: In British English, this is usually just called a 'rubber'.

example: She carries her books in a backpack.
examplePt: Ela carrega seus livros em uma mochila.
tip: One word. Worn on your back, hence the name.

example: The teacher writes on the blackboard.
examplePt: O professor escreve no quadro-negro.
tip: Modern classrooms often use a white 'whiteboard' instead.

example: I have a math exam tomorrow.
examplePt: Eu tenho uma prova de matemática amanhã.
tip: Short for 'examination'. Used the same way as 'test'.

example: She got a good grade on the test.
examplePt: Ela tirou uma boa nota na prova.
tip: Also means a school year level, like 'fifth grade'.

example: Today's lesson is about animals.
examplePt: A lição de hoje é sobre animais.
tip: Can mean a single class or something learned from experience.

example: She receives her salary every month.
examplePt: Ela recebe o salário dela todo mês.
tip: Comes from the Latin word for salt — Roman soldiers were once paid in it!

example: He has a job interview tomorrow.
examplePt: Ele tem uma entrevista de emprego amanhã.
tip: A formal meeting to evaluate someone for a job or for a news story.

example: Send your resume to apply for the job.
examplePt: Envie seu currículo para se candidatar à vaga.
tip: In British English, this is usually called a 'CV' (curriculum vitae).

example: My colleague helped me finish the project.
examplePt: Meu colega de trabalho me ajudou a terminar o projeto.
tip: Specifically means someone you work with, not just any friend.

example: The deadline for the project is Friday.
examplePt: O prazo do projeto é sexta-feira.
tip: Literally 'a line you cannot cross' — the final date for something.

example: We finished the project on time.
examplePt: Nós terminamos o projeto no prazo.
tip: Can be a noun (a project) or a verb (to project, meaning to plan or predict).

example: They signed the contract yesterday.
examplePt: Eles assinaram o contrato ontem.
tip: A formal, legal agreement between two or more people or companies.

example: She is wearing a blue skirt.
examplePt: Ela está usando uma saia azul.
tip: A piece of clothing worn from the waist down, without separate legs.

example: I wear a sweater when it's cold.
examplePt: Eu uso um suéter quando está frio.
tip: Called a 'jumper' in British English.

example: She wrapped a scarf around her neck.
examplePt: Ela enrolou um cachecol no pescoço.
tip: Plural can be 'scarfs' or 'scarves' — both are correct!

example: He wears a tie to work.
examplePt: Ele usa gravata para trabalhar.
tip: Also a verb meaning to fasten something, like 'tie your shoes'.

example: I need sunglasses; it's very sunny.
examplePt: Eu preciso de óculos de sol; está muito ensolarado.
tip: Always plural, like 'glasses' and 'pants' — you never say 'a sunglass'.

example: Put on your coat, it's cold outside.
examplePt: Coloque seu casaco, está frio lá fora.
tip: Usually heavier and longer than a jacket.

example: She wears boots in winter.
examplePt: Ela usa botas no inverno.
tip: Usually used in plural, since you wear two of them.

example: He carries his bag on one shoulder.
examplePt: Ele carrega a bolsa em um ombro.
tip: 'Cold shoulder' is an expression meaning to ignore someone.

example: She bent her elbow to wave.
examplePt: Ela dobrou o cotovelo para acenar.
tip: The joint that lets you bend your arm.

example: He hurt his knee playing soccer.
examplePt: Ele machucou o joelho jogando futebol.
tip: The 'k' is silent — it's pronounced just like 'nee'.

example: She wears a necklace on her neck.
examplePt: Ela usa um colar no pescoço.
tip: Connects your head to the rest of your body.

example: He touched his chin while thinking.
examplePt: Ele tocou o queixo enquanto pensava.
tip: The lowest part of your face, below your mouth.

example: She has a ring on her finger.
examplePt: Ela tem um anel no dedo.
tip: Used for the hand; the word for a foot digit is 'toe'.

example: The election happens every four years.
examplePt: A eleição acontece a cada quatro anos.
tip: When people vote to choose their leaders.

example: Everyone helps in this community.
examplePt: Todo mundo ajuda nessa comunidade.
tip: A group of people living in the same area or sharing something in common.

example: Brazil has a rich culture.
examplePt: O Brasil tem uma cultura rica.
tip: Includes a group's traditions, art, food, music, and beliefs.

example: This is an old family tradition.
examplePt: Essa é uma tradição de família antiga.
tip: A custom or belief passed down from one generation to the next.

example: People practice many religions around the world.
examplePt: As pessoas praticam muitas religiões ao redor do mundo.
tip: A system of faith and worship, often centered on beliefs about a higher power.

example: It's important to vote in elections.
examplePt: É importante votar nas eleições.
tip: Can be a verb (to vote) or a noun (a vote).

example: My neighbor is very friendly.
examplePt: Meu vizinho é muito simpático.
tip: Spelled 'neighbour' in British English, with a 'u'.

example: We need to negotiate the price.
examplePt: Precisamos negociar o preço.
tip: To discuss something to reach an agreement, usually about price or terms.

example: Please send the invoice by email.
examplePt: Por favor, envie a fatura por e-mail.
tip: A document that lists what was sold and how much is owed.

example: The client wants a discount.
examplePt: O cliente quer um desconto.
tip: Usually refers to someone who buys a service, while 'customer' buys a product.

example: We are over budget this month.
examplePt: Estamos acima do orçamento este mês.
tip: A plan for how much money you can spend.

example: The company's revenue grew this year.
examplePt: A receita da empresa cresceu este ano.
tip: The total money a business earns, before subtracting costs.

example: They made a big profit last quarter.
examplePt: Eles tiveram um grande lucro no último trimestre.
tip: What's left after you subtract costs from revenue.

example: The startup reported a loss this year.
examplePt: A startup registrou um prejuízo este ano.
tip: The opposite of profit — when costs are higher than revenue.

example: The two banks announced a merger.
examplePt: Os dois bancos anunciaram uma fusão.
tip: When two companies combine into one.

example: All stakeholders approved the plan.
examplePt: Todas as partes interessadas aprovaram o plano.
tip: Anyone affected by or interested in a business decision — employees, investors, customers.

example: Shareholders vote on major decisions.
examplePt: Os acionistas votam nas decisões importantes.
tip: Someone who owns shares (stock) in a company.

example: The supply chain was disrupted last year.
examplePt: A cadeia de suprimentos foi interrompida no ano passado.
tip: The whole process from raw materials to the finished product reaching the customer.

example: They formed a partnership with a local firm.
examplePt: Eles formaram uma parceria com uma empresa local.
tip: A formal relationship between two or more people or companies working together.

example: We sent our proposal to the client.
examplePt: Enviamos nossa proposta ao cliente.
tip: A formal suggestion or plan, often written, offered for consideration.

example: Let's follow the agenda for today's meeting.
examplePt: Vamos seguir a pauta da reunião de hoje.
tip: A list of topics to be discussed in a meeting.

example: She gave a great presentation.
examplePt: Ela fez uma ótima apresentação.
tip: A talk, often with slides, explaining an idea or project.

example: He is good at networking at events.
examplePt: Ele é bom em fazer networking em eventos.
tip: Building professional relationships that can help your career or business.

example: Our marketing strategy changed.
examplePt: Nossa estratégia de marketing mudou.
tip: A plan of action designed to achieve a long-term goal.

example: Our biggest competitor launched a new product.
examplePt: Nosso maior concorrente lançou um novo produto.
tip: A rival company or person competing for the same customers.

example: The company increased its market share.
examplePt: A empresa aumentou sua fatia de mercado.
tip: The percentage of total sales in an industry that one company controls.

example: This is a very famous brand.
examplePt: Esta é uma marca muito famosa.
tip: The name, image, and reputation that identify a company or product.

example: Their customer service is excellent.
examplePt: O atendimento ao cliente deles é excelente.
tip: The support a company gives before, during, and after a purchase.

example: I'd love to hear your feedback.
examplePt: Eu adoraria ouvir seu feedback.
tip: Information or opinions about how something is going, used to improve it.

example: They decided to outsource the design work.
examplePt: Eles decidiram terceirizar o trabalho de design.
tip: To hire an outside company to do work instead of doing it in-house.

example: The headquarters is located downtown.
examplePt: A sede fica no centro da cidade.
tip: The main office of a company, often abbreviated 'HQ'.

example: It's a subsidiary of a larger corporation.
examplePt: É uma subsidiária de uma corporação maior.
tip: A company that is owned or controlled by another, larger company.

example: The board of directors approved the budget.
examplePt: O conselho de administração aprovou o orçamento.
tip: The group of people elected to oversee a company's management.

example: She became CEO at 35.
examplePt: Ela se tornou CEO aos 35 anos.
tip: Short for 'Chief Executive Officer', the top boss of a company.

example: I work as a freelancer now.
examplePt: Eu trabalho como freelancer agora.
tip: Someone who works for different clients instead of one employer.

example: She's a successful entrepreneur.
examplePt: Ela é uma empreendedora de sucesso.
tip: A person who starts and runs their own business, taking financial risks.

example: He founded a tech startup.
examplePt: Ele fundou uma startup de tecnologia.
tip: A new company, usually small and aiming to grow quickly.

example: They found a new investor.
examplePt: Eles encontraram um novo investidor.
tip: A person or company that puts money into a business hoping to profit.

example: The startup raised venture capital.
examplePt: A startup captou capital de risco.
tip: Money invested in new, risky businesses that have high growth potential.

example: The company had a deficit this quarter.
examplePt: A empresa teve um déficit neste trimestre.
tip: When spending is greater than income.

example: The country reported a trade surplus.
examplePt: O país registrou um superávit comercial.
tip: When you have more than you need — the opposite of a deficit.

example: The doctor gave her a diagnosis.
examplePt: O médico deu um diagnóstico para ela.
tip: The identification of an illness based on its symptoms.

example: Fever is a common symptom.
examplePt: Febre é um sintoma comum.
tip: A sign that shows something may be wrong with your health.

example: The treatment lasted six weeks.
examplePt: O tratamento durou seis semanas.
tip: The medical care given to cure or manage an illness.

example: You need a prescription for this medicine.
examplePt: Você precisa de uma receita médica para este remédio.
tip: A written order from a doctor allowing you to get specific medicine.

example: He had surgery last week.
examplePt: Ele fez uma cirurgia na semana passada.
tip: A medical procedure where a doctor operates on the body.

example: The vaccine protects against the flu.
examplePt: A vacina protege contra a gripe.
tip: A substance that trains your immune system to fight a disease.

example: The wound got infected.
examplePt: A ferida infeccionou.
tip: When harmful germs invade and multiply in the body.

example: A strong immune system fights disease.
examplePt: Um sistema imunológico forte combate doenças.
tip: The body's natural defense against germs and disease.

example: She has a chronic condition.
examplePt: Ela tem uma condição crônica.
tip: Describes a long-lasting illness, the opposite of 'acute'.

example: See a physician if it doesn't improve.
examplePt: Procure um médico se não melhorar.
tip: A more formal word for 'doctor', common in written English.

example: The surgeon performed the operation.
examplePt: O cirurgião realizou a operação.
tip: A doctor who specializes in performing surgery.

example: The nurse checked his temperature.
examplePt: O enfermeiro verificou a temperatura dele.
tip: A healthcare professional who cares for patients, often alongside doctors.

example: The patient is resting now.
examplePt: O paciente está descansando agora.
tip: A person receiving medical treatment. Also means 'calm and tolerant' as an adjective!

example: They took him to the emergency room.
examplePt: Levaram ele para o pronto-socorro.
tip: Often shortened to 'ER' — where you go for urgent medical care.

example: The nurse checked her blood pressure.
examplePt: A enfermeira verificou a pressão arterial dela.
tip: The force of blood pushing against artery walls, measured in two numbers.

example: The doctor prescribed an antibiotic.
examplePt: O médico receitou um antibiótico.
tip: Medicine that fights bacterial infections. Doesn't work on viruses!

example: She has an allergy to peanuts.
examplePt: Ela tem alergia a amendoim.
tip: When the immune system overreacts to something harmless, like pollen or food.

example: He goes to therapy every week.
examplePt: Ele vai à terapia toda semana.
tip: Treatment for physical or mental health, often involving regular sessions.

example: She started rehabilitation after the injury.
examplePt: Ela começou a reabilitação depois da lesão.
tip: Often shortened to 'rehab' — the process of recovering health or ability.

example: The surgery required general anesthesia.
examplePt: A cirurgia exigiu anestesia geral.
tip: A treatment that stops you from feeling pain, often during surgery.

example: The doctor ordered an x-ray.
examplePt: O médico pediu um raio-X.
tip: An image that shows the bones and inside of the body.

example: His recovery was quick.
examplePt: A recuperação dele foi rápida.
tip: The process of getting better after an illness, injury, or surgery.

example: This disease is very rare.
examplePt: Essa doença é muito rara.
tip: A general word for illness, often more serious or long-term than 'sickness'.

example: The city faced an epidemic.
examplePt: A cidade enfrentou uma epidemia.
tip: A disease that spreads quickly among many people in one area.

example: The pandemic changed how we work.
examplePt: A pandemia mudou a forma como trabalhamos.
tip: An epidemic that spreads across countries or the whole world.

example: There's a new clinic in town.
examplePt: Há uma clínica nova na cidade.
tip: A place, usually smaller than a hospital, offering medical care.

example: You should see a specialist.
examplePt: Você deveria consultar um especialista.
tip: A doctor who focuses on one specific area of medicine.

example: The prognosis is very good.
examplePt: O prognóstico é muito bom.
tip: A doctor's prediction of how an illness will develop.

example: Clean the wound carefully.
examplePt: Limpe a ferida com cuidado.
tip: An injury that breaks the skin, like a cut.

example: She has a fracture in her arm.
examplePt: Ela tem uma fratura no braço.
tip: A crack or break, usually in a bone.

example: The inflammation reduced with medicine.
examplePt: A inflamação diminuiu com o remédio.
tip: Redness, heat, and swelling — the body's response to injury or infection.

example: Good nutrition keeps you healthy.
examplePt: Uma boa nutrição mantém você saudável.
tip: The science and practice of eating well for health.

example: Exercise improves your well-being.
examplePt: Exercício melhora o seu bem-estar.
tip: A general state of being healthy, happy, and comfortable.

example: Mental health is just as important as physical health.
examplePt: A saúde mental é tão importante quanto a física.
tip: Emotional and psychological well-being — how you think, feel, and cope.

example: They filed a lawsuit against the company.
examplePt: Eles abriram um processo judicial contra a empresa.
tip: A legal case brought to court, usually to settle a dispute.

example: She hired an attorney.
examplePt: Ela contratou um advogado.
tip: The American English word for 'lawyer', very common in the US.

example: The jury reached a verdict.
examplePt: O júri chegou a um veredito.
tip: A group of citizens who decide if someone is guilty or innocent in court.

example: The verdict surprised everyone.
examplePt: O veredito surpreendeu todo mundo.
tip: The final decision made by a jury or judge in a trial.

example: The eyewitness described the suspect.
examplePt: A testemunha ocular descreveu o suspeito.
tip: Someone who personally saw an event happen.

example: There wasn't enough evidence.
examplePt: Não havia evidência suficiente.
tip: Facts or proof used to support a claim in an investigation or trial.

example: Her testimony changed the case.
examplePt: O depoimento dela mudou o caso.
tip: A formal statement given as evidence, usually under oath.

example: The defendant pleaded not guilty.
examplePt: O réu se declarou inocente.
tip: The person being accused in a court case.

example: The plaintiff seeks compensation.
examplePt: O autor da ação busca uma indenização.
tip: The person who starts a lawsuit against someone else.

example: The jury found him guilty.
examplePt: O júri o considerou culpado.
tip: Legally responsible for a crime. The opposite is 'innocent'.

example: She proved she was innocent.
examplePt: Ela provou que era inocente.
tip: Not guilty of a crime. Everyone is 'innocent until proven guilty'.

example: The judge announced the sentence.
examplePt: O juiz anunciou a sentença.
tip: As a legal term, it's the punishment given by a court — not just a group of words!

example: The lawyer filed an appeal.
examplePt: O advogado entrou com um recurso.
tip: A request to a higher court to review a decision.

example: He specializes in contract law.
examplePt: Ele é especialista em direito contratual.
tip: The area of law dealing with agreements between people or companies.

example: It's not legal to do that here.
examplePt: Não é legal fazer isso aqui.
tip: Allowed by law. Careful: doesn't mean 'cool' like Portuguese slang 'legal'!

example: Driving without a license is illegal.
examplePt: Dirigir sem carteira é ilegal.
tip: Against the law — the opposite of 'legal'.

example: New regulations were introduced.
examplePt: Novos regulamentos foram introduzidos.
tip: An official rule set by an authority or government.

example: The legislation passed last year.
examplePt: A legislação foi aprovada no ano passado.
tip: Laws considered as a group, or the process of making laws.

example: The constitution protects free speech.
examplePt: A constituição protege a liberdade de expressão.
tip: The fundamental set of laws and principles that a country is governed by.

example: The organization defends human rights.
examplePt: A organização defende os direitos humanos.
tip: Basic rights and freedoms every person is entitled to, regardless of who they are.

example: The company accepted liability for the damage.
examplePt: A empresa assumiu a responsabilidade legal pelo dano.
tip: Being legally responsible for something, especially a loss or damage.

example: The mother has custody of the children.
examplePt: A mãe tem a guarda das crianças.
tip: Legal responsibility for taking care of someone, often a child.

example: He was released on bail.
examplePt: Ele foi solto sob fiança.
tip: Money paid to let someone go free while waiting for trial.

example: She will testify tomorrow.
examplePt: Ela vai testemunhar amanhã.
tip: To give a formal statement as a witness in court.

example: The prosecutor presented the case.
examplePt: O promotor apresentou o caso.
tip: The lawyer who represents the state and argues that the defendant is guilty.

example: It was charged as a felony.
examplePt: Foi acusado como crime grave.
tip: A serious crime, usually punished with a long prison sentence.

example: It's only a misdemeanor.
examplePt: É apenas uma contravenção.
tip: A minor crime, less serious than a felony.

example: The dispute led to litigation.
examplePt: A disputa levou a um litígio.
tip: The process of taking legal action or going to court.

example: They settled the dispute through arbitration.
examplePt: Eles resolveram a disputa por arbitragem.
tip: Settling a dispute outside of court, with a neutral third party deciding.

example: The court issued an injunction.
examplePt: O tribunal emitiu uma liminar.
tip: A court order telling someone to do or stop doing something.

example: Read the contract clause carefully.
examplePt: Leia a cláusula do contrato com cuidado.
tip: A specific section or condition within a legal document.

example: It was a breach of contract.
examplePt: Foi uma violação de contrato.
tip: Breaking a rule, law, or agreement.

example: The company ensures legal compliance.
examplePt: A empresa garante conformidade legal.
tip: Following rules, laws, or regulations correctly.

example: The director won an award.
examplePt: O diretor ganhou um prêmio.
tip: The person who controls how a film is made artistically.

example: She wrote the screenplay in a month.
examplePt: Ela escreveu o roteiro em um mês.
tip: The written script of a movie, including dialogue and scene descriptions.

example: He is a talented actor.
examplePt: Ele é um ator talentoso.
tip: Someone who performs a role in a film, play, or show.

example: The actress gave an amazing performance.
examplePt: A atriz deu uma atuação incrível.
tip: The female form of 'actor', though many now use 'actor' for everyone.

example: That scene made me cry.
examplePt: Aquela cena me fez chorar.
tip: A single part of a movie, filmed in one location or moment.

example: The plot was full of surprises.
examplePt: O enredo foi cheio de surpresas.
tip: The main story or sequence of events in a movie or book.

example: My favorite character died in the end.
examplePt: Meu personagem favorito morreu no final.
tip: A person (or being) in a story, film, or show.

example: The movie has a huge cast.
examplePt: O filme tem um elenco enorme.
tip: All the actors who perform in a film or show.

example: The premiere is next Friday.
examplePt: A estreia é na próxima sexta-feira.
tip: The very first public showing of a movie.

example: They already announced the sequel.
examplePt: Eles já anunciaram a continuação.
tip: A film that continues the story of an earlier one.

example: The trailer looks amazing.
examplePt: O trailer parece incrível.
tip: A short preview clip that advertises an upcoming movie.

example: The film broke box office records.
examplePt: O filme quebrou recordes de bilheteria.
tip: Where movie tickets are sold, or the money a film earns in total.

example: The special effects were incredible.
examplePt: Os efeitos especiais foram incríveis.
tip: Visual tricks used to create things that aren't really there, like explosions or monsters.

example: The cinematography won an award.
examplePt: A cinematografia ganhou um prêmio.
tip: The art of camera work and visual style in a film.

example: We watched a documentary about the ocean.
examplePt: Assistimos a um documentário sobre o oceano.
tip: A film that shows real facts and events, not fiction.

example: Animation takes a long time to make.
examplePt: Animação demora muito para ser feita.
tip: A technique that creates movement from drawings or computer images.

example: It became a summer blockbuster.
examplePt: Se tornou um sucesso de bilheteria no verão.
tip: A movie that is extremely popular and earns a lot of money.

example: The movie got great reviews.
examplePt: O filme recebeu ótimas críticas.
tip: A written opinion evaluating a movie, book, or product.

example: I watched it with subtitles.
examplePt: Eu assisti com legendas.
tip: Text at the bottom of the screen showing translated or written dialogue.

example: The dubbing wasn't very good.
examplePt: A dublagem não estava muito boa.
tip: Replacing the original voices in a film with a different language.

example: The actors memorized the script.
examplePt: Os atores memorizaram o roteiro.
tip: Similar to 'screenplay', but can also refer to TV or theater texts.

example: The storyline was hard to follow.
examplePt: A trama foi difícil de acompanhar.
tip: The plot or sequence of events that make up a story.

example: The villain had a tragic past.
examplePt: O vilão tinha um passado trágico.
tip: The bad character who opposes the hero.

example: The protagonist is a young detective.
examplePt: O protagonista é um jovem detetive.
tip: The main character of a story, usually the hero.

example: She won Best Supporting Role.
examplePt: Ela ganhou o prêmio de Melhor Papel Coadjuvante.
tip: A smaller role that supports the main characters.

example: The film received many awards.
examplePt: O filme recebeu muitos prêmios.
tip: A prize given to recognize achievement or excellence.

example: It received five nominations.
examplePt: Recebeu cinco indicações.
tip: Being officially suggested as a candidate to win an award.

example: The critics loved the film.
examplePt: Os críticos adoraram o filme.
tip: A professional who reviews and judges films, books, or art.

example: It's part of a huge franchise.
examplePt: Faz parte de uma franquia enorme.
tip: A series of connected movies, like a superhero universe.

example: They're making a remake of the classic.
examplePt: Estão fazendo uma refilmagem do clássico.
tip: A new version of a movie that already existed.

example: The movie uses flashbacks a lot.
examplePt: O filme usa muitos flashbacks.
tip: A scene that shows something that happened in the past.

example: The climax was very intense.
examplePt: O clímax foi muito intenso.
tip: The most exciting or important moment in a story.

example: The episode ended on a cliffhanger.
examplePt: O episódio terminou em um final de suspense.
tip: An ending that leaves the audience in suspense, wanting more.

example: The melody is very catchy.
examplePt: A melodia é muito grudenta.
