tip: The main tune of a song — the part you hum.

example: She has a great sense of rhythm.
examplePt: Ela tem um ótimo senso de ritmo.
tip: The pattern of beats in music. Notice the tricky spelling: r-h-y-t-h-m!

example: The singers created beautiful harmony.
examplePt: Os cantores criaram uma harmonia linda.
tip: When different musical notes sound good together.

example: I know all the lyrics by heart.
examplePt: Eu sei toda a letra de cor.
tip: The words of a song.

example: He learned three chords on guitar.
examplePt: Ele aprendeu três acordes no violão.
tip: Several musical notes played together at the same time.

example: She hit every note perfectly.
examplePt: Ela acertou cada nota perfeitamente.
tip: A single musical sound with a specific pitch.

example: This song has a strong beat.
examplePt: Essa música tem uma batida forte.
tip: The steady rhythm or pulse that you tap your foot to.

example: The tempo speeds up in the chorus.
examplePt: O andamento acelera no refrão.
tip: How fast or slow a piece of music is played.

example: Beethoven is a famous composer.
examplePt: Beethoven é um compositor famoso.
tip: A person who writes original music.

example: The orchestra played beautifully.
examplePt: A orquestra tocou lindamente.
tip: A large group of musicians playing different instruments together.

example: The conductor raised his baton.
examplePt: O regente levantou a batuta.
tip: The person who leads and directs an orchestra.

example: She sings in the school choir.
examplePt: Ela canta no coral da escola.
tip: A group of people who sing together.

example: What instrument do you play?
examplePt: Que instrumento você toca?
tip: An object used to make music, like a guitar or piano.

example: She plays the violin beautifully.
examplePt: Ela toca violino lindamente.
tip: A small, stringed instrument played with a bow.

example: He plays drums in a band.
examplePt: Ele toca bateria em uma banda.
tip: A percussion instrument you hit to make a beat.

example: We went to a concert last night.
examplePt: Fomos a um show ontem à noite.
tip: A live music performance.

example: Their new album just came out.
examplePt: O novo álbum deles acabou de sair.
tip: A collection of songs released together.

example: This is my favorite track.
examplePt: Essa é minha faixa favorita.
tip: A single song, especially on an album.

example: What music genre do you like?
examplePt: Que gênero musical você gosta?
tip: A category or style of music, like rock or jazz.

example: Her vocals are incredible.
examplePt: Os vocais dela são incríveis.
tip: Related to the singing voice.

example: He sang slightly off pitch.
examplePt: Ele cantou um pouco desafinado.
tip: How high or low a musical note sounds.

example: That's a catchy tune.
examplePt: Essa é uma melodia grudenta.
tip: Can mean 'a melody' or the verb 'to adjust an instrument's pitch'.

example: They performed his fifth symphony.
examplePt: Eles apresentaram a quinta sinfonia dele.
tip: A long orchestral piece, usually in several parts.

example: That bassline is so groovy.
examplePt: Essa linha de baixo é muito envolvente.
tip: The low musical line that gives a song its groove.

example: Jazz is famous for improvisation.
examplePt: O jazz é famoso pela improvisação.
tip: Creating music spontaneously, without planning it in advance.

example: I love the movie's soundtrack.
examplePt: Eu amo a trilha sonora do filme.
tip: The music that plays throughout a movie or show.

example: She's a talented songwriter.
examplePt: Ela é uma compositora de canções talentosa.
tip: Someone who writes both the music and lyrics of songs.

example: The song builds to a crescendo.
examplePt: A música se constrói até um crescendo.
tip: A gradual increase in loudness or intensity.

example: The crowd asked for an encore.
examplePt: A plateia pediu um bis.
tip: An extra performance requested by an audience after the show ends.

example: She has an audition tomorrow.
examplePt: Ela tem uma audição amanhã.
tip: A short performance to test if someone is good enough for a role.

example: We have rehearsal every Tuesday.
examplePt: Temos ensaio toda terça-feira.
tip: A practice session before a real performance.

example: He played an acoustic version.
examplePt: Ele tocou uma versão acústica.
tip: Music played without electronic amplification.

example: They booked a recording studio.
examplePt: Eles reservaram um estúdio de gravação.
tip: A place equipped to record music professionally.

example: Don't forget your passport.
examplePt: Não esqueça seu passaporte.
tip: The official document you need to travel to another country.

example: Our itinerary includes three cities.
examplePt: Nosso roteiro inclui três cidades.
tip: A detailed plan of a trip, including dates and places.

example: Show your boarding pass at the gate.
examplePt: Mostre seu cartão de embarque no portão.
tip: The ticket that allows you to board a plane.

example: My luggage was lost at the airport.
examplePt: Minha bagagem se perdeu no aeroporto.
tip: A general, uncountable word for suitcases and bags.

example: We waited in line at customs.
examplePt: Esperamos na fila da alfândega.
tip: The place at a border where officials check your bags and documents.

example: Our departure is at 6 AM.
examplePt: Nossa partida é às 6h da manhã.
tip: The act of leaving, especially for a flight or trip.

example: The arrival is scheduled for noon.
examplePt: A chegada está marcada para o meio-dia.
tip: The moment you reach your destination.

example: We had a two-hour layover in Miami.
examplePt: Tivemos uma escala de duas horas em Miami.
tip: A stop between flights before reaching the final destination.

example: Paris is a popular destination.
examplePt: Paris é um destino popular.
tip: The place where you are going.

example: We booked our accommodation online.
examplePt: Reservamos nossa hospedagem online.
tip: A place to stay, like a hotel or hostel.

example: I made a reservation for two.
examplePt: Eu fiz uma reserva para duas pessoas.
tip: A booking made in advance for a room, table, or seat.

example: The city is full of tourists.
examplePt: A cidade está cheia de turistas.
tip: A person traveling for pleasure, visiting places away from home.

example: We spent the day sightseeing.
examplePt: Passamos o dia fazendo passeios turísticos.
tip: Visiting interesting or famous places as a tourist.

example: The tower is a famous landmark.
examplePt: A torre é um ponto turístico famoso.
tip: A well-known building or place that helps identify a location.

example: I bought a souvenir for my mom.
examplePt: Comprei uma lembrança para minha mãe.
tip: An object you keep to remember a place or trip.

example: There's a currency exchange at the airport.
examplePt: Há um câmbio de moeda no aeroporto.
tip: The place or process of trading one country's money for another's.

example: She traveled as a backpacker for a year.
examplePt: Ela viajou como mochileira por um ano.
tip: A traveler who carries their belongings in a backpack, on a budget.

example: It was a long journey.
examplePt: Foi uma jornada longa.
tip: A trip from one place to another, often a long one.

example: They set out on a voyage across the ocean.
examplePt: Eles partiram numa viagem através do oceano.
tip: A long journey, especially by sea or in space.

example: We booked a boat excursion.
examplePt: Reservamos uma excursão de barco.
tip: A short trip made for pleasure, often organized in a group.

example: You need a visa to enter the country.
examplePt: Você precisa de um visto para entrar no país.
tip: Official permission to enter or stay in a foreign country.

example: We crossed the border by car.
examplePt: Cruzamos a fronteira de carro.
tip: The line that separates two countries.

example: Our flight leaves from terminal 2.
examplePt: Nosso voo sai do terminal 2.
tip: A building at an airport where passengers arrive and depart.

example: They went on a cruise for their honeymoon.
examplePt: Eles fizeram um cruzeiro na lua de mel.
tip: A vacation trip on a large ship, visiting several ports.

example: We stayed at a beach resort.
examplePt: Ficamos em um resort na praia.
tip: A hotel or place designed for vacation and relaxation.

example: The hostel was cheap and clean.
examplePt: O albergue era barato e limpo.
tip: Budget-friendly accommodation, often with shared rooms.

example: Our guide spoke three languages.
examplePt: Nosso guia falava três idiomas.
tip: A person who shows tourists around and explains local sights.

example: We took a different route home.
examplePt: Tomamos uma rota diferente para casa.
tip: The path or way taken to get somewhere.

example: It was the adventure of a lifetime.
examplePt: Foi a aventura de uma vida.
tip: An exciting, sometimes risky, experience or journey.

example: She felt culture shock when she moved abroad.
examplePt: Ela sentiu choque cultural quando se mudou para o exterior.
tip: The confusion or discomfort felt when experiencing a new culture.

example: Ask a local for recommendations.
examplePt: Peça recomendações a um morador local.
tip: As a noun, it means someone who lives in that place — not a tourist.

example: They organized an expedition to the mountains.
examplePt: Eles organizaram uma expedição para as montanhas.
tip: A journey with a specific purpose, often to explore somewhere difficult to reach.

example: She has serious wanderlust.
examplePt: Ela tem uma vontade enorme de viajar.
tip: A strong desire to travel and explore the world.

example: This recipe is from my grandmother.
examplePt: Esta receita é da minha avó.
tip: Instructions for preparing a dish. Careful: 'receita médica' is 'prescription'!

example: We need one more ingredient.
examplePt: Precisamos de mais um ingrediente.
tip: Any food item used to make a dish.

example: Add a little spice to the sauce.
examplePt: Adicione um pouco de tempero ao molho.
tip: A dried seasoning from seeds, bark, or roots, like pepper or cinnamon.

example: Fresh herbs make a big difference.
examplePt: Ervas frescas fazem muita diferença.
tip: A leafy green seasoning like basil or parsley. In American English, the 'h' is silent!

example: Let's bake a cake today.
examplePt: Vamos assar um bolo hoje.
tip: To cook in an oven using dry heat, typical for bread and cakes.

example: Boil the water first.
examplePt: Ferva a água primeiro.
tip: To heat liquid until it bubbles at 100°C.

example: Fry the onions until golden.
examplePt: Frite as cebolas até dourarem.
tip: To cook in hot oil or fat.

example: We grilled fish for dinner.
examplePt: Grelhamos peixe no jantar.
tip: To cook over direct heat, usually on metal bars.

example: She roasted a chicken.
examplePt: Ela assou um frango.
tip: To cook meat or vegetables in an oven with fat, until browned outside.

example: Let the soup simmer for an hour.
examplePt: Deixe a sopa cozinhar em fogo baixo por uma hora.
tip: To cook gently just below boiling, with small bubbles.

example: Chop the garlic finely.
examplePt: Pique o alho finamente.
tip: To cut food into small pieces with a knife.

example: Slice the bread, please.
examplePt: Fatie o pão, por favor.
tip: To cut into thin, flat pieces. Also a noun: 'a slice of pizza'.

example: Stir the sauce constantly.
examplePt: Mexa o molho constantemente.
tip: To move food around in circles with a spoon.

example: Whisk the eggs until fluffy.
examplePt: Bata os ovos até ficarem fofos.
tip: Both the tool and the action of beating ingredients quickly to add air.

example: Knead the dough for ten minutes.
examplePt: Sove a massa por dez minutos.
tip: To press and fold dough with your hands. The 'k' is silent!

example: Marinate the meat overnight.
examplePt: Marine a carne durante a noite.
tip: To soak food in a seasoned liquid before cooking, to add flavor.

example: Garnish with fresh parsley.
examplePt: Guarneça com salsinha fresca.
tip: To decorate a dish with something small and edible.

example: We ordered an appetizer first.
examplePt: Pedimos uma entrada primeiro.
tip: A small dish served before the main course. Called 'starter' in the UK.

example: What's for dessert?
examplePt: O que tem de sobremesa?
tip: The sweet dish at the end of a meal. Two 's' — 'desert' with one 's' is a dry place!

example: The chef prepared a special menu.
examplePt: O chef preparou um menu especial.
tip: A professional cook, especially one in charge of a kitchen.

example: This sauce has a strong flavor.
examplePt: Este molho tem um sabor forte.
tip: The taste of food. Spelled 'flavour' in British English.

example: I love the texture of this bread.
examplePt: Eu amo a textura deste pão.
tip: How food feels in your mouth — creamy, crunchy, smooth.

example: The aroma of coffee filled the room.
examplePt: O aroma de café encheu a sala.
tip: A pleasant smell, especially from food or drink.

example: This lemon is very sour.
examplePt: Este limão está muito azedo.
tip: The sharp taste of lemons and vinegar.

example: Dark chocolate tastes bitter.
examplePt: Chocolate amargo tem gosto amargo.
tip: The strong, sharp taste of coffee or dark chocolate.

example: I love spicy food.
examplePt: Eu amo comida picante.
tip: Food that burns your mouth, like chili peppers.

example: I prefer savory snacks over sweet ones.
examplePt: Prefiro lanches salgados aos doces.
tip: Tasty but not sweet — the opposite of dessert flavors.

example: The fries are perfectly crispy.
examplePt: As batatas estão perfeitamente crocantes.
tip: Hard and making a nice sound when you bite it.

example: These bananas are ripe now.
examplePt: Essas bananas estão maduras agora.
tip: Fruit that is ready to eat, fully developed.

example: We ate the leftovers for lunch.
examplePt: Comemos as sobras no almoço.
tip: Food remaining from an earlier meal. Always plural!

example: Italian cuisine is famous worldwide.
examplePt: A culinária italiana é famosa mundialmente.
tip: A style of cooking, usually connected to a country or region.

example: Can I see the menu, please?
examplePt: Posso ver o cardápio, por favor?
tip: The list of dishes available at a restaurant.

example: Let the dough rest for an hour.
examplePt: Deixe a massa descansar por uma hora.
tip: The uncooked mix of flour and water used for bread and pizza.

example: Solve this equation, please.
examplePt: Resolva esta equação, por favor.
tip: A math statement showing two things are equal, using the = sign.

example: I forgot the formula for area.
examplePt: Esqueci a fórmula da área.
tip: A rule expressed in symbols. Plural can be 'formulas' or 'formulae'.

example: The Pythagorean theorem is famous.
examplePt: O teorema de Pitágoras é famoso.
tip: A mathematical statement that has been proven true.

example: The proof took three pages.
examplePt: A demonstração levou três páginas.
tip: A logical argument showing something is definitely true.

example: Let x be the variable.
examplePt: Seja x a variável.
tip: A symbol (usually a letter) representing an unknown value.

example: One half is a fraction.
examplePt: Um meio é uma fração.
tip: A part of a whole, written like 1/2 or 3/4.

example: Round to two decimal places.
examplePt: Arredonde para duas casas decimais.
tip: A number with a point, like 3.14. English uses a dot, Portuguese uses a comma!

example: What percentage passed the test?
examplePt: Qual porcentagem passou na prova?
tip: A number expressed as a part of 100, using the % symbol.

example: The ratio is two to one.
examplePt: A razão é dois para um.
tip: A comparison between two quantities, written like 2:1.

example: The average score was 75.
examplePt: A média das notas foi 75.
tip: Add all values and divide by how many there are. Also called 'mean'.

example: The sum of 2 and 3 is 5.
examplePt: A soma de 2 e 3 é 5.
tip: The result of adding numbers together.

example: Subtract five from ten.
examplePt: Subtraia cinco de dez.
tip: To take one number away from another.

example: Multiply the length by the width.
examplePt: Multiplique o comprimento pela largura.
tip: To add a number to itself a certain number of times.

example: Divide the cake into eight pieces.
examplePt: Divida o bolo em oito pedaços.
tip: To split into equal parts.

example: The square root of nine is three.
examplePt: A raiz quadrada de nove é três.
tip: A number that, multiplied by itself, gives the original number.

example: The exponent tells you the power.
examplePt: O expoente indica a potência.
tip: The small number written above, showing how many times to multiply.

example: Algebra uses letters for numbers.
examplePt: Álgebra usa letras no lugar de números.
tip: The branch of math using symbols to represent unknown numbers.

example: Geometry studies shapes and space.
examplePt: Geometria estuda formas e espaço.
tip: The branch of math dealing with shapes, lines, and angles.

example: Calculus is used in physics.
examplePt: Cálculo é usado em física.
tip: Advanced math studying continuous change and rates.

example: Statistics show a clear trend.
examplePt: As estatísticas mostram uma tendência clara.
tip: The study of collecting and analyzing data.

example: The probability is fifty percent.
examplePt: A probabilidade é de cinquenta por cento.
tip: How likely something is to happen.

example: The graph shows growth over time.
examplePt: O gráfico mostra o crescimento ao longo do tempo.
tip: A visual diagram showing the relationship between numbers.

example: Label the horizontal axis.
examplePt: Nomeie o eixo horizontal.
tip: A reference line on a graph. Plural is 'axes'.

example: A right angle is ninety degrees.
examplePt: Um ângulo reto tem noventa graus.
tip: The space between two lines that meet, measured in degrees.

example: A triangle has three sides.
examplePt: Um triângulo tem três lados.
tip: A shape with three straight sides and three angles.

example: Draw a perfect circle.
examplePt: Desenhe um círculo perfeito.
tip: A perfectly round shape where every point is the same distance from the center.

example: Measure the radius of the circle.
examplePt: Meça o raio do círculo.
tip: The distance from the center of a circle to its edge.

example: The diameter is twice the radius.
examplePt: O diâmetro é o dobro do raio.
tip: A straight line passing through the center, from edge to edge.

example: The design has perfect symmetry.
examplePt: O design tem simetria perfeita.
tip: When both halves of something look exactly the same.

example: The sequence continues to infinity.
examplePt: A sequência continua até o infinito.
tip: A quantity without any limit or end, written with a sideways 8.

example: Can you estimate the cost?
examplePt: Você pode estimar o custo?
tip: To calculate an approximate value, not an exact one.

example: Calculate the total, please.
examplePt: Calcule o total, por favor.
tip: To work out an answer using math.

example: Seven is an odd number.
examplePt: Sete é um número ímpar.
tip: A number that cannot be divided evenly by 2. 'Odd' also means 'strange'!

example: Ten is an even number.
examplePt: Dez é um número par.
tip: A number that divides evenly by 2.

example: Our galaxy is called the Milky Way.
examplePt: Nossa galáxia se chama Via Láctea.
tip: A huge system of billions of stars held together by gravity.

example: The Moon orbits the Earth.
examplePt: A Lua orbita a Terra.
tip: The curved path an object takes around a planet or star.

example: We watched Saturn through a telescope.
examplePt: Observamos Saturno pelo telescópio.
tip: An instrument that makes distant objects look closer.

example: Mars is the fourth planet.
examplePt: Marte é o quarto planeta.
tip: A large body orbiting a star. Our solar system has eight.

example: The satellite sends weather data.
examplePt: O satélite envia dados meteorológicos.
tip: An object orbiting a planet — natural (the Moon) or artificial.

example: The comet appears every 76 years.
examplePt: O cometa aparece a cada 76 anos.
tip: An icy body that grows a bright tail when it nears the Sun.

example: An asteroid passed close to Earth.
examplePt: Um asteroide passou perto da Terra.
tip: A rocky object orbiting the Sun, smaller than a planet.

example: We saw a meteor last night.
examplePt: Vimos um meteoro ontem à noite.
tip: A space rock burning up in the atmosphere — a 'shooting star'.

example: The solar eclipse lasted two minutes.
examplePt: O eclipse solar durou dois minutos.
tip: When one space object blocks the light of another.

example: Orion is a famous constellation.
examplePt: Órion é uma constelação famosa.
tip: A group of stars forming a recognizable pattern in the sky.

example: The nebula glows in many colors.
examplePt: A nebulosa brilha em muitas cores.
tip: A giant cloud of gas and dust where stars are born.

example: Nothing escapes a black hole.
examplePt: Nada escapa de um buraco negro.
tip: A region where gravity is so strong that not even light can escape.

example: Our solar system has eight planets.
examplePt: Nosso sistema solar tem oito planetas.
tip: The Sun and everything that orbits it.

example: The universe is always expanding.
examplePt: O universo está sempre se expandindo.
tip: Everything that exists — all space, matter, and time.

example: That star is four light years away.
examplePt: Aquela estrela está a quatro anos-luz.
tip: A measure of DISTANCE, not time — how far light travels in one year.

example: The astronaut floated in the station.
examplePt: O astronauta flutuou na estação.
tip: A person trained to travel in space.

example: The spacecraft landed on Mars.
examplePt: A nave espacial pousou em Marte.
tip: A vehicle designed to travel in space.

example: The rocket launched at dawn.
examplePt: O foguete foi lançado ao amanhecer.
tip: A vehicle that pushes itself upward by burning fuel.

example: The launch was delayed by weather.
examplePt: O lançamento foi adiado pelo tempo.
tip: To send something into the air or space. Also used for new products!

example: Earth's atmosphere protects us.
examplePt: A atmosfera da Terra nos protege.
tip: The layer of gases surrounding a planet. Also means 'mood' of a place!

example: The Moon is covered in craters.
examplePt: A Lua é coberta de crateras.
tip: A round hole made by an impact or volcanic activity.

example: The lunar surface is dusty.
examplePt: A superfície lunar é empoeirada.
tip: Related to the Moon. 'Solar' is the equivalent for the Sun.

example: A supernova is a dying star exploding.
examplePt: Uma supernova é uma estrela morrendo em explosão.
tip: The massive explosion of a star at the end of its life.

example: We visited the observatory at night.
examplePt: Visitamos o observatório à noite.
tip: A building with telescopes for studying the sky.

example: The astronomer discovered a new planet.
examplePt: O astrônomo descobriu um novo planeta.
tip: A scientist who studies space. Not the same as an 'astrologer'!

example: Stars are celestial bodies.
examplePt: Estrelas são corpos celestes.
tip: Related to the sky or outer space.

example: Space radiation is dangerous.
examplePt: A radiação espacial é perigosa.
tip: Energy traveling as waves or particles, like light or X-rays.

example: Dark matter is invisible but has mass.
examplePt: A matéria escura é invisível mas tem massa.
tip: Mysterious material that makes up most of the universe's mass.

example: Interstellar travel is still science fiction.
examplePt: Viagem interestelar ainda é ficção científica.
tip: Between the stars. 'Inter' = between, 'stellar' = of stars.

example: Astronauts live on the space station.
examplePt: Astronautas vivem na estação espacial.
tip: A large spacecraft where people can live and work in orbit.

example: The planet has a strong gravity field.
examplePt: O planeta tem um campo gravitacional forte.
tip: The region around a mass where its gravitational pull is felt.

example: She studies astronomy at university.
examplePt: Ela estuda astronomia na universidade.
tip: The scientific study of stars, planets, and space.

example: The cosmos is full of mysteries.
examplePt: O cosmos é cheio de mistérios.
tip: A poetic word for the universe seen as an ordered whole.

example: Sustainability matters for the future.
examplePt: Sustentabilidade importa para o futuro.
tip: Using resources in a way that doesn't harm future generations.

example: Recycling reduces waste.
examplePt: A reciclagem reduz o lixo.
tip: Turning used materials into new products.

example: Air pollution is a serious problem.
examplePt: A poluição do ar é um problema sério.
tip: Harmful substances released into the air, water, or soil.

example: Car emissions harm the atmosphere.
examplePt: As emissões dos carros prejudicam a atmosfera.
tip: Gases or substances released into the air, usually harmful.

example: Solar power is renewable energy.
examplePt: Energia solar é energia renovável.
tip: A resource that naturally replaces itself, like wind or sunlight.

example: Flying increases your carbon footprint.
examplePt: Voar aumenta sua pegada de carbono.
tip: The total greenhouse gases your actions produce.

example: The greenhouse effect warms the planet.
examplePt: O efeito estufa aquece o planeta.
tip: When gases trap heat in the atmosphere, like glass in a greenhouse.

example: Deforestation threatens the Amazon.
examplePt: O desmatamento ameaça a Amazônia.
tip: The clearing or destruction of forests.

example: Brazil has amazing biodiversity.
examplePt: O Brasil tem uma biodiversidade incrível.
tip: The variety of all living things in an area.

example: The reef is a fragile ecosystem.
examplePt: O recife é um ecossistema frágil.
tip: A community of living things interacting with their environment.

example: Conservation protects natural areas.
examplePt: A conservação protege áreas naturais.
tip: Protecting nature and using resources carefully.

example: Tigers are an endangered species.
examplePt: Tigres são uma espécie em extinção.
tip: At serious risk of disappearing forever.

example: Dinosaurs are extinct.
examplePt: Os dinossauros estão extintos.
tip: No longer existing anywhere on Earth.

example: Pollution destroys their habitat.
examplePt: A poluição destrói o habitat deles.
tip: The natural home of an animal or plant.

example: Climate change affects everyone.
examplePt: A mudança climática afeta todos.
tip: Long-term shifts in temperature and weather patterns.

example: Global warming melts the ice caps.
examplePt: O aquecimento global derrete as calotas polares.
tip: The rise in Earth's average temperature over time.

example: Coal is a fossil fuel.
examplePt: Carvão é um combustível fóssil.
tip: Energy sources formed from ancient plants and animals, like oil and coal.

example: They installed solar panels on the roof.
examplePt: Eles instalaram painéis solares no telhado.
tip: A device that converts sunlight into electricity.

example: Wind turbines generate clean energy.
examplePt: Turbinas eólicas geram energia limpa.
tip: A tall machine that turns wind into electricity.

example: We make compost from food scraps.
examplePt: Fazemos composto com restos de comida.
tip: Decayed organic matter used to enrich soil.

example: Most plastic ends up in a landfill.
examplePt: A maior parte do plástico acaba em um aterro.
tip: A site where garbage is buried underground.

example: We must reduce food waste.
examplePt: Precisamos reduzir o desperdício de comida.
tip: Material thrown away, or the act of using something carelessly.

example: The drought lasted three years.
examplePt: A seca durou três anos.
tip: A long period with little or no rain. The 'gh' is silent!

example: The flood destroyed many homes.
examplePt: A enchente destruiu muitas casas.
tip: When water covers land that is usually dry.

example: Erosion is wearing down the cliff.
examplePt: A erosão está desgastando o penhasco.
tip: The slow wearing away of soil or rock by wind and water.

example: The rainforest produces oxygen.
examplePt: A floresta tropical produz oxigênio.
tip: A dense forest with very high rainfall, full of species.

example: The park protects local wildlife.
examplePt: O parque protege a vida selvagem local.
tip: Wild animals living in their natural environment.

example: This species lives only here.
examplePt: Esta espécie vive só aqui.
tip: A group of similar organisms that can reproduce together. Same in singular and plural!

example: She buys organic vegetables.
examplePt: Ela compra vegetais orgânicos.
tip: Grown without artificial chemicals or pesticides.

example: The river contains toxic chemicals.
examplePt: O rio contém produtos químicos tóxicos.
tip: Poisonous and harmful to living things.

example: Water contamination is dangerous.
examplePt: A contaminação da água é perigosa.
tip: When something harmful gets mixed into something clean.

example: We must preserve the forest.
examplePt: Devemos preservar a floresta.
tip: To protect something so it stays in its original state.

example: This is a sustainable solution.
examplePt: Esta é uma solução sustentável.
tip: Able to continue without damaging the environment.

example: His behavior changed suddenly.
examplePt: O comportamento dele mudou de repente.
tip: The way someone acts. Spelled 'behaviour' in British English.

example: Perception can be misleading.
examplePt: A percepção pode ser enganosa.
tip: How we interpret information from our senses.

example: Sleep affects cognition.
examplePt: O sono afeta a cognição.
tip: The mental processes of thinking, learning, and understanding.

example: He lost consciousness for a moment.
examplePt: Ele perdeu a consciência por um momento.
tip: Being awake and aware of yourself and your surroundings.

example: Dreams come from the subconscious.
examplePt: Os sonhos vêm do subconsciente.
tip: The part of your mind working below your awareness.

example: She struggles with anxiety.
examplePt: Ela luta contra a ansiedade.
tip: A feeling of worry or nervousness, often about the future.

example: Depression is a real illness.
examplePt: A depressão é uma doença real.
tip: A serious mood disorder causing lasting sadness and loss of interest.

example: Too much stress harms your health.
examplePt: Estresse demais prejudica sua saúde.
tip: Mental or physical tension from difficult situations.

example: He is recovering from trauma.
examplePt: Ele está se recuperando de um trauma.
tip: A deeply disturbing experience with lasting effects.

example: Empathy helps us connect.
examplePt: A empatia nos ajuda a conectar.
tip: The ability to understand and share another person's feelings.

example: I lost my motivation to study.
examplePt: Perdi minha motivação para estudar.
tip: The reason or drive that makes you act.

example: She has a warm personality.
examplePt: Ela tem uma personalidade calorosa.
tip: The combination of traits that makes each person unique.

example: Reading is a good habit.
examplePt: Ler é um bom hábito.
tip: Something you do regularly, often without thinking.

example: Trust your instinct.
examplePt: Confie no seu instinto.
tip: A natural, automatic reaction you're born with.

example: He hid his emotions well.
examplePt: Ele escondeu bem suas emoções.
tip: A strong feeling like joy, anger, or fear.

example: I'm in a good mood today.
examplePt: Estou de bom humor hoje.
tip: Your temporary emotional state. Not 'humor' as in comedy!

example: Praise builds self-esteem.
examplePt: Elogios constroem a autoestima.
tip: How much you value and respect yourself.

example: A growth mindset helps you learn.
examplePt: Uma mentalidade de crescimento ajuda a aprender.
tip: Your established set of attitudes and beliefs.

example: Pay attention to the details.
examplePt: Preste atenção aos detalhes.
tip: Mental focus directed at something.

example: I can't focus with this noise.
examplePt: Não consigo focar com esse barulho.
tip: To concentrate on one thing. Also a noun: 'my focus'.

example: We all have unconscious bias.
examplePt: Todos temos vieses inconscientes.
tip: An unfair preference or prejudice that affects judgment.

example: He is still in denial.
examplePt: Ele ainda está em negação.
tip: Refusing to accept a painful truth.

example: Her resilience is inspiring.
examplePt: A resiliência dela é inspiradora.
tip: The ability to recover quickly from difficulties.

example: He started counseling last month.
examplePt: Ele começou o aconselhamento mês passado.
tip: Professional guidance to help with personal problems.

example: She was diagnosed with a sleep disorder.
examplePt: Ela foi diagnosticada com um transtorno do sono.
tip: A condition that disrupts normal physical or mental function.

example: Addiction requires treatment.
examplePt: O vício requer tratamento.
tip: A compulsive need for a substance or behavior.

example: Blinking is a reflex.
examplePt: Piscar é um reflexo.
tip: An automatic body response you can't control.

example: He bought it on impulse.
examplePt: Ele comprou por impulso.
tip: A sudden urge to act without thinking.

example: Self-awareness is important.
examplePt: A autopercepção é importante.
tip: Knowledge or understanding of a situation or yourself.

example: As an introvert, she needs quiet time.
examplePt: Como introvertida, ela precisa de tempo em silêncio.
tip: Someone who gains energy from being alone.

example: He's a natural extrovert.
examplePt: Ele é um extrovertido nato.
tip: Someone who gains energy from being around people.

example: She suffered burnout from overwork.
examplePt: Ela sofreu esgotamento por excesso de trabalho.
tip: Complete exhaustion caused by prolonged stress.

example: Exercise is a healthy coping strategy.
examplePt: Exercício é uma estratégia saudável de enfrentamento.
tip: Dealing successfully with a difficult situation.

example: The Roman Empire lasted centuries.
examplePt: O Império Romano durou séculos.
tip: A large group of countries ruled by one supreme authority.

example: Ancient civilizations built great cities.
examplePt: Civilizações antigas construíram grandes cidades.
tip: An advanced society with cities, government, and writing.

example: The revolution changed the country.
examplePt: A revolução mudou o país.
tip: A sudden, complete overthrow of a government or system.

example: The dynasty ruled for 300 years.
examplePt: A dinastia governou por 300 anos.
tip: A series of rulers from the same family.

example: Brazil was a Portuguese colony.
examplePt: O Brasil foi uma colônia portuguesa.
tip: A territory controlled by a distant country.

example: The conquest took ten years.
examplePt: A conquista levou dez anos.
tip: Taking control of a place by force.

example: They signed a peace treaty.
examplePt: Eles assinaram um tratado de paz.
tip: A formal agreement between countries.

example: Ancient Egypt fascinates me.
examplePt: O Egito Antigo me fascina.
tip: Belonging to the very distant past.

example: Medieval castles were fortresses.
examplePt: Castelos medievais eram fortalezas.
tip: Related to the Middle Ages, roughly 500-1500 AD.

example: The Renaissance began in Italy.
examplePt: O Renascimento começou na Itália.
tip: The European rebirth of art and learning, 14th-17th centuries.

example: The UK is still a monarchy.
examplePt: O Reino Unido ainda é uma monarquia.
tip: A system where a king or queen is head of state.

example: The emperor ruled with absolute power.
examplePt: O imperador governava com poder absoluto.
tip: The ruler of an empire, above a king in rank.

example: The knight wore heavy armor.
examplePt: O cavaleiro usava armadura pesada.
tip: A medieval warrior on horseback. The 'k' and 'gh' are silent!

example: The castle stood on a hill.
examplePt: O castelo ficava numa colina.
tip: A large fortified building. The 't' is silent!

example: The pharaoh was buried in a pyramid.
examplePt: O faraó foi enterrado numa pirâmide.
tip: The title of ancient Egyptian rulers.

example: The tribe lived near the river.
examplePt: A tribo vivia perto do rio.
tip: A social group sharing ancestry, customs, and leadership.

example: The museum displays ancient artifacts.
examplePt: O museu exibe artefatos antigos.
tip: An object made by humans, valuable for historical study.

example: The excavation revealed a tomb.
examplePt: A escavação revelou uma tumba.
tip: Digging carefully to uncover buried remains.

example: We explored the ancient ruins.
examplePt: Exploramos as ruínas antigas.
tip: The remains of destroyed buildings. Usually plural!

example: This site is world heritage.
examplePt: Este local é patrimônio mundial.
tip: Traditions and buildings passed down from the past.

example: His legacy still influences us.
examplePt: O legado dele ainda nos influencia.
tip: Something handed down from the past, or left behind by a person.

example: It was the end of an era.
examplePt: Foi o fim de uma era.
tip: A long, distinct period of history.

example: This happened in the 19th century.
examplePt: Isso aconteceu no século 19.
tip: A period of one hundred years.

example: The 90s were a great decade.
examplePt: Os anos 90 foram uma ótima década.
tip: A period of ten years.

example: They declared independence in 1822.
examplePt: Eles declararam independência em 1822.
tip: Freedom from control by another country.

example: The rebellion was crushed.
examplePt: A rebelião foi esmagada.
tip: An organized resistance against authority.

example: The two nations formed an alliance.
examplePt: As duas nações formaram uma aliança.
tip: A formal agreement to cooperate, especially between countries.

example: The invasion started at dawn.
examplePt: A invasão começou ao amanhecer.
tip: Entering a place by force to take control.

example: The siege lasted six months.
examplePt: O cerco durou seis meses.
tip: Surrounding a city to force it to surrender.

example: The fortress protected the city.
examplePt: A fortaleza protegia a cidade.
tip: A heavily defended military building.

example: Archaeology reveals lost cultures.
examplePt: A arqueologia revela culturas perdidas.
tip: The study of human history through excavated objects.

example: Nomads move with the seasons.
examplePt: Nômades se movem com as estações.
tip: A person who moves from place to place instead of settling.

example: The chronicle records daily life.
examplePt: A crônica registra a vida cotidiana.
tip: A written record of historical events in order of time.

example: The crisis was solved through diplomacy.
examplePt: A crise foi resolvida pela diplomacia.
tip: Managing relations between countries peacefully.

example: The ambassador met the president.
examplePt: O embaixador encontrou o presidente.
tip: A country's official representative in another nation.

example: Go to the embassy for your visa.
examplePt: Vá à embaixada para seu visto.
tip: The official building where a country's diplomats work abroad.

example: They defended their national sovereignty.
examplePt: Eles defenderam sua soberania nacional.
tip: A country's full authority to govern itself.

example: Democracy depends on free elections.
examplePt: A democracia depende de eleições livres.
tip: A system where citizens vote to choose their government.

example: Brazil is a federal republic.
examplePt: O Brasil é uma república federativa.
tip: A state where power rests with elected representatives, not a monarch.

example: The country lived under a dictatorship.
examplePt: O país viveu sob uma ditadura.
tip: Government by a single ruler with absolute power.

example: Parliament voted on the new law.
examplePt: O parlamento votou a nova lei.
tip: The legislative body that makes laws in many countries.

example: The Senate approved the bill.
examplePt: O Senado aprovou o projeto de lei.
tip: The upper chamber of a legislature in many countries.

example: Three candidates are running.
examplePt: Três candidatos estão concorrendo.
tip: A person seeking election to a position.

example: The campaign lasted three months.
examplePt: A campanha durou três meses.
tip: An organized effort to win an election or achieve a goal.

example: She marked her ballot carefully.
examplePt: Ela marcou sua cédula com cuidado.
tip: The paper or system used to cast a secret vote.

example: The referendum passed by a small margin.
examplePt: O referendo passou por uma pequena margem.
tip: A direct public vote on a single political question.

example: The new policy takes effect Monday.
examplePt: A nova política entra em vigor segunda.
tip: A course of action adopted by a government or organization. Not 'politics'!

example: The president chose his cabinet.
examplePt: O presidente escolheu seu gabinete.
tip: The group of senior ministers advising a head of government.

example: The finance minister resigned.
examplePt: O ministro da fazenda renunciou.
tip: A senior government official heading a department.

example: Too much bureaucracy slows everything.
examplePt: Burocracia demais atrasa tudo.
tip: A system of complex administrative rules and procedures.

example: They imposed economic sanctions.
examplePt: Eles impuseram sanções econômicas.
tip: A penalty imposed on a country to force a change in behavior.

example: World leaders met at the summit.
examplePt: Líderes mundiais se reuniram na cúpula.
tip: A meeting between heads of state. Also means a mountain top!

example: A delegation arrived from Japan.
examplePt: Uma delegação chegou do Japão.
tip: A group of people representing a country or organization.

example: They formed a governing coalition.
examplePt: Eles formaram uma coalizão de governo.
tip: An alliance of parties or groups working together temporarily.

example: The opposition criticized the plan.
examplePt: A oposição criticou o plano.
tip: The political parties not in power.

example: The regime spread propaganda.
examplePt: O regime espalhou propaganda.
tip: Biased information used to promote a political cause.

example: Censorship limits free speech.
examplePt: A censura limita a liberdade de expressão.
tip: Suppressing information considered unacceptable by authorities.

example: They investigated corruption charges.
examplePt: Eles investigaram acusações de corrupção.
tip: Dishonest behavior by those in power, usually for personal gain.

example: Tax reform is urgently needed.
examplePt: A reforma tributária é urgente.
tip: Changing something to improve it, especially institutions or laws.

example: It's a federal law, not a state one.
examplePt: É uma lei federal, não estadual.
tip: Related to the central government of a union of states.

example: Municipal elections are next year.
examplePt: As eleições municipais são no ano que vem.
tip: Related to a city or town's local government.

example: Switzerland maintained neutrality.
examplePt: A Suíça manteve a neutralidade.
tip: Not supporting either side in a conflict.

example: The president used his veto power.
examplePt: O presidente usou seu poder de veto.
tip: The right to reject a decision or proposal.

example: The impeachment process began.
examplePt: O processo de impeachment começou.
tip: Formally charging a public official with misconduct to remove them.

example: The negotiation lasted all night.
examplePt: A negociação durou a noite toda.
tip: Formal discussion aimed at reaching an agreement.

example: English syntax differs from Portuguese.
examplePt: A sintaxe do inglês difere da do português.
tip: The rules for arranging words into sentences.

example: That's just semantics.
examplePt: Isso é só semântica.
tip: The study of meaning in language.

example: Phonetics helps with pronunciation.
examplePt: A fonética ajuda com a pronúncia.
tip: The study of speech sounds.

example: Her grammar is excellent.
examplePt: A gramática dela é excelente.
tip: The system of rules governing a language's structure.

example: Every region has its dialect.
examplePt: Cada região tem seu dialeto.
tip: A regional variety of a language with its own words and grammar.

example: She has a lovely accent.
examplePt: Ela tem um sotaque adorável.
tip: The way someone pronounces words, showing their origin.

example: 'Break a leg' is an idiom.
examplePt: 'Break a leg' é uma expressão idiomática.
tip: A phrase whose meaning can't be guessed from its individual words.

example: 'Time is money' is a metaphor.
examplePt: 'Tempo é dinheiro' é uma metáfora.
tip: Describing one thing as if it were another, without using 'like'.

example: 'Brave as a lion' is a simile.
examplePt: 'Corajoso como um leão' é um símile.
tip: A comparison using 'like' or 'as'. A metaphor doesn't use them.

example: The irony was not lost on us.
examplePt: A ironia não nos escapou.
tip: When the opposite of what's expected happens or is said.

example: His sarcasm was obvious.
examplePt: O sarcasmo dele era óbvio.
tip: Saying the opposite of what you mean, usually to mock.

example: The contract's ambiguity caused problems.
examplePt: A ambiguidade do contrato causou problemas.
tip: When something can be understood in more than one way.

example: You missed the nuance of his reply.
examplePt: Você perdeu a nuance da resposta dele.
tip: A subtle difference in meaning or tone.

example: That word has a negative connotation.
examplePt: Essa palavra tem uma conotação negativa.
tip: The feeling a word suggests, beyond its literal meaning.

example: 'Big' and 'large' are synonyms.
examplePt: 'Big' e 'large' são sinônimos.
tip: A word with the same or similar meaning as another.

example: 'Hot' is the antonym of 'cold'.
examplePt: 'Hot' é o antônimo de 'cold'.
tip: A word with the opposite meaning of another.

example: 'Un-' is a common prefix.
examplePt: 'Un-' é um prefixo comum.
tip: Letters added to the START of a word to change its meaning.

example: '-ly' is a suffix for adverbs.
examplePt: '-ly' é um sufixo de advérbios.
tip: Letters added to the END of a word to change its meaning.

example: Reading builds vocabulary.
examplePt: Ler constrói vocabulário.
tip: All the words a person knows or uses.

example: Fluency takes years of practice.
examplePt: A fluência leva anos de prática.
tip: Speaking a language smoothly and easily.

example: She is bilingual in English and Spanish.
examplePt: Ela é bilíngue em inglês e espanhol.
tip: Able to speak two languages fluently.

example: The translation lost some meaning.
examplePt: A tradução perdeu um pouco do sentido.
tip: Converting written text from one language to another.

example: Her interpretation was accurate.
examplePt: A interpretação dela foi precisa.
tip: Explaining meaning, or translating speech in real time.

example: Literacy rates are improving.
examplePt: As taxas de alfabetização estão melhorando.
tip: The ability to read and write.

example: His rhetoric convinced the crowd.
examplePt: A retórica dele convenceu a multidão.
tip: The art of persuasive speaking or writing.

example: She spoke with great eloquence.
examplePt: Ela falou com grande eloquência.
tip: Fluent, powerful, and persuasive expression.

example: That's a colloquial expression.
examplePt: Essa é uma expressão coloquial.
tip: Informal language used in everyday conversation.

example: Teenagers use a lot of slang.
examplePt: Adolescentes usam muita gíria.
tip: Very informal words, often specific to a group or generation.

example: Legal jargon is hard to understand.
examplePt: O jargão jurídico é difícil de entender.
tip: Specialized vocabulary used by a particular profession.

example: The etymology of that word is Latin.
examplePt: A etimologia dessa palavra é latina.
tip: The study of the origin and history of words.

example: The denotation is the dictionary meaning.
examplePt: A denotação é o significado do dicionário.
tip: The literal meaning of a word, unlike connotation.

example: He is very articulate.
examplePt: Ele se expressa muito bem.
tip: Able to express ideas clearly and effectively.

example: Can you paraphrase that sentence?
examplePt: Você pode parafrasear essa frase?
tip: To restate something using different words.

example: She defended her thesis last week.
examplePt: Ela defendeu sua tese na semana passada.
tip: A long research paper, or the central argument of an essay.

example: His dissertation took four years.
examplePt: A dissertação dele levou quatro anos.
tip: A long academic paper, usually for a doctoral degree.

example: The experiment tested the hypothesis.
examplePt: O experimento testou a hipótese.
tip: A proposed explanation that can be tested. Plural: 'hypotheses'.

example: Explain your methodology clearly.
examplePt: Explique sua metodologia com clareza.
tip: The system of methods used in a study or research.

example: The analysis revealed a pattern.
examplePt: A análise revelou um padrão.
tip: Detailed examination of something. Plural: 'analyses'.

example: The paper offers a synthesis of both theories.
examplePt: O artigo oferece uma síntese das duas teorias.
tip: Combining separate elements into a coherent whole.

example: Include a citation for every source.
examplePt: Inclua uma citação para cada fonte.
tip: A reference to a source used in your work.

example: The bibliography lists 50 books.
examplePt: A bibliografia lista 50 livros.
tip: The full list of sources at the end of academic work.

example: The article passed peer review.
examplePt: O artigo passou pela revisão por pares.
tip: Evaluation of research by other experts before publication.

example: Read the abstract first.
examplePt: Leia o resumo primeiro.
tip: A short summary at the start of an academic paper.

example: The argument rests on a false premise.
examplePt: O argumento se apoia em uma premissa falsa.
tip: A statement assumed true, used as the basis for an argument.

example: Her argument was very convincing.
examplePt: O argumento dela foi muito convincente.
tip: A set of reasons supporting an idea. Also means a disagreement!

example: The research took two years.
examplePt: A pesquisa levou dois anos.
tip: Systematic study to discover new facts. Usually uncountable.

example: She is a respected scholar.
examplePt: Ela é uma acadêmica respeitada.
tip: A person with deep knowledge in an academic field.

example: The lecture starts at 9 AM.
examplePt: A palestra começa às 9h.
tip: A formal talk given to teach an audience.

example: We discussed the topic in a seminar.
examplePt: Discutimos o tema em um seminário.
tip: A small class or meeting for discussion and study.

example: The curriculum changed this year.
examplePt: O currículo mudou este ano.
tip: The subjects taught in a course or school.

example: I take five classes this semester.
examplePt: Faço cinco disciplinas neste semestre.
tip: Half of an academic year.

example: She is an undergraduate student.
examplePt: Ela é uma aluna de graduação.
tip: A student working toward a first university degree.

example: He earned a doctorate in physics.
examplePt: Ele obteve um doutorado em física.
tip: The highest university degree, giving the title 'Doctor'.

example: The faculty voted on the proposal.
examplePt: O corpo docente votou a proposta.
tip: All the teaching staff of a university.

example: Biology is a scientific discipline.
examplePt: Biologia é uma disciplina científica.
tip: A branch of knowledge. Also means self-control!

example: We need a theoretical framework.
examplePt: Precisamos de uma estrutura teórica.
tip: A basic structure of ideas supporting an approach.

example: This discovery shifted the paradigm.
examplePt: Essa descoberta mudou o paradigma.
tip: A typical model or pattern of thinking in a field. The 'g' is silent!

example: We need empirical evidence.
examplePt: Precisamos de evidência empírica.
tip: Based on observation and experiment, not just theory.

example: It's a theoretical problem.
examplePt: É um problema teórico.
tip: Based on ideas rather than practical experience.

example: Try to stay objective.
examplePt: Tente permanecer objetivo.
tip: Based on facts, not personal feelings. Also means 'a goal'.

example: Beauty is subjective.
examplePt: Beleza é subjetiva.
tip: Based on personal opinion rather than facts.

example: She wrote a critique of the theory.
examplePt: Ela escreveu uma crítica da teoria.
tip: A detailed analysis and assessment, not just negative criticism.

example: Plagiarism is a serious offense.
examplePt: Plágio é uma ofensa grave.
tip: Using someone else's work without giving credit.

example: He received a full scholarship.
examplePt: Ele recebeu uma bolsa integral.
tip: Financial support given to a student. Also means academic study.

example: The dean signed the certificate.
examplePt: O reitor assinou o certificado.
tip: The head of a university faculty or college.

example: Good evening, everyone!
examplePt: Boa noite a todos!
tip: Used as a greeting when arriving in the evening — 'Good night' is only for saying goodbye.

example: Nice to see you again!
examplePt: Bom te ver de novo!
tip: Different from 'Nice to meet you' — this one is for someone you already know.

example: Hey! How's it going?
examplePt: E aí! Como vai?
tip: A casual way to ask 'How are you?' among friends.

example: Hi! What's new with you?
examplePt: Oi! O que há de novo com você?
tip: A friendly opener when you haven't talked to someone in a while.

pt: Tenha um bom fim de semana
example: See you Monday! Have a good weekend.
examplePt: Te vejo segunda! Tenha um bom fim de semana.
tip: Common thing to say to coworkers on a Friday afternoon.

example: Have a good trip! Send me photos.
examplePt: Tenha uma boa viagem! Me manda fotos.
tip: Said to someone who is about to travel.

example: Cheers! To our friendship.
examplePt: Saúde! À nossa amizade.
tip: Used both as a toast with drinks and, in British English, as an informal 'thanks'.

example: Well done on your exam!
examplePt: Muito bem na sua prova!
tip: Praise for something someone just finished or achieved.

example: Good job on the presentation.
examplePt: Bom trabalho na apresentação.
tip: Very common encouragement, used with kids and adults alike.

example: No worries, take your time.
examplePt: Sem problemas, fique à vontade.
tip: A relaxed way to say 'it's okay' or 'you're welcome', very common in Australia.

example: Take your time, there's no rush.
examplePt: Sem pressa, não tem pressa nenhuma.
tip: Reassures someone that they don't need to hurry.

example: Have a nice day! — Same to you!
examplePt: Tenha um bom dia! — Igualmente!
tip: The standard reply when someone wishes you something nice first.

pt: A gente se vê por aí
example: See you around, take care!
examplePt: A gente se vê por aí, se cuida!
tip: A casual farewell when you're not sure exactly when you'll meet again.

example: Gotta go, catch you later!
examplePt: Preciso ir, te pego depois!
tip: Very informal goodbye, typical among young people.

example: Long time no see! How have you been?
examplePt: Quanto tempo! Como você tem passado?
tip: Said when you run into someone you haven't seen in a long while.

example: Welcome back! We missed you.
examplePt: Bem-vindo(a) de volta! Sentimos sua falta.
tip: Said to someone returning from a trip, vacation, or absence.

example: Thanks for the help! — My pleasure.
examplePt: Obrigado pela ajuda! — O prazer é meu.
tip: A warmer alternative to 'You're welcome'.

example: It's a pleasure to finally meet you.
examplePt: É um prazer finalmente te conhecer.
tip: A slightly formal way to greet someone you're happy to meet.

example: Come in, make yourself at home.
examplePt: Entre, fique à vontade.
tip: What a host says to welcome a guest into their house.

example: Best wishes on your new job!
examplePt: Votos de sucesso no seu novo emprego!
tip: A warm closing line for cards, emails, and farewells.

example: I heard you're sick — get well soon!
examplePt: Soube que você está doente — melhoras!
tip: Said to someone who is ill, wishing them a fast recovery.

example: Happy birthday! Have an amazing day.
examplePt: Feliz aniversário! Tenha um dia incrível.
tip: The classic birthday greeting — 'Happy' is used for most celebrations in English.

example: She is thirteen years old.
examplePt: Ela tem treze anos.
tip: The first of the 'teen' numbers with an irregular start — notice it isn't 'threeteen'.

example: There are fourteen students here.
examplePt: Há catorze alunos aqui.
tip: Note the spelling keeps the 'u' from 'four', unlike 'forty'.

example: I'll be back in fifteen minutes.
examplePt: Eu volto em quinze minutos.
tip: Half of thirty — a very common amount of time to mention.

example: He turns sixteen next month.
examplePt: Ele faz dezesseis anos mês que vem.
tip: In many countries, this is the age to start driving.

example: The store closes at seventeen hours.
examplePt: A loja fecha às dezessete horas.
tip: In the 24-hour clock, this is 5 PM.

example: You need to be eighteen to vote here.
examplePt: Você precisa ter dezoito anos para votar aqui.
tip: The age of legal adulthood in most countries.

example: The film is set in nineteen forty-five.
examplePt: O filme se passa em mil novecentos e quarenta e cinco.
tip: The last of the 'teen' numbers before twenty.

example: My uncle just turned forty.
examplePt: Meu tio acabou de fazer quarenta anos.
tip: Watch the spelling — it drops the 'u' that 'four' has.

example: There are sixty seconds in a minute.
examplePt: Há sessenta segundos em um minuto.
tip: How many minutes are in one hour, too.

example: My grandfather is seventy years old.
examplePt: Meu avô tem setenta anos.
tip: Comes right after sixty in the counting sequence.

example: The speed limit is eighty km/h.
examplePt: O limite de velocidade é oitenta km/h.
tip: Often seen on road signs and speedometers.

example: The song is from the nineties.
examplePt: A música é dos anos noventa.
tip: 'The nineties' refers to the 1990s decade.

example: This is my first time here.
examplePt: Esta é minha primeira vez aqui.
tip: The first ordinal number — irregular, it doesn't end in '-th' like most others.

example: She finished in second place.
examplePt: Ela terminou em segundo lugar.
tip: Also means the unit of time — context tells them apart.

example: Turn left at the third light.
examplePt: Vire à esquerda no terceiro sinal.
tip: The last of the three irregular ordinals — after this, they all end in '-th'.

example: I only ate half of the sandwich.
examplePt: Eu só comi metade do sanduíche.
tip: Used in time too: 'half past three' means 3:30.

example: Can I have a dozen eggs?
examplePt: Posso levar uma dúzia de ovos?
tip: Always means exactly twelve, most often used for eggs.

example: The city has two million people.
examplePt: A cidade tem dois milhões de pessoas.
tip: A thousand thousands — commonly used to describe large populations or amounts of money.

example: The company is worth a billion dollars.
examplePt: A empresa vale um bilhão de dólares.
tip: A thousand million — in older British English it used to mean something different, but today it matches the American value everywhere.

example: She wore a maroon dress.
examplePt: Ela usava um vestido bordô.
tip: A dark brownish-red, named after a French word for 'chestnut'.

example: He always wears a navy suit.
examplePt: Ele sempre usa um terno azul-marinho.
tip: Named after the dark blue uniforms of naval officers.

example: The jacket is olive green.
examplePt: A jaqueta é verde-oliva.
tip: Named after the color of unripe olives — common in military clothing.

example: The walls are painted lime green.
examplePt: As paredes estão pintadas de verde-limão.
tip: A bright, yellowish green, named after the citrus fruit.

example: Her nails are painted coral.
examplePt: As unhas dela estão pintadas de coral.
tip: A pinkish-orange named after the sea creature of the same name.

example: I love this teal sofa.
examplePt: Eu adoro esse sofá azul-petróleo.
tip: A mix of blue and green, named after the color around a teal duck's eye.

example: The walls are painted ivory.
examplePt: As paredes estão pintadas de marfim.
tip: A soft off-white, named after the material from elephant tusks.

example: She bought a mint green bag.
examplePt: Ela comprou uma bolsa verde-menta.
tip: A pale, cool green named after the fresh mint leaf.

example: They painted the nursery rose gold.
examplePt: Eles pintaram o quarto do bebê de rosé.
tip: A soft pink named after the flower — also a popular metal finish.

example: The traffic light turned amber.
examplePt: O semáforo ficou âmbar.
tip: A warm orange-yellow, named after the fossilized tree resin.

example: He wore a charcoal gray suit.
examplePt: Ele usava um terno cinza-chumbo.
tip: A very dark gray, named after burnt wood used for drawing and grilling.

example: Khaki pants are a wardrobe classic.
examplePt: Calças cáqui são um clássico do guarda-roupa.
tip: A dusty tan color, originally used for military uniforms in hot climates.

example: The curtains are a deep crimson.
examplePt: As cortinas são de um carmesim profundo.
tip: A rich, deep red — often used to describe blood or autumn leaves.

example: Indigo sits between blue and violet.
examplePt: O anil fica entre o azul e o violeta.
tip: One of the seven colors of the rainbow, between blue and violet.

example: The flowers are a bright magenta.
examplePt: As flores são de um magenta vibrante.
tip: A vivid pinkish-purple, one of the four inks used in color printing.

example: The bedroom walls are lavender.
examplePt: As paredes do quarto são lilás.
tip: A pale purple named after the fragrant lavender flower.

example: The sunset painted the sky golden.
examplePt: O pôr do sol pintou o céu de dourado.
tip: The adjective form of 'gold' — used for color, not the metal itself.

example: The giraffe has a very long neck.
examplePt: A girafa tem um pescoço muito longo.
tip: The tallest land animal in the world, and its tongue can be nearly 50 cm long.

example: Every zebra has a unique pattern of stripes.
examplePt: Cada zebra tem um padrão único de listras.
tip: No two zebras have exactly the same stripe pattern — like a fingerprint.

example: Kangaroos carry their babies in a pouch.
examplePt: Cangurus carregam seus filhotes em uma bolsa.
tip: It can't walk backward, and it uses its powerful tail for balance while jumping.

example: The panda eats bamboo all day.
examplePt: O panda come bambu o dia todo.
tip: It spends up to 12 hours a day eating, mostly bamboo.

example: The koala sleeps most of the day.
examplePt: O coala dorme a maior parte do dia.
tip: It sleeps up to 20 hours a day, largely because eucalyptus leaves give it very little energy.

example: The camel can survive without water for days.
examplePt: O camelo pode sobreviver sem água por dias.
tip: Its hump stores fat, not water, which it converts into energy and moisture.

example: The hippopotamus spends most of its day in water.
examplePt: O hipopótamo passa a maior parte do dia na água.
tip: Despite its size, it can outrun a human on land over short distances.

example: The rhinoceros has thick, tough skin.
examplePt: O rinoceronte tem uma pele grossa e resistente.
tip: Its horn is made of keratin — the same protein found in human hair and nails.

example: The crocodile waited silently in the water.
examplePt: O crocodilo esperou silenciosamente na água.
tip: It has one of the strongest bite forces of any living animal.

example: An alligator has a wider snout than a crocodile.
examplePt: O jacaré tem o focinho mais largo que o crocodilo.
tip: The easiest way to tell it apart from a crocodile is its rounder, U-shaped snout.

example: Dolphins are known for their intelligence.
examplePt: Golfinhos são conhecidos por sua inteligência.
tip: It sleeps with only half its brain at a time, so it can keep breathing.

example: The blue whale is the largest animal on Earth.
examplePt: A baleia-azul é o maior animal da Terra.
tip: Its heart alone can weigh as much as a small car.

example: An octopus has eight arms.
examplePt: Um polvo tem oito braços.
tip: It has three hearts and blue blood, and can change color in an instant.

example: The squid shoots ink to escape predators.
examplePt: A lula solta tinta para escapar de predadores.
tip: Some deep-sea species can grow over 12 meters long.

example: The crab walks sideways.
examplePt: O caranguejo anda de lado.
tip: Its sideways walk comes from how its legs bend — it's actually its fastest direction.

example: Lobster turns red only after it's cooked.
examplePt: A lagosta só fica vermelha depois de cozida.
tip: It's actually a dark blue-green while alive; the red color appears when it's cooked.

example: Some jellyfish can sting even after they're dead.
examplePt: Algumas águas-vivas podem picar mesmo depois de mortas.
tip: It has no brain, no heart, and is made of about 95% water.

example: The seal swam gracefully near the shore.
examplePt: A foca nadou graciosamente perto da costa.
tip: It can hold its breath underwater for up to two hours.

example: Penguins can't fly, but they swim very well.
examplePt: Pinguins não voam, mas nadam muito bem.
tip: It can't fly in the air, but it 'flies' underwater using its wings as flippers.

example: The flamingo is famous for its pink feathers.
examplePt: O flamingo é famoso por suas penas rosas.
tip: Its pink color actually comes from the shrimp and algae it eats.

example: The peacock spread its colorful tail.
examplePt: O pavão abriu sua cauda colorida.
tip: Only the males have the famous colorful tail, used to attract females.

example: The parrot can repeat words it hears.
examplePt: O papagaio consegue repetir palavras que ouve.
tip: Some species can live over 60 years and learn hundreds of words.

example: The eagle spotted its prey from far away.
examplePt: A águia avistou sua presa de longe.
tip: Its eyesight is about 4 to 8 times sharper than a human's.

example: A hawk circled above the field.
examplePt: Um falcão sobrevoava o campo em círculos.
tip: It can dive at incredible speeds while hunting small animals.

example: The falcon is the fastest animal on Earth.
examplePt: O falcão é o animal mais rápido da Terra.
tip: In a hunting dive, it can reach speeds over 300 km/h.

example: The squirrel buried nuts for the winter.
examplePt: O esquilo enterrou nozes para o inverno.
tip: It forgets where it buried many of its nuts — which accidentally plants new trees.

example: The hedgehog curled into a ball.
examplePt: O ouriço se enrolou em uma bola.
tip: It has around 5,000 spines and curls into a ball to protect itself.

example: A raccoon rummaged through the trash at night.
examplePt: Um guaxinim vasculhou o lixo à noite.
tip: It's famous for washing its food before eating, whenever water is nearby.

examplePt: Não chegue perto — um gambá pode te borrifar!
tip: It can spray its awful-smelling defense up to 3 meters away.

examplePt: O castor construiu uma represa no rio.
tip: Its front teeth never stop growing, so it must gnaw on wood constantly.

example: Otters hold hands while sleeping so they don't drift apart.
examplePt: Lontras dão as mãos enquanto dormem para não se afastarem.
tip: It often floats on its back and uses a rock to crack open shellfish.

example: The donkey carried heavy bags up the hill.
examplePt: O burro carregou sacos pesados morro acima.
tip: Despite its reputation, it's actually very intelligent and cautious, not stubborn without reason.

example: I bought a bunch of grapes.
examplePt: Eu comprei um cacho de uvas.
tip: Grapes are used to make both juice and wine.

example: She likes strawberry ice cream.
examplePt: Ela gosta de sorvete de morango.
tip: Technically, it's not a true berry — its seeds sit on the outside, unlike most berries.

example: Watermelon is perfect for hot days.
examplePt: Melancia é perfeita para dias quentes.
tip: It's about 92% water, which is where its name comes from.

example: Add a squeeze of lemon to your tea.
examplePt: Adicione um pouco de limão no seu chá.
tip: In Brazil, 'lemon' and 'lime' are often both called 'limão' — but in English they're different fruits.

example: The pear was sweet and juicy.
examplePt: A pera estava doce e suculenta.
tip: Sounds exactly like 'pair' (a set of two) — context tells them apart.

example: Mango is one of the most popular fruits in the world.
examplePt: A manga é uma das frutas mais populares do mundo.
tip: It's sometimes called the 'king of fruits' in South Asia.

example: Pineapple pizza is controversial!
examplePt: Pizza de abacaxi é polêmica!
tip: It takes about two years to grow a single pineapple.

example: We had melon for dessert.
examplePt: Comemos melão de sobremesa.
tip: A broad term that includes watermelon, cantaloupe, and honeydew.

example: There's a cherry on top of the cake.
examplePt: Tem uma cereja em cima do bolo.
tip: 'The cherry on top' is an idiom for the perfect finishing touch.

example: Coconut water is very refreshing.
examplePt: Água de coco é muito refrescante.
tip: Botanically, it's classified as a fruit, a nut, and a seed all at once.

example: I love avocado on toast.
examplePt: Eu adoro abacate na torrada.
tip: It's technically a large berry with a single seed.

example: Rabbits love eating carrots.
examplePt: Coelhos adoram comer cenouras.
tip: Wild carrots were originally purple or white — orange ones were bred later.

example: Add some lettuce to the sandwich.
examplePt: Adicione um pouco de alface no sanduíche.
tip: The base of most salads, and about 95% water.

example: The cucumber salad is very light.
examplePt: A salada de pepino é bem leve.
tip: 'Cool as a cucumber' is an idiom meaning very calm under pressure.

example: Add a bit of pepper to the soup.
examplePt: Adicione um pouco de pimenta na sopa.
tip: Can mean both the spice (ground pepper) and the vegetable (bell pepper).

example: This pizza has mushrooms on it.
examplePt: Essa pizza tem cogumelos.
tip: Technically a fungus, not a plant.

example: We grilled corn for the barbecue.
examplePt: Nós grelhamos milho para o churrasco.
tip: In American English, this is often called 'corn'; in British English, 'maize'.

example: I'm cooking pasta for dinner.
examplePt: Estou cozinhando massa para o jantar.
tip: An Italian word that became international, covering hundreds of different shapes.

example: We ordered noodles at the restaurant.
examplePt: Pedimos macarrão no restaurante.
tip: Usually refers to long, thin Asian-style pasta, unlike Italian 'pasta'.

example: We had sausage and eggs for breakfast.
examplePt: Comemos salsicha e ovos no café da manhã.
tip: One of the oldest processed foods, dating back thousands of years.

example: The smell of bacon woke me up.
examplePt: O cheiro de bacon me acordou.
tip: Made from cured pork, and one of the most recognizable smells in cooking.

example: I have yogurt with fruit every morning.
examplePt: Eu como iogurte com frutas toda manhã.
tip: The word comes from Turkish, and the food dates back thousands of years.

example: We made pancakes for Sunday breakfast.
examplePt: Fizemos panquecas no café da manhã de domingo.
tip: 'As flat as a pancake' is a common idiom for something completely flat.

example: He drinks an espresso every morning.
examplePt: Ele toma um expresso toda manhã.
tip: A strong, concentrated coffee shot — the base for cappuccino and latte.

example: I'll have a cappuccino, please.
examplePt: Eu quero um capuccino, por favor.
tip: Named after Capuchin friars, whose brown robes resembled the drink's color.

example: She ordered a chocolate milkshake.
examplePt: Ela pediu um milkshake de chocolate.
tip: A blend of milk, ice cream, and flavoring, shaken or blended together.

example: The bartender made a fruity cocktail.
examplePt: O barman fez um coquetel frutado.
tip: A mixed alcoholic drink, usually combining spirits with juice or soda.

example: They opened champagne to celebrate.
examplePt: Eles abriram champanhe para comemorar.
tip: Only sparkling wine from the Champagne region of France can legally use this name.

example: He prefers whiskey with ice.
examplePt: Ele prefere uísque com gelo.
tip: Spelled 'whiskey' in the US and Ireland, but 'whisky' in Scotland and Canada.

example: The cocktail is made with rum and lime.
examplePt: O coquetel é feito com rum e limão.
tip: Made from sugarcane, and historically linked to pirates and the Caribbean.

example: Vodka is usually served very cold.
examplePt: Vodca costuma ser servida bem gelada.
tip: Its name comes from a Slavic word meaning 'little water'.

example: We drank apple cider at the fair.
examplePt: Bebemos sidra de maçã na feira.
tip: Made from fermented apples — popular in the UK and parts of the US.

example: Herbal tea helps me relax before bed.
examplePt: Chá de ervas me ajuda a relaxar antes de dormir.
tip: Unlike regular tea, it usually contains no caffeine at all.

example: Iced tea is perfect for summer.
examplePt: Chá gelado é perfeito para o verão.
tip: Extremely popular in the southern United States, often served pre-sweetened.

example: He drank an energy drink before the exam.
examplePt: Ele tomou uma bebida energética antes da prova.
tip: Usually contains caffeine and sugar to give a quick boost of alertness.

example: My parents live nearby.
examplePt: Meus pais moram perto.
tip: Always plural — refers to mother and father together.

example: Do you have any siblings?
examplePt: Você tem irmãos?
tip: A gender-neutral word covering both brothers and sisters.

example: Her grandson visits every weekend.
examplePt: O neto dela visita todo fim de semana.
tip: The male form — 'granddaughter' is the female equivalent.

example: His granddaughter just turned five.
examplePt: A neta dele acabou de fazer cinco anos.
tip: The female counterpart of 'grandson'.

example: My uncle is my godfather.
examplePt: Meu tio é meu padrinho.
tip: A spiritual or symbolic guardian, often chosen at a baptism.

example: My godmother gave me this necklace.
examplePt: Minha madrinha me deu esse colar.
tip: The female equivalent of a godfather.

example: He treats his godson like his own child.
examplePt: Ele trata o afilhado como filho próprio.
tip: The child a godparent takes spiritual responsibility for.

example: My goddaughter is getting married next year.
examplePt: Minha afilhada vai se casar ano que vem.
tip: The female form of 'godson'.

example: We're having dinner with the in-laws.
examplePt: Vamos jantar com os parentes por casamento.
tip: A general term for relatives gained through marriage — attach it to any family word.

example: My mother-in-law is visiting this weekend.
examplePt: Minha sogra vai visitar neste fim de semana.
tip: Your spouse's mother.

example: I get along well with my father-in-law.
examplePt: Eu me dou bem com meu sogro.
tip: Your spouse's father.

example: My brother-in-law works as an engineer.
examplePt: Meu cunhado trabalha como engenheiro.
tip: Can mean your spouse's brother, or your sibling's husband.

example: My sister-in-law is coming to the party.
examplePt: Minha cunhada vai à festa.
tip: Can mean your spouse's sister, or your sibling's wife.

example: This is my fiancé, David.
examplePt: Este é meu noivo, David.
tip: Borrowed from French — this spelling (one 'e') refers to a man.

example: He introduced his fiancée to the family.
examplePt: Ele apresentou a noiva para a família.
tip: The female form — spelled with a double 'e' in French tradition.

example: She has been a widow for two years.
examplePt: Ela é viúva há dois anos.
tip: A woman whose spouse has passed away.

example: He became a widower last year.
examplePt: Ele ficou viúvo no ano passado.
tip: The male equivalent of 'widow'.

example: Her ancestors came from Portugal.
examplePt: Os ancestrais dela vieram de Portugal.
tip: Someone from whom a person is descended, usually further back than grandparents.

example: He is a descendant of the town's founder.
examplePt: Ele é descendente do fundador da cidade.
tip: The opposite of 'ancestor' — someone who comes after, in the family line.

example: Her aunt became her legal guardian.
examplePt: A tia dela se tornou sua tutora legal.
tip: A person legally responsible for a child who isn't their biological parent.

example: They have two adopted children.
examplePt: Eles têm dois filhos adotados.
tip: Describes a child who was legally made part of a family they weren't born into.

example: The newborn slept through the whole party.
examplePt: O recém-nascido dormiu a festa inteira.
tip: Used for a baby in its very first days or weeks of life.

example: They live in a small apartment.
examplePt: Eles moram em um apartamento pequeno.
tip: In British English, it's more commonly called a 'flat'.

example: We keep old boxes in the basement.
examplePt: Guardamos caixas velhas no porão.
tip: The floor below ground level in a house.

example: The old photos are stored in the attic.
examplePt: As fotos antigas estão guardadas no sótão.
tip: The space right under the roof, opposite of the basement.

example: He parked the car in the garage.
examplePt: Ele estacionou o carro na garagem.
tip: Also used as a verb in 'to garage a car', meaning to store it there.

example: The bedrooms are down the hallway.
examplePt: Os quartos ficam no fim do corredor.
tip: The narrow passage that connects rooms inside a house.

example: She hung her coat in the closet.
examplePt: Ela pendurou o casaco no armário.
tip: In American English, this is the standard word — British English says 'wardrobe'.

example: Close the curtains, it's too bright.
examplePt: Feche as cortinas, está muito claro.
tip: Used to block light or add privacy to a window.

example: The living room has a soft carpet.
examplePt: A sala tem um carpete macio.
tip: Wall-to-wall floor covering — a smaller version is called a 'rug'.

example: I need a new pillow, mine is too flat.
examplePt: Preciso de um travesseiro novo, o meu está muito baixo.
tip: What you rest your head on — a 'cushion' is the similar object used on a sofa.

example: She pulled the blanket over her shoulders.
examplePt: Ela puxou o cobertor sobre os ombros.
tip: Used to keep warm — a thinner version is called a 'sheet'.

example: We bought a new mattress last week.
examplePt: Compramos um colchão novo semana passada.
tip: The padded part of the bed you actually lie on.

example: The faucet is leaking again.
examplePt: A torneira está vazando de novo.
tip: American English word — British English uses 'tap' instead.

example: Please wash the dishes in the sink.
examplePt: Por favor, lave a louça na pia.
tip: Also a verb meaning to go down into water — like 'the ship began to sink'.

example: The cake is baking in the oven.
examplePt: O bolo está assando no forno.
tip: Used for baking, unlike the 'stove', which is used for cooking on top.

example: She left the soup on the stove.
examplePt: Ela deixou a sopa no fogão.
tip: In British English, this is usually called the 'hob' or 'cooker'.

example: Just heat it in the microwave for a minute.
examplePt: É só esquentar no micro-ondas por um minuto.
tip: Short for 'microwave oven' — invented accidentally by a radar engineer in 1945.

example: Just put the plates in the dishwasher.
examplePt: É só colocar os pratos no lava-louças.
tip: A compound word: 'dish' + 'washer' — exactly what it sounds like.

example: She put the roses in a glass vase.
examplePt: Ela colocou as rosas em um vaso de vidro.
tip: Used for flowers — a plant pot for soil is a different word: 'flowerpot'.

example: Someone just rang the doorbell.
examplePt: Alguém acabou de tocar a campainha.
tip: A compound word joining 'door' and 'bell'.

example: Check the mailbox for new letters.
examplePt: Confira a caixa de correio se chegou carta.
tip: In British English, this is usually called a 'letterbox'.

example: Smoke rose from the chimney.
examplePt: Fumaça saía da chaminé.
tip: Famous in stories as the way Santa Claus enters houses.

example: They sat on the porch and watched the sunset.
examplePt: Eles ficaram sentados na varanda observando o pôr do sol.
tip: A covered entrance area, typical of American houses.

example: The car is parked in the driveway.
examplePt: O carro está estacionado na entrada da garagem.
tip: The private road that connects a house's garage to the street.
