example: There's a small rug by the front door.
examplePt: Tem um tapete pequeno perto da porta da frente.
tip: A smaller, movable version of a carpet.

example: They bought new furniture for the living room.
examplePt: Eles compraram móveis novos para a sala.
tip: An uncountable noun in English — you never say 'a furniture' or 'furnitures'.

example: Use the pliers to bend the wire.
examplePt: Use o alicate para dobrar o fio.
tip: Always used in the plural form, like 'scissors'.

example: The sculptor used a chisel on the stone.
examplePt: O escultor usou um formão na pedra.
tip: A tool used to carve or shape wood, stone, or metal.

example: Smooth the surface with sandpaper.
examplePt: Alise a superfície com lixa.
tip: Comes in different grits, from rough to very fine.

example: He used a tape measure to check the wall.
examplePt: Ele usou uma trena para medir a parede.
tip: A flexible ruler that rolls up into a small case.

example: Duct tape can fix almost anything temporarily.
examplePt: Fita adesiva forte pode consertar quase tudo temporariamente.
tip: Originally developed to seal ammunition boxes during World War II.

example: Use glue to stick the pieces together.
examplePt: Use cola para colar as peças.
tip: One of the shortest common English words — just three letters.

example: Clean the paintbrush after use.
examplePt: Limpe o pincel depois de usar.
tip: A compound word combining 'paint' and 'brush'.

example: He pushed the wheelbarrow full of dirt.
examplePt: Ele empurrou o carrinho de mão cheio de terra.
tip: A one-wheeled cart used to carry heavy loads by hand.

example: All the tools are in the toolbox.
examplePt: Todas as ferramentas estão na caixa de ferramentas.
tip: A simple compound word — 'tool' plus 'box'.

example: Tighten the bolt with a wrench.
examplePt: Aperte o parafuso com uma chave inglesa.
tip: Usually paired with a nut, unlike a 'screw', which threads directly into material.

example: This shelf needs one more screw.
examplePt: Esta prateleira precisa de mais um parafuso.
tip: Tightened with a screwdriver, which is named after it.

example: He pried the door open with a crowbar.
examplePt: Ele forçou a porta com um pé de cabra.
tip: A metal bar used to pry things apart, named for its curved, bird-foot-like end.

example: Use a mallet, not a hammer, on that surface.
examplePt: Use uma marreta, não um martelo, nessa superfície.
tip: Softer than a hammer, so it won't damage delicate surfaces.

example: The clamp holds the wood in place while it dries.
examplePt: O grampo segura a madeira no lugar enquanto seca.
tip: Used to hold two pieces together firmly while gluing or cutting.

example: Hang your coat on the hook.
examplePt: Pendure seu casaco no gancho.
tip: Also used as a verb, meaning to catch or attach something.

example: Soccer is the most popular sport in Brazil.
examplePt: O futebol é o esporte mais popular no Brasil.
tip: American English says 'soccer'; almost everywhere else in English it's called 'football'.

example: He plays basketball every weekend.
examplePt: Ele joga basquete todo fim de semana.
tip: Invented in 1891 by a Canadian teacher using a soccer ball and peach baskets.

example: They played tennis at the club.
examplePt: Eles jogaram tênis no clube.
tip: Note the difference: 'tennis' is the sport, but 'tennis shoes' are the sneakers.

example: Brazil has a strong volleyball team.
examplePt: O Brasil tem uma seleção forte de vôlei.
tip: A compound word: you 'volley' the ball back and forth over the net.

example: He trains boxing three times a week.
examplePt: Ele treina boxe três vezes por semana.
tip: One of the oldest combat sports, dating back to ancient civilizations.

example: Cycling is great exercise for the legs.
examplePt: Ciclismo é um ótimo exercício para as pernas.
tip: Comes from 'cycle', referring to the wheels of the bicycle.

example: She finished her first marathon last year.
examplePt: Ela terminou sua primeira maratona ano passado.
tip: Named after the Greek battle where a messenger supposedly ran about 40 km to deliver news.

example: The referee blew the whistle.
examplePt: O árbitro apitou.
tip: The official who enforces the rules during a match.

example: The stadium was completely full.
examplePt: O estádio estava completamente lotado.
tip: The word comes from an ancient Greek unit of distance used for footraces.

example: The team lifted the trophy after winning.
examplePt: O time ergueu o troféu após vencer.
tip: Awarded to the winner as a symbol of victory.

example: The detective examined the crime scene.
examplePt: O detetive examinou a cena do crime.
tip: Comes from 'detect' — someone whose job is to discover the truth.

example: The police questioned the main suspect.
examplePt: A polícia interrogou o principal suspeito.
tip: As a verb, the stress moves: 'to suspéct' someone.

example: The detective couldn't find a clear motive.
examplePt: O detetive não conseguiu achar um motivo claro.
tip: The reason behind a crime — every good mystery hides one.

example: The bank robbery was caught on camera.
examplePt: O roubo ao banco foi flagrado pela câmera.
tip: Involves force or threat — theft without confrontation is just called 'stealing'.

example: The movie is about a kidnapping case.
examplePt: O filme é sobre um caso de sequestro.
tip: Literally 'kid' (child) + 'nap' (an old word for stealing).

example: The interrogation lasted for hours.
examplePt: O interrogatório durou horas.
tip: Formal questioning meant to get information from a suspect.

example: The officer put handcuffs on the thief.
examplePt: O policial colocou algemas no ladrão.
tip: Always used in the plural, like 'scissors' or 'pants'.

example: He finally made a full confession.
examplePt: Ele finalmente fez uma confissão completa.
tip: When a suspect admits guilt, either to police or in court.

example: Forensics found DNA at the scene.
examplePt: A perícia forense encontrou DNA na cena.
tip: The scientific side of crime investigation — think fingerprints and lab tests.

example: Police sealed off the crime scene.
examplePt: A polícia isolou a cena do crime.
tip: The exact location where a crime happened, usually taped off for investigation.

example: The painter stretched a new canvas.
examplePt: O pintor esticou uma tela nova.
tip: The fabric surface artists paint on — originally made of hemp or cotton.

example: She cleaned her brush after painting.
examplePt: Ela limpou o pincel depois de pintar.
tip: Can also mean a quick, light touch, as in 'a brush with fame'.

example: The gallery is showing modern art this month.
examplePt: A galeria está exibindo arte moderna este mês.
tip: A space to display art — smaller and more commercial than a 'museum'.

example: We visited a photography exhibition.
examplePt: Visitamos uma exposição de fotografia.
tip: British English keeps this spelling; American English often shortens it to 'exhibit'.

example: The artist painted her portrait.
examplePt: O artista pintou o retrato dela.
tip: A painting or photo focused on a person's face — the opposite framing is 'landscape'.

example: He specializes in landscape painting.
examplePt: Ele é especialista em pintura de paisagem.
tip: Also the name for the wide, horizontal orientation of a page or photo.

example: The Mona Lisa is considered a masterpiece.
examplePt: A Mona Lisa é considerada uma obra-prima.
tip: Originally the piece a craftsman made to prove they'd become a master.

example: She just published her first novel.
examplePt: Ela acabou de publicar seu primeiro romance.
tip: A long fictional story — as an adjective, 'novel' also means 'new and original'.

example: Shakespeare is history's most famous playwright.
examplePt: Shakespeare é o dramaturgo mais famoso da história.
tip: Someone who writes plays — the '-wright' part means 'maker', as in 'shipwright'.

example: The choreography of the ballet was stunning.
examplePt: A coreografia do balé foi impressionante.
tip: The art of designing dance movements and sequences.

example: The whole ensemble took a bow.
examplePt: Todo o elenco fez uma reverência.
tip: Borrowed from French, meaning 'together' — used for a group of performers or musicians.

example: She has practiced ballet since she was five.
examplePt: Ela pratica balé desde os cinco anos.
tip: The 't' at the end is silent, since the word comes from French.

example: The artist painted a huge mural downtown.
examplePt: O artista pintou um mural enorme no centro.
tip: A large painting made directly on a wall, often in public spaces.

example: The painter mixed colors on her palette.
examplePt: A pintora misturou as cores na paleta.
tip: Can mean the physical board for mixing paint, or simply a range of colors used.

example: The principal gave a speech at graduation.
examplePt: O diretor fez um discurso na formatura.
tip: In British English, this role is usually called 'headmaster' or 'headteacher'.

example: The kids ran to the playground.
examplePt: As crianças correram para o pátio de recreio.
tip: A compound word — literally 'play' + 'ground'.

example: We eat lunch in the school cafeteria.
examplePt: Almoçamos na cantina da escola.
tip: Comes from Spanish, but is now standard in American school vocabulary.

example: She keeps her books in her locker.
examplePt: Ela guarda os livros no armário escolar.
tip: A small locked storage space, very common in American schools.

example: Check your class schedule for today.
examplePt: Confira sua grade horária de hoje.
tip: American English pronounces it 'SKE-jool'; British English says 'SHE-dyool'.

example: Math is my favorite subject.
examplePt: Matemática é minha matéria favorita.
tip: As a verb (subJECT), the stress shifts to the second syllable.

example: I finished my assignment last night.
examplePt: Terminei minha tarefa ontem à noite.
tip: A broader word than 'homework' — can include projects and long-term work.

example: We have a quiz tomorrow.
examplePt: Temos um teste rápido amanhã.
tip: Shorter and less formal than a full 'test' or 'exam'.

example: She received her diploma with honors.
examplePt: Ela recebeu seu diploma com honras.
tip: The official document proving you completed a course of study.

example: Graduation day was very emotional.
examplePt: O dia da formatura foi muito emocionante.
tip: Comes from 'grade' — originally referred to moving up a step or degree.

example: My report card had all good grades.
examplePt: Meu boletim teve todas notas boas.
tip: The document that reports a student's grades to their parents.

example: The teacher wrote the date in chalk.
examplePt: O professor escreveu a data com giz.
tip: Used on blackboards, though many classrooms now use whiteboard markers instead.

example: Use a marker to write on the whiteboard.
examplePt: Use um marcador para escrever no quadro branco.
tip: Used on whiteboards, unlike chalk, which is used on blackboards.

example: Open your textbook to page ten.
examplePt: Abram o livro didático na página dez.
tip: A compound word: 'text' + 'book' — the official book for a school subject.

example: The kids play outside during recess.
examplePt: As crianças brincam lá fora durante o recreio.
tip: American English term for the break between classes — British English says 'break time'.

example: Students must wear their uniform every day.
examplePt: Os alunos devem usar o uniforme todo dia.
tip: From 'uni-' (one) + 'form' — literally, the same shape for everyone.

example: She hired a math tutor for her son.
examplePt: Ela contratou um professor particular de matemática para o filho.
tip: A private teacher who helps one student, unlike a classroom teacher.

example: The teacher checks attendance every morning.
examplePt: O professor confere a presença toda manhã.
tip: From the verb 'attend' — refers to whether or not you showed up.

example: Check the timetable for your next class.
examplePt: Confira o horário para sua próxima aula.
tip: Mostly British English — American English usually prefers 'schedule'.

example: She is a loyal employee of the company.
examplePt: Ela é uma funcionária leal da empresa.
tip: Someone who works for a company, opposite of 'employer'.

example: My employer offers good benefits.
examplePt: Meu empregador oferece bons benefícios.
tip: The person or company that hires and pays workers.

example: I need to talk to my manager.
examplePt: Preciso falar com meu gerente.
tip: Comes from 'manage' — someone responsible for running a team or department.

example: This project requires good teamwork.
examplePt: Este projeto exige um bom trabalho em equipe.
tip: A compound word — 'team' plus 'work'.

example: She got a promotion after two years.
examplePt: Ela conseguiu uma promoção depois de dois anos.
tip: Can also mean advertising, so context matters: job promotion vs. sales promotion.

example: He worked overtime to finish the report.
examplePt: Ele fez hora extra para terminar o relatório.
tip: Also used in sports, meaning extra time played after a tie.

example: She did an internship at a law firm.
examplePt: Ela fez estágio em um escritório de advocacia.
tip: A temporary position, often unpaid or low-paid, meant to gain experience.

example: New employees receive a week of training.
examplePt: Novos funcionários recebem uma semana de treinamento.
tip: Can apply to both a new job and to physical exercise, like 'gym training'.

example: Communication is an important skill.
examplePt: Comunicação é uma habilidade importante.
tip: Something you get better at with practice.

example: She built a successful career in medicine.
examplePt: Ela construiu uma carreira de sucesso na medicina.
tip: Refers to your whole professional path, not just one job.

example: The workplace has a very friendly atmosphere.
examplePt: O local de trabalho tem um ambiente muito amigável.
tip: A compound word combining 'work' and 'place'.

example: I work the night shift this week.
examplePt: Trabalho no turno da noite esta semana.
tip: Also a verb meaning to move or change, as in 'to shift positions'.

example: He gets his paycheck every two weeks.
examplePt: Ele recebe o contracheque a cada duas semanas.
tip: American English word for the document or deposit showing your salary.

example: She is planning her retirement carefully.
examplePt: Ela está planejando sua aposentadoria com cuidado.
tip: From the verb 'retire' — to formally stop working, usually due to age.

example: The company values work-life balance.
examplePt: A empresa valoriza o equilíbrio entre vida e trabalho.
tip: A modern phrase describing the healthy split between career and personal time.

example: He's wearing a plain white T-shirt.
examplePt: Ele está usando uma camiseta branca lisa.
tip: Named 'T-shirt' because, laid flat, its shape resembles the letter T.

example: These jeans are my favorite.
examplePt: Essa calça jeans é minha favorita.
tip: Named after Genoa, Italy ('Gênes' in French), where a similar fabric was first made.

example: It's hot, so I'm wearing shorts today.
examplePt: Está calor, então estou de bermuda hoje.
tip: Like 'pants', it's always used in the plural form in English.

example: She bought a silk blouse for the interview.
examplePt: Ela comprou uma blusa de seda para a entrevista.
tip: Usually refers to a light, feminine top — more formal than a T-shirt.

example: He wore a black suit to the wedding.
examplePt: Ele usou um terno preto no casamento.
tip: Also a verb: 'to suit' someone means to look good on them.

example: He put on a vest under his jacket.
examplePt: Ele colocou um colete embaixo da jaqueta.
tip: In British English, 'vest' actually means an undershirt — the outer piece is called a 'waistcoat'.

example: She's still in her pajamas.
examplePt: Ela ainda está de pijama.
tip: Comes from a Persian/Urdu word for loose trousers — always plural in English.

example: Don't forget your swimsuit for the beach.
examplePt: Não esqueça o maiô para a praia.
tip: A compound word: 'swim' + 'suit'.

example: Wear a raincoat, it might rain later.
examplePt: Use uma capa de chuva, pode chover mais tarde.
tip: A compound word combining 'rain' and 'coat'.

example: I always carry an umbrella in my bag.
examplePt: Eu sempre carrego um guarda-chuva na bolsa.
tip: Comes from the Latin word 'umbra', meaning shade or shadow.

example: She wore a gold necklace.
examplePt: Ela usava um colar de ouro.
tip: A compound word — 'neck' + 'lace'.

example: He gave her a silver bracelet.
examplePt: Ele deu a ela uma pulseira de prata.
tip: From French 'bracel', related to 'bras', meaning arm.

example: She only wears small earrings.
examplePt: Ela só usa brincos pequenos.
tip: Almost always used in the plural, since they come in pairs.

example: I forgot my wallet at home.
examplePt: Esqueci minha carteira em casa.
tip: Usually refers to a small, flat case for men — used for cards and cash.

example: She keeps her keys in her purse.
examplePt: Ela guarda as chaves na bolsa.
tip: In American English, this means a small handbag; in British English, it means a coin purse.

example: She matched her handbag to her shoes.
examplePt: Ela combinou a bolsa de mão com os sapatos.
tip: The standard British English word for what Americans usually call a 'purse'.

example: The zipper on my jacket got stuck.
examplePt: O zíper da minha jaqueta emperrou.
tip: Invented in the late 1800s, the name comes from the 'zip' sound it makes.

example: One button fell off my shirt.
examplePt: Um botão caiu da minha camisa.
tip: Also used for buttons you press, like on a remote control or elevator.

example: This fabric feels very soft.
examplePt: Esse tecido é bem macio ao toque.
tip: A general word for cloth material, before it's sewn into clothing.

example: This shirt is made of 100% cotton.
examplePt: Essa camisa é feita de 100% algodão.
tip: One of the oldest and most widely used natural fabrics in the world.

example: He bought a leather jacket.
examplePt: Ele comprou uma jaqueta de couro.
tip: Made from animal hide — spelled similarly to 'feather', but pronounced differently.

example: I wear sandals all summer.
examplePt: Eu uso sandálias o verão todo.
tip: Open shoes, ideal for hot weather — always used in the plural.

example: She bought new sneakers for running.
examplePt: Ela comprou tênis novos para correr.
tip: American English word — British English usually says 'trainers'.

example: He gave a thumbs up.
examplePt: Ele fez sinal de positivo com o polegar.
tip: The 'b' at the end is silent.

example: I stubbed my toe on the table.
examplePt: Bati o dedo do pé na mesa.
tip: The 'finger' equivalent for the foot.

example: She twisted her ankle playing soccer.
examplePt: Ela torceu o tornozelo jogando futebol.
tip: The joint that connects the foot to the leg.

example: He wears a watch on his wrist.
examplePt: Ele usa um relógio no pulso.
tip: The 'w' is silent, just like in 'write' and 'wrong'.

example: She put her hands on her hips.
examplePt: Ela colocou as mãos no quadril.
tip: Also part of the phrase 'hip-hop', a music and dance style.

example: The belt fits perfectly around his waist.
examplePt: O cinto serve perfeitamente na cintura dele.
tip: Sounds exactly like 'waste' (garbage) — spelling is the only difference.

example: He felt a pain in his chest.
examplePt: Ele sentiu uma dor no peito.
tip: Also means a large storage box, like a 'treasure chest'.

example: My back hurts from sitting all day.
examplePt: Minhas costas doem de tanto sentar.
tip: One of the most common English words — also means 'to return' or 'the rear side' of anything.

example: The spine protects the spinal cord.
examplePt: A coluna vertebral protege a medula espinhal.
tip: Also the word for the narrow back edge of a book, where its title is printed.

example: He pulled a muscle at the gym.
examplePt: Ele estirou um músculo na academia.
tip: The 'c' is silent — it's pronounced like 'mussel', the shellfish.

example: The dentist touched a nerve.
examplePt: O dentista tocou em um nervo.
tip: 'Nerve' also means courage, as in 'he had the nerve to ask'.

example: You can see the veins on his arm.
examplePt: Dá para ver as veias no braço dele.
tip: Sounds exactly like 'vain' (excessively proud) — different spelling, same sound.

example: Arteries carry blood away from the heart.
examplePt: As artérias levam sangue para longe do coração.
tip: The opposite of a vein — it carries blood away from, not toward, the heart.

example: The liver filters toxins from the blood.
examplePt: O fígado filtra as toxinas do sangue.
tip: One of the few organs in the body that can regenerate itself.

example: Humans have two kidneys.
examplePt: Humanos têm dois rins.
tip: Named after its bean-like shape — 'kidney beans' were named after the organ, not the other way around.

example: My stomach hurts after that meal.
examplePt: Meu estômago dói depois dessa refeição.
tip: Notice the spelling — pronounced 'STUM-ək', not with a hard 'ch' sound.

example: She raised an eyebrow in surprise.
examplePt: Ela ergueu a sobrancelha, surpresa.
tip: A compound word: 'eye' + 'brow'.

example: A eyelash fell into her eye.
examplePt: Um cílio caiu no olho dela.
tip: A compound word: 'eye' + 'lash'.

example: He kissed her on the cheek.
examplePt: Ele a beijou na bochecha.
tip: 'Cheeky' as an adjective means playfully disrespectful.

example: She touched his forehead to check for fever.
examplePt: Ela tocou a testa dele para ver se tinha febre.
tip: A compound word: 'fore' (front) + 'head'.

example: His jaw dropped in shock.
examplePt: O queixo dele caiu de choque.
tip: 'Jaw-dropping' is a common idiom for something amazing or shocking.

example: She painted her fingernails red.
examplePt: Ela pintou as unhas das mãos de vermelho.
tip: A compound word — 'finger' + 'nail', distinguishing it from a toenail.

example: She bit her lip nervously.
examplePt: Ela mordeu o lábio, nervosa.
tip: 'To read someone's lips' means to understand speech just by watching the mouth.

example: I have a sore throat today.
examplePt: Estou com dor de garganta hoje.
tip: 'A frog in your throat' is an idiom meaning a raspy, hoarse voice.

example: This software needs an update.
examplePt: Esse software precisa de atualização.
tip: The opposite of 'hardware' — the programs, not the physical parts, of a computer.

example: The computer's hardware is very old.
examplePt: O hardware do computador é muito antigo.
tip: The physical parts of a computer — screen, keyboard, chips, and cables.

example: Visit our website for more information.
examplePt: Visite nosso site para mais informações.
tip: A compound word: 'web' + 'site' — literally a 'place' on the web.

example: Please enter your password.
examplePt: Por favor, digite sua senha.
tip: A compound word — 'pass' (to gain entry) + 'word'.

example: I need to download this file.
examplePt: Preciso baixar esse arquivo.
tip: The opposite of 'upload' — bringing data down to your device.

example: She uploaded the photos to the cloud.
examplePt: Ela enviou as fotos para a nuvem.
tip: Sending data up from your device to the internet or a server.

example: The office has wireless internet.
examplePt: O escritório tem internet sem fio.
tip: The '-less' suffix means 'without' — literally 'without wires'.

example: The factory uses robots to assemble cars.
examplePt: A fábrica usa robôs para montar carros.
tip: The word comes from a Czech play, based on a word meaning 'forced labor'.

example: The sensor detects motion in the room.
examplePt: O sensor detecta movimento na sala.
tip: A device that reacts to light, heat, motion, or other physical changes.

example: The circuit broke, so the light stopped working.
examplePt: O circuito quebrou, então a luz parou de funcionar.
tip: A closed loop that lets electricity flow — 'short circuit' is when it flows the wrong way.

example: The village sits in a green valley.
examplePt: A vila fica em um vale verde.
tip: Low land between two mountains or hills, often carved by a river.

example: The Grand Canyon is over a mile deep.
examplePt: O Grand Canyon tem mais de um quilômetro de profundidade.
tip: A deep, narrow valley carved by a river over millions of years.

example: We hiked to see the waterfall.
examplePt: Fizemos trilha para ver a cachoeira.
tip: A compound word: 'water' + 'fall'.

example: The glacier is slowly melting.
examplePt: A geleira está derretendo lentamente.
tip: A massive, slow-moving river of ice, formed over hundreds of years.

example: Florida is a peninsula in the United States.
examplePt: A Flórida é uma península nos Estados Unidos.
tip: From Latin: 'paene' (almost) + 'insula' (island) — 'almost an island'.

example: Africa is the second largest continent.
examplePt: A África é o segundo maior continente.
tip: There are seven of them, though some geographers count only six.

example: Brazil is crossed by the equator.
examplePt: O Brasil é cortado pela linha do Equador.
tip: The imaginary line dividing the Earth into the Northern and Southern hemispheres.

example: Brazil is in the Southern Hemisphere.
examplePt: O Brasil fica no hemisfério sul.
tip: From Greek: 'hemi' (half) + 'sphere' (globe) — literally 'half a sphere'.

example: The house stands on a cliff above the sea.
examplePt: A casa fica em um penhasco acima do mar.
tip: A steep rock face, often found along coastlines.

example: Bats live inside the cave.
examplePt: Morcegos vivem dentro da caverna.
tip: Prehistoric humans famously used caves for shelter — hence 'caveman'.

example: The Great Plains stretch across the US.
examplePt: As Grandes Planícies se estendem pelos EUA.
tip: Sounds exactly like 'plane' (aircraft) — spelled differently, though.

example: The plateau offers a wide view of the valley.
examplePt: O planalto oferece uma vista ampla do vale.
tip: A flat, elevated area — like a plain, but raised above the surrounding land.

example: They spent the summer on the coast.
examplePt: Eles passaram o verão no litoral.
tip: 'The coast is clear' is a common idiom meaning it's safe to proceed.

example: The hurricane caused major damage.
examplePt: O furacão causou grandes danos.
tip: The same storm is called a 'typhoon' in the Pacific and a 'cyclone' in the Indian Ocean.

example: A tornado touched down near the farm.
examplePt: Um tornado atingiu perto da fazenda.
tip: The United States sees more tornadoes than any other country in the world.

example: The earthquake triggered a tsunami.
examplePt: O terremoto provocou um tsunami.
tip: A Japanese word meaning 'harbor wave' — now used in English worldwide.

example: Every citizen has the right to vote.
examplePt: Todo cidadão tem direito ao voto.
tip: A legally recognized member of a country or nation.

example: Technology is changing society quickly.
examplePt: A tecnologia está mudando a sociedade rapidamente.
tip: A broad word for people living together with shared laws and customs.

example: The victims are demanding justice.
examplePt: As vítimas estão exigindo justiça.
tip: Also the title for a judge, especially on a Supreme Court.

example: Freedom of speech is a basic right.
examplePt: Liberdade de expressão é um direito básico.
tip: From 'free' + '-dom', a suffix meaning 'the state of being'.

example: The movement fights for equality.
examplePt: O movimento luta pela igualdade.
tip: The state of being equal in rights, status, or opportunities.

example: The two countries finally made peace.
examplePt: Os dois países finalmente fizeram as pazes.
tip: Sounds exactly like 'piece' (a part of something) — different spelling entirely.

example: Thousands joined the protest downtown.
examplePt: Milhares se juntaram ao protesto no centro.
tip: As a verb, the stress shifts: 'to protést' something.

example: Workers went on strike for better pay.
examplePt: Os trabalhadores entraram em greve por salários melhores.
tip: Also means to hit something, as in 'lightning struck the tree'.

example: She donates to charity every month.
examplePt: Ela doa para caridade todo mês.
tip: Can mean the concept of kindness, or a specific organization that helps people.

example: He volunteers at the shelter on weekends.
examplePt: Ele trabalha como voluntário no abrigo nos fins de semana.
tip: Works as both a noun (a person) and a verb (to offer help for free).

example: Immigration policy is a hot political topic.
examplePt: A política de imigração é um tema político quente.
tip: 'Immigrate' means to move INTO a country; 'emigrate' means to move OUT of one.

example: The city is known for its cultural diversity.
examplePt: A cidade é conhecida por sua diversidade cultural.
tip: From 'diverse' — the presence of many different kinds of people or ideas.

example: The country welcomed thousands of refugees.
examplePt: O país acolheu milhares de refugiados.
tip: Someone forced to flee their country due to war, violence, or persecution.

example: The census counts every resident of the country.
examplePt: O censo conta todos os moradores do país.
tip: An official count of a population, usually done every ten years.

example: The program improves the welfare of children.
examplePt: O programa melhora o bem-estar das crianças.
tip: Can mean general well-being, or government aid for people in need.

example: The wires are made of copper.
examplePt: Os fios são feitos de cobre.
tip: One of the best natural conductors of electricity, used in most wiring.

example: Aluminum is light but very strong.
examplePt: O alumínio é leve, mas muito resistente.
tip: American English spells it 'aluminum'; British English spells it 'aluminium'.

example: The tires are made of rubber.
examplePt: Os pneus são feitos de borracha.
tip: Named because it was originally used to 'rub out' pencil marks.

example: The workers poured cement for the floor.
examplePt: Os trabalhadores despejaram cimento para o piso.
tip: Mixed with water, sand, and gravel, it becomes concrete.

example: The path is made of flat stones.
examplePt: O caminho é feito de pedras planas.
tip: In British English, it's also a unit of weight equal to 6.35 kg.

example: The statue was carved from marble.
examplePt: A estátua foi esculpida em mármore.
tip: A prized stone for sculpture and architecture, used since ancient Greece.

example: The chandelier is made of crystal.
examplePt: O lustre é feito de cristal.
tip: A solid whose atoms are arranged in a highly ordered, repeating pattern.

example: Water is a liquid at room temperature.
examplePt: A água é líquida em temperatura ambiente.
tip: One of the three basic states of matter, along with solid and gas.

example: This bridge is built entirely of metal.
examplePt: Esta ponte é feita inteiramente de metal.
tip: Also the name of a music genre known for its heavy, distorted sound.

example: We saw lions at the zoo.
examplePt: Vimos leões no zoológico.
tip: Short for 'zoological garden' — one of the shortest words in English.

example: Let's meet at the mall this weekend.
examplePt: Vamos nos encontrar no shopping neste fim de semana.
tip: Short for 'shopping mall' — American English term for a shopping center.

example: She buys fresh vegetables at the market.
examplePt: Ela compra verduras frescas no mercado.
tip: Can mean a physical place, or the broader economic concept, like 'the stock market'.

example: I need to pick up medicine from the pharmacy.
examplePt: Preciso pegar remédio na farmácia.
tip: British English also commonly uses the word 'chemist's' for this.

example: He goes to the gym every morning.
examplePt: Ele vai à academia toda manhã.
tip: Short for 'gymnasium', which originally referred to a Greek training ground.

example: Let's go to the cinema tonight.
examplePt: Vamos ao cinema hoje à noite.
tip: British English says 'cinema'; American English usually says 'movie theater'.

example: They grow corn on their farm.
examplePt: Eles cultivam milho na fazenda.
tip: Also used as a verb: 'to farm' means to work the land for crops or animals.

example: The factory produces thousands of cars a year.
examplePt: A fábrica produz milhares de carros por ano.
tip: From 'facere' in Latin, meaning 'to make'.

example: They live in a small village in the mountains.
examplePt: Eles moram em um pequeno vilarejo nas montanhas.
tip: Smaller than a town, usually with a close-knit community.

example: It's a quiet town with friendly people.
examplePt: É uma cidade pequena e tranquila, com gente simpática.
tip: Bigger than a village, smaller than a 'city'.

example: We live in a quiet neighborhood.
examplePt: Moramos em um bairro tranquilo.
tip: American English spelling — British English writes it 'neighbourhood'.

example: The office is downtown.
examplePt: O escritório fica no centro da cidade.
tip: American English term — British English usually says 'city centre'.

example: Fishing boats returned to the harbor.
examplePt: Os barcos de pesca voltaram ao porto.
tip: American spelling; British English writes it 'harbour'.

example: He rides a motorcycle to work.
examplePt: Ele vai de motocicleta para o trabalho.
tip: A compound word: 'motor' + 'cycle'.

example: The truck delivers goods every morning.
examplePt: O caminhão entrega mercadorias toda manhã.
tip: British English calls this a 'lorry' instead.

example: I take the subway to school.
examplePt: Eu vou de metrô para a escola.
tip: American English word — British English calls it the 'underground' or 'the tube'.

example: The ship sailed across the ocean.
examplePt: O navio navegou pelo oceano.
tip: Larger than a boat — generally used for ocean travel, not rivers or lakes.

example: A helicopter flew over the city.
examplePt: Um helicóptero sobrevoou a cidade.
tip: From Greek: 'helix' (spiral) + 'pteron' (wing).

example: Kids ride scooters in the park.
examplePt: As crianças andam de patinete no parque.
tip: Can mean the small two-wheeled kick vehicle, or the motorized version.

example: We took the ferry across the river.
examplePt: Pegamos a balsa para atravessar o rio.
tip: A boat that regularly carries passengers and vehicles across water.

example: The train will arrive at noon.
examplePt: O trem vai chegar ao meio-dia.
tip: The opposite of 'to leave' — always followed by 'at' or 'in', never 'to'.

example: I have to leave early today.
examplePt: Eu preciso sair cedo hoje.
tip: Also means to leave something behind, as in 'don't leave your bag'.

example: Please wait for me here.
examplePt: Por favor, me espere aqui.
tip: Sounds exactly like 'weight' (how heavy something is).

example: Can I ask you a question?
examplePt: Posso te fazer uma pergunta?
tip: Covers both asking a question and asking for something.

example: She didn't answer my call.
examplePt: Ela não atendeu minha ligação.
tip: The 'w' is silent — pronounced 'AN-ser'.

example: Just try your best.
examplePt: Apenas tente o seu melhor.
tip: Followed by 'to' plus a verb: 'try to understand', not 'try understand'.

example: I need to finish this project today.
examplePt: Preciso terminar esse projeto hoje.
tip: Can be followed by '-ing': 'finish reading', unlike many other verbs.

example: The movie starts at eight.
examplePt: O filme começa às oito.
tip: Also used for machines and vehicles — 'the car won't start'.

example: Stop the car, please!
examplePt: Pare o carro, por favor!
tip: 'Stop doing X' means quit it; 'stop to do X' means pause in order to do it.

example: Please continue with the story.
examplePt: Por favor, continue com a história.
tip: The opposite of 'to stop'.

example: Our team won the match.
examplePt: Nosso time venceu a partida.
tip: Irregular verb: win, won, won.

example: I always lose my keys.
examplePt: Eu sempre perco minhas chaves.
tip: Careful not to confuse with 'loose' (not tight) — different spelling and sound.

example: They sell fruit at the market.
examplePt: Eles vendem frutas no mercado.
tip: Opposite of 'to buy' — irregular: sell, sold, sold.

example: Can I pay by card?
examplePt: Posso pagar com cartão?
tip: Irregular past tense: 'paid', not 'payed'.

example: She spends a lot on books.
examplePt: Ela gasta muito com livros.
tip: Used for both money and time: 'spend money' and 'spend time'.

example: I'm trying to save money this month.
examplePt: Estou tentando economizar dinheiro este mês.
tip: Also used for saving files on a computer.

example: Please send me the report.
examplePt: Por favor, me envie o relatório.
tip: Irregular verb: send, sent, sent.

example: I received your message.
examplePt: Eu recebi sua mensagem.
tip: Follows the 'i before e except after c' spelling rule.

example: I'll call you tonight.
examplePt: Eu te ligo hoje à noite.
tip: Also means to name someone: 'they called him John'.

example: Nice to meet you!
examplePt: Prazer em te conhecer!
tip: Irregular verb: meet, met, met.

example: We're going to visit my grandmother.
examplePt: Vamos visitar minha avó.
tip: Can be used for both people and places.

example: They love to travel abroad.
examplePt: Eles adoram viajar para o exterior.
tip: American English doubles the 'l' in '-ing': 'traveling' or 'travelling', both accepted.

example: She drives to work every day.
examplePt: Ela dirige para o trabalho todos os dias.
tip: Irregular verb: drive, drove, driven.

example: He learned to ride a bike at six.
examplePt: Ele aprendeu a andar de bicicleta aos seis anos.
tip: Used for bikes, horses, and motorcycles — not cars, which use 'drive'.

example: Can you fix my computer?
examplePt: Você pode consertar meu computador?
tip: Also means to make something permanent, as in 'fix a date'.

example: I need to clean my room.
examplePt: Preciso limpar meu quarto.
tip: Also an adjective: 'a clean house' means a house that is already tidy.

example: Wash your hands before eating.
examplePt: Lave as mãos antes de comer.
tip: More specific than 'clean' — usually involves water and soap.

example: She loves to paint landscapes.
examplePt: Ela adora pintar paisagens.
tip: Used for both art and painting walls or objects.

example: He can draw really well.
examplePt: Ele sabe desenhar muito bem.
tip: Irregular verb: draw, drew, drawn — also means to end a game in a tie.

example: She sings beautifully.
examplePt: Ela canta lindamente.
tip: Irregular verb: sing, sang, sung.

example: They danced all night.
examplePt: Eles dançaram a noite toda.
tip: American English says 'dénss'; British English says 'dahnss'.

example: That joke made everyone laugh.
examplePt: Aquela piada fez todo mundo rir.
tip: The 'gh' is pronounced like an 'f' — one of English's trickiest spellings.

example: The baby started to cry.
examplePt: O bebê começou a chorar.
tip: Also means to shout, as in 'a battle cry'.

example: She smiled when she saw him.
examplePt: Ela sorriu quando o viu.
tip: Unlike 'laugh', it doesn't produce any sound.

example: Don't shout, I can hear you.
examplePt: Não grite, eu consigo te ouvir.
tip: A synonym is 'to yell' — both mean to speak very loudly.

example: She whispered the secret to me.
examplePt: Ela sussurrou o segredo para mim.
tip: The exact opposite of 'to shout'.

example: Follow me, it's this way.
examplePt: Me siga, é por aqui.
tip: Also used online: 'to follow' someone on social media.

example: She leads a team of ten people.
examplePt: Ela lidera uma equipe de dez pessoas.
tip: Pronounced like 'lead' the verb (líd), different from 'lead' the metal (léd).

example: He teaches math at the school.
examplePt: Ele ensina matemática na escola.
tip: Irregular verb: teach, taught, taught — related to 'teacher'.

example: Can you explain this rule again?
examplePt: Você pode explicar essa regra de novo?
tip: Followed directly by the topic — no preposition needed: 'explain the rule'.

example: I don't understand this question.
examplePt: Eu não entendo essa pergunta.
tip: Irregular verb: understand, understood, understood.

example: I can't remember his name.
examplePt: Eu não consigo lembrar o nome dele.
tip: The opposite of 'to forget'.

example: Imagine living on the moon!
examplePt: Imagine viver na lua!
tip: Often followed by '-ing': 'imagine living', not 'imagine to live'.

example: She dreams of becoming a doctor.
examplePt: Ela sonha em se tornar médica.
tip: Both a verb for sleeping visions and for hopes about the future.

example: I wake up at six every day.
examplePt: Eu acordo às seis todo dia.
tip: A phrasal verb — 'wake' alone can sound incomplete in everyday speech.

example: You should rest after the surgery.
examplePt: Você deve descansar depois da cirurgia.
tip: Also a noun meaning 'the remaining part', as in 'the rest of the day'.

example: Just relax, everything will be fine.
examplePt: Só relaxe, vai dar tudo certo.
tip: Related to the adjective 'relaxed', meaning calm.

example: Don't worry, I'll handle it.
examplePt: Não se preocupe, eu resolvo isso.
tip: 'Worry about' is the standard pattern: 'worry about the exam'.

example: I really care about you.
examplePt: Eu realmente me importo com você.
tip: 'Take care' as a farewell literally means 'look after yourself'.

example: Can you share your notes with me?
examplePt: Você pode compartilhar suas anotações comigo?
tip: Used both for physical things and digital content, like photos or posts.

example: The disappearance remains a mystery.
examplePt: O desaparecimento continua sendo um mistério.
tip: Something unexplained that raises curiosity and questions.

example: Can you solve this riddle?
examplePt: Você consegue resolver essa charada?
tip: A puzzling question, often with a clever or hidden answer.

example: This puzzle has a thousand pieces.
examplePt: Esse quebra-cabeça tem mil peças.
tip: Can mean a physical jigsaw or any confusing problem to solve.

example: It was just an optical illusion.
examplePt: Era apenas uma ilusão de ótica.
tip: Something that appears real but isn't — a trick of perception.

example: Time travel creates famous paradoxes.
examplePt: Viagem no tempo cria paradoxos famosos.
tip: A statement that seems to contradict itself, yet may still be true.

example: They believed it was fate that brought them together.
examplePt: Eles acreditavam que foi o destino que os uniu.
tip: Suggests events controlled by an unseen, unavoidable force.

example: She believes she was born for a great destiny.
examplePt: Ela acredita que nasceu para um grande destino.
tip: Similar to 'fate', but often used more personally, about one's life path.

example: With age comes wisdom.
examplePt: Com a idade vem a sabedoria.
tip: Different from 'knowledge' — wisdom is knowing how to use what you know.

example: Knowledge is power.
examplePt: Conhecimento é poder.
tip: The 'k' and 'w' are silent — pronounced 'NOL-ij'.

example: Curiosity led her to explore the cave.
examplePt: A curiosidade a levou a explorar a caverna.
tip: 'Curiosity killed the cat' is a famous idiom warning against being too curious.

example: Children have wonderful imaginations.
examplePt: Crianças têm imaginações maravilhosas.
tip: The mental ability to form new ideas or images not present to the senses.

example: He felt a strange emptiness after the trip ended.
examplePt: Ele sentiu um vazio estranho depois que a viagem acabou.
tip: Often used emotionally, unlike 'void', which is more physical or abstract.

example: It felt like an eternity waiting for the results.
examplePt: Pareceu uma eternidade esperando os resultados.
tip: Time without end — often used to exaggerate how long something felt.

example: By chance, they met again years later.
examplePt: Por acaso, eles se encontraram de novo anos depois.
tip: Can mean an opportunity, or pure randomness — context decides which.

example: What a coincidence running into you here!
examplePt: Que coincidência te encontrar aqui!
tip: Two events happening together by chance, without any real connection.

example: The dove is a symbol of peace.
examplePt: A pomba é um símbolo de paz.
tip: Something that represents an idea larger than itself.

example: He gave the signal to start.
examplePt: Ele deu o sinal para começar.
tip: Can be a sound, light, or gesture used to communicate quickly.

example: There's a clear pattern in her behavior.
examplePt: Há um padrão claro no comportamento dela.
tip: A repeated arrangement — used for both fabric designs and abstract behavior.

example: Yoga helps improve balance.
examplePt: Yoga ajuda a melhorar o equilíbrio.
tip: Also used financially, as in 'bank balance' — the amount you have left.

example: The universe seems to follow a hidden order.
examplePt: O universo parece seguir uma ordem oculta.
tip: Can mean sequence, command, or the opposite of chaos, depending on context.

example: The origin of the word is unknown.
examplePt: A origem da palavra é desconhecida.
tip: Where something first began — from Latin 'origo', meaning 'a rising'.

example: Kindness is the essence of who she is.
examplePt: A bondade é a essência de quem ela é.
tip: The core, fundamental nature of something — what makes it truly itself.

example: Philosophers debate the meaning of existence.
examplePt: Filósofos debatem o sentido da existência.
tip: The state of being real or alive, as opposed to not existing at all.

example: The mask hid his true identity.
examplePt: A máscara escondia sua verdadeira identidade.
tip: Who or what someone or something fundamentally is.

example: Try seeing it from her perspective.
examplePt: Tente ver pela perspectiva dela.
tip: A particular way of viewing or understanding something.

example: You need to set healthy boundaries.
examplePt: Você precisa estabelecer limites saudáveis.
tip: Can mean a physical border or a personal, emotional limit.

example: The sun disappeared below the horizon.
examplePt: O sol desapareceu no horizonte.
tip: 'On the horizon' is an idiom meaning something is about to happen soon.

example: Her voice echoed through the cave.
examplePt: A voz dela ecoou pela caverna.
tip: In Greek myth, Echo was a nymph cursed to only repeat others' words.

example: She spoke in a soft whisper.
examplePt: Ela falou em um sussurro suave.
tip: The noun form of 'to whisper' — a very quiet way of speaking.

example: Her face lit up with joy.
examplePt: O rosto dela se iluminou de alegria.
tip: A deeper, more intense feeling than simple happiness.

example: Their love grew stronger over the years.
examplePt: O amor deles ficou mais forte ao longo dos anos.
tip: In tennis, 'love' also strangely means a score of zero.

example: He struggled to control his anger.
examplePt: Ele lutou para controlar sua raiva.
tip: The noun form related to the adjective 'angry'.

example: She looked worried about the test.
examplePt: Ela parecia preocupada com a prova.
tip: The adjective form of the verb 'to worry'.

example: Stay calm, everything is under control.
examplePt: Fique calmo, está tudo sob controle.
tip: The 'l' is silent — pronounced 'kahm'.

example: He felt relaxed after the massage.
examplePt: Ele se sentiu relaxado depois da massagem.
tip: The adjective form of the verb 'to relax'.

example: I'm too tired to go out tonight.
examplePt: Estou cansado demais para sair hoje à noite.
tip: Less intense than 'exhausted' — everyday tiredness.

example: She was exhausted after the marathon.
examplePt: Ela estava exausta depois da maratona.
tip: A much stronger word than 'tired' — completely drained of energy.

example: I'm confused by these instructions.
examplePt: Estou confuso com essas instruções.
tip: The adjective form of the verb 'to confuse'.

example: She felt confident before the interview.
examplePt: Ela se sentiu confiante antes da entrevista.
tip: Related to the noun 'confidence' — belief in your own abilities.

example: The kids were curious about the old house.
examplePt: As crianças estavam curiosas sobre a casa velha.
tip: The adjective form related to the noun 'curiosity'.

example: I'm grateful for your help.
examplePt: Sou grato pela sua ajuda.
tip: Literally 'full of grace' or gratitude — a stronger word than just 'thankful'.

example: She remained hopeful about the results.
examplePt: Ela permaneceu esperançosa quanto aos resultados.
tip: 'Hope' + '-ful', meaning 'full of hope'.

example: He felt lonely in the big city.
examplePt: Ele se sentiu solitário na cidade grande.
tip: Different from 'alone' — 'alone' is a fact, 'lonely' is a feeling.

example: She was embarrassed by the mistake.
examplePt: Ela ficou envergonhada com o erro.
tip: Notice the double 'r' and double 's' — a commonly misspelled word.

example: He was disappointed with the results.
examplePt: Ele ficou decepcionado com os resultados.
tip: Related to the verb 'to disappoint' — to fail to meet expectations.

example: She felt frustrated with the slow internet.
examplePt: Ela ficou frustrada com a internet lenta.
tip: That specific mix of anger and helplessness when something doesn't work.

example: I was relieved to hear the good news.
examplePt: Fiquei aliviado ao ouvir a boa notícia.
tip: That feeling right after worry disappears.

example: She was satisfied with her performance.
examplePt: Ela ficou satisfeita com sua performance.
tip: The adjective form of the verb 'to satisfy'.

example: He is always cheerful in the morning.
examplePt: Ele está sempre animado de manhã.
tip: 'Cheer' + '-ful' — full of good spirits.

example: The rain made the trip miserable.
examplePt: A chuva deixou a viagem infeliz.
tip: Describes deep unhappiness, or very unpleasant conditions.

example: She seems content with her simple life.
examplePt: Ela parece contente com sua vida simples.
tip: Quieter than 'happy' — a calm, settled satisfaction. As a noun (CON-tent), it means the material inside something.

example: I have two options — which one do you like?
examplePt: Eu tenho duas opções — qual delas você gosta?
tip: Used when choosing between specific, known options.

example: Whose is this jacket? I found it on the chair.
examplePt: De quem é essa jaqueta? Achei na cadeira.
tip: 'Whose' asks about ownership — don't confuse it with 'who's' (who is).

example: You need a ladder? What for?
examplePt: Você precisa de uma escada? Para quê?
tip: A short, casual way to ask about purpose.

example: How long does the flight take?
examplePt: Quanto tempo dura o voo?
tip: Asks about duration, not distance — for distance, use 'how far'.

example: How far is the beach from here?
examplePt: A que distância fica a praia daqui?
tip: Asks specifically about distance, not time.

example: How often do you exercise?
examplePt: Com que frequência você se exercita?
tip: Used to ask about frequency, like 'daily' or 'twice a week'.

example: Is it okay if I open the window?
examplePt: Tudo bem se eu abrir a janela?
tip: A polite way to ask for permission or check if something is acceptable.

example: Excuse me, could you help me with this bag?
examplePt: Com licença, você poderia me ajudar com essa mala?
tip: 'Could' makes a request more polite than 'can'.

example: I don't know this word — what does it mean?
examplePt: Não conheço essa palavra — o que ela significa?
tip: A very useful phrase when you're actively learning a new language.

example: I can't find my phone. Where is it?
examplePt: Não acho meu celular. Onde está?
tip: One of the most common questions in daily conversation.

example: You look upset — what happened?
examplePt: Você parece chateado — o que aconteceu?
tip: Asked when something seems to have gone wrong or changed suddenly.

example: I agree with your idea.
examplePt: Eu concordo com sua ideia.
tip: The opposite is 'I disagree'.

example: I disagree, I think it's a bad plan.
examplePt: Eu discordo, acho que é um mau plano.
tip: A polite way to express a different opinion.

example: Oh, that makes sense now.
examplePt: Ah, agora isso faz sentido.
tip: Said when something finally becomes clear or logical.

example: It doesn't matter what time we arrive.
examplePt: Não importa a que horas chegamos.
tip: A common phrase to show something isn't important.

example: Let me think about it and I'll let you know.
examplePt: Deixa eu pensar sobre isso e te aviso.
tip: Buys you a moment before answering a question.

example: I'll be right back, one second.
examplePt: Já volto, um segundo.
tip: Used when stepping away briefly.

example: Please take your seat, class is starting.
examplePt: Por favor, sente-se, a aula vai começar.
tip: A polite instruction to sit down, common in classrooms and events.

example: Hold on a second, I need to grab my phone.
examplePt: Espera um segundo, preciso pegar meu celular.
tip: A very common way to ask someone to wait briefly.

example: We can go either way, it's up to you.
examplePt: Podemos ir dos dois jeitos, você decide.
tip: Hands the decision over to the other person.

example: Don't worry, I'm on my way!
examplePt: Não se preocupe, estou a caminho!
tip: Very common when someone is running late and reassuring another person.

example: Could you speak slowly, please? I'm still learning.
examplePt: Você poderia falar devagar, por favor? Ainda estou aprendendo.
tip: An essential phrase for any language learner.

example: Sorry, could you say that again?
examplePt: Desculpe, você pode repetir?
tip: A polite way to ask for repetition, more formal than 'What?'

example: Excuse me, I have a question.
examplePt: Com licença, eu tenho uma pergunta.
tip: A polite way to interrupt politely, especially in a classroom or meeting.

example: That's not right, let me check again.
examplePt: Isso não está certo, deixa eu conferir de novo.
tip: Used to point out an error, gently.

example: Good point, I hadn't thought of that.
examplePt: Boa observação, eu não tinha pensado nisso.
tip: A common way to acknowledge someone's smart comment during a conversation.

example: Never mind, it's not important anymore.
examplePt: Deixa pra lá, não é mais importante.
tip: Used to dismiss something you said, or to say something isn't a big deal.

example: Please send it as soon as possible.
examplePt: Por favor, envie o mais rápido possível.
tip: Often abbreviated in writing as 'ASAP'.

example: The trip was expensive, but it's worth it.
examplePt: A viagem foi cara, mas vale a pena.
tip: Says that something is good enough to justify its cost or effort.

example: I'm not sure what time the store closes.
examplePt: Não tenho certeza a que horas a loja fecha.
tip: A softer way to say 'I don't know'.

example: I'm busy now, let's talk later.
examplePt: Estou ocupado agora, vamos conversar depois.
tip: A polite way to postpone a conversation.

example: The quarterly report shows steady growth.
examplePt: O relatório trimestral mostra crescimento constante.
tip: Published every three months to track a company's performance.

example: Our fiscal year starts in April.
examplePt: Nosso ano fiscal começa em abril.
tip: A company's 12-month accounting period, which doesn't always match the calendar year.

example: The startup struggled with cash flow.
examplePt: A startup teve dificuldades com o fluxo de caixa.
tip: The movement of money in and out of a business.

example: Rent is a major overhead cost.
examplePt: O aluguel é um custo fixo importante.
tip: Ongoing expenses not tied directly to producing a product, like rent or utilities.

example: The company's net worth doubled last year.
examplePt: O patrimônio líquido da empresa dobrou no ano passado.
tip: Total assets minus total liabilities — what's really left over.

example: Investors received equity in the company.
examplePt: Os investidores receberam participação acionária na empresa.
tip: Ownership value in a company, often given in exchange for investment.

example: Shareholders received a dividend this quarter.
examplePt: Os acionistas receberam um dividendo neste trimestre.
tip: A portion of company profits paid out to shareholders.

example: The acquisition doubled the company's size.
examplePt: A aquisição dobrou o tamanho da empresa.
tip: When one company buys and takes control of another.

example: The bank maintains high liquidity.
examplePt: O banco mantém alta liquidez.
tip: How easily assets can be converted into cash without losing value.

example: The company filed for bankruptcy.
examplePt: A empresa entrou com pedido de falência.
tip: The legal process for a business or person unable to pay their debts.

example: The company had a monopoly on the market.
examplePt: A empresa tinha o monopólio do mercado.
tip: When a single company completely controls a market — also a famous board game.

example: Logistics is key to on-time delivery.
examplePt: A logística é essencial para entregas no prazo.
tip: The planning and coordination of moving goods and resources.

example: The procurement team negotiated a better price.
examplePt: A equipe de compras negociou um preço melhor.
tip: The formal process of obtaining goods or services for a business.

example: We need to check the inventory levels.
examplePt: Precisamos conferir os níveis de estoque.
tip: All the goods and materials a business currently holds.

example: They buy products wholesale and resell them.
examplePt: Eles compram produtos no atacado e revendem.
tip: Selling in large quantities at lower prices, usually to other businesses.

example: Retail prices are higher than wholesale.
examplePt: Os preços no varejo são mais altos que no atacado.
tip: Selling directly to the final consumer, usually in smaller quantities.

example: She earns a commission on every sale.
examplePt: Ela recebe uma comissão em cada venda.
tip: A payment based on a percentage of sales made.

example: The author receives a royalty for each book sold.
examplePt: O autor recebe um royalty por cada livro vendido.
tip: A payment made to the owner of a right, like a patent or a book.

example: The logo is a registered trademark.
examplePt: O logotipo é uma marca registrada.
tip: A legally protected symbol, name, or design that identifies a brand.

example: The inventor filed a patent for his design.
examplePt: O inventor registrou uma patente para o design dele.
tip: Legal protection that stops others from copying an invention.

example: The brand grows through licensing deals.
examplePt: A marca cresce por meio de acordos de licenciamento.
tip: Granting official permission for someone else to use your product, brand, or technology.

example: The company passed its annual audit.
examplePt: A empresa passou pela auditoria anual.
tip: A formal, independent check of a company's finances or processes.

example: The sales forecast looks promising.
examplePt: A previsão de vendas parece promissora.
tip: Also used for weather — a prediction based on current data and trends.

example: This product sets the benchmark for quality.
examplePt: Esse produto define o padrão de referência de qualidade.
tip: A standard used to measure and compare performance.

example: Launching the app was a major milestone.
examplePt: Lançar o aplicativo foi um marco importante.
tip: A significant point of progress in a project or plan.

example: The onboarding process takes one week.
examplePt: O processo de integração dura uma semana.
tip: The process of training and settling new employees into a company.

example: The company announced downsizing last month.
examplePt: A empresa anunciou redução de quadro no mês passado.
tip: Reducing the number of employees, usually to cut costs.

example: The layoffs affected hundreds of workers.
examplePt: As demissões em massa afetaram centenas de trabalhadores.
tip: A temporary or permanent dismissal of workers, often due to a downturn.

example: The restaurant has high staff turnover.
examplePt: O restaurante tem alta rotatividade de funcionários.
tip: Can mean employee replacement rate, or total sales revenue, depending on context.

example: The company offers incentives for good performance.
examplePt: A empresa oferece incentivos para bom desempenho.
tip: Something that motivates people to act in a certain way, often a reward.

example: I collect points in the airline's loyalty program.
examplePt: Eu acumulo pontos no programa de fidelidade da companhia aérea.
tip: Rewards designed to keep customers coming back.

example: The buyer did due diligence before the deal.
examplePt: O comprador fez a diligência prévia antes do negócio.
tip: Careful investigation of a company before making a deal, like buying it.

example: They did a cost-benefit analysis first.
examplePt: Eles fizeram uma análise de custo-benefício primeiro.
tip: Weighing what something costs against what it delivers in return.

example: The bottom line is what really matters to investors.
examplePt: O resultado final é o que realmente importa para os investidores.
tip: Literally the last line of a financial statement — the final profit or loss.

example: Ask the pharmacist about side effects.
examplePt: Pergunte ao farmacêutico sobre os efeitos colaterais.
tip: The professional who prepares and dispenses medication.

example: She saw a cardiologist about her heart.
examplePt: Ela consultou um cardiologista sobre o coração.
tip: From 'cardio' (heart) + '-ologist' (specialist).

example: The pediatrician checked the baby's weight.
examplePt: O pediatra conferiu o peso do bebê.
tip: A doctor who specializes in treating children.

example: I have an appointment with a dermatologist.
examplePt: Tenho consulta marcada com um dermatologista.
tip: From 'derma' (skin) — a doctor who treats skin conditions.

example: A psychiatrist can prescribe medication.
examplePt: Um psiquiatra pode prescrever medicação.
tip: Unlike a psychologist, a psychiatrist is a medical doctor who can prescribe drugs.

example: The radiologist reviewed the X-ray.
examplePt: O radiologista analisou o raio-X.
tip: A specialist who interprets medical images like X-rays and MRIs.

example: The anesthesiologist prepared the patient for surgery.
examplePt: O anestesista preparou o paciente para a cirurgia.
tip: One of the longest common medical job titles in English.

example: The body produces antibodies to fight infection.
examplePt: O corpo produz anticorpos para combater a infecção.
tip: A protein made by the immune system to fight off invaders like viruses.

example: Not all bacteria are harmful.
examplePt: Nem todas as bactérias são prejudiciais.
tip: Always plural — the singular form, rarely used, is 'bacterium'.

example: The virus spreads through close contact.
examplePt: O vírus se espalha por contato próximo.
tip: Unlike bacteria, viruses can't reproduce without infecting a living cell.

example: Clean the wound with antiseptic.
examplePt: Limpe o ferimento com antisséptico.
tip: Used on skin to prevent infection, unlike a disinfectant, used on surfaces.

example: The doctor gave her a mild sedative.
examplePt: O médico deu a ela um sedativo leve.
tip: A drug used to calm the patient or induce sleep before a procedure.

example: Take a painkiller if the headache continues.
examplePt: Tome um analgésico se a dor de cabeça continuar.
tip: A compound word — literally 'pain' + 'killer'.

example: The cut needed five stitches.
examplePt: O corte precisou de cinco pontos.
tip: Used to close a wound — always used in the plural when referring to sutures.

example: She wrapped a bandage around his knee.
examplePt: Ela enrolou uma bandagem no joelho dele.
tip: Used to protect and support an injured part of the body.

example: The doctor applied a splint to the broken finger.
examplePt: O médico colocou uma tala no dedo quebrado.
tip: A rigid support used to keep a broken bone still while it heals.

example: He walked with crutches after the surgery.
examplePt: Ele andava de muletas depois da cirurgia.
tip: Always used in the plural, just like 'scissors' and 'glasses'.

example: She uses a wheelchair to get around.
examplePt: Ela usa cadeira de rodas para se locomover.
tip: A compound word: 'wheel' + 'chair'.

example: The doctor used a stethoscope to check his heart.
examplePt: O médico usou um estetoscópio para checar o coração dele.
tip: Invented in 1816 to listen to the heart and lungs without direct contact.

example: The thermometer showed a high fever.
examplePt: O termômetro mostrou febre alta.
tip: From Greek 'thermo' (heat) + 'meter' (measure).

example: The nurse prepared the syringe.
examplePt: A enfermeira preparou a seringa.
tip: Used to inject or withdraw fluids from the body.

example: The ambulance arrived within minutes.
examplePt: A ambulância chegou em minutos.
tip: From a French term meaning 'mobile hospital', first used for battlefield care.

example: The patient was moved to intensive care.
examplePt: O paciente foi transferido para os cuidados intensivos.
tip: Often abbreviated 'ICU' — Intensive Care Unit.

example: The surgery was done on an outpatient basis.
examplePt: A cirurgia foi feita em regime ambulatorial.
tip: A patient who receives treatment without staying overnight.

example: He was admitted as an inpatient.
examplePt: Ele foi internado como paciente.
tip: The opposite of an outpatient — someone who stays in the hospital.

example: I have an annual checkup next week.
examplePt: Tenho um check-up anual semana que vem.
tip: A routine medical exam to confirm everything is healthy.

example: The clinic offers free cancer screening.
examplePt: A clínica oferece triagem gratuita de câncer.
tip: A test done to detect a disease early, before symptoms appear.

example: The doctor recommended a biopsy.
examplePt: O médico recomendou uma biópsia.
tip: The removal of a small tissue sample to examine it closely.

example: She started chemotherapy last month.
examplePt: Ela começou a quimioterapia no mês passado.
tip: Often shortened to 'chemo' in casual speech.

example: Radiotherapy targets cancer cells directly.
examplePt: A radioterapia atinge diretamente as células cancerígenas.
tip: Uses radiation to destroy or shrink abnormal cells.

example: He needs a kidney transplant.
examplePt: Ele precisa de um transplante de rim.
tip: Moving an organ or tissue from one body to another.

example: She registered as an organ donor.
examplePt: Ela se cadastrou como doadora de órgãos.
tip: Someone who gives blood, organs, or tissue to help another person.

example: He suffers from chronic insomnia.
examplePt: Ele sofre de insônia crônica.
tip: From Latin: 'in-' (without) + 'somnus' (sleep).

example: She gets migraines when she's stressed.
examplePt: Ela tem enxaquecas quando está estressada.
tip: Much more intense than a regular headache, often with light sensitivity and nausea.

example: The case falls under federal jurisdiction.
examplePt: O caso está sob jurisdição federal.
tip: The official authority to make legal decisions over a specific area or case.

example: The statute was passed last year.
examplePt: O estatuto foi aprovado no ano passado.
tip: A formal, written law created by a legislature.

example: The ruling set an important precedent.
examplePt: A decisão estabeleceu um precedente importante.
tip: A previous case used as a legal example or guide for future decisions.

example: This is a classic case of tort law.
examplePt: Este é um caso clássico de direito de responsabilidade civil.
tip: A civil wrong that causes harm, allowing the victim to sue for damages.

example: The company was sued for negligence.
examplePt: A empresa foi processada por negligência.
tip: Failing to take reasonable care, resulting in harm to someone else.

example: The court awarded damages to the victim.
examplePt: O tribunal concedeu indenização à vítima.
tip: In legal English, this plural noun means monetary compensation, not just harm.

example: They reached a settlement out of court.
examplePt: Eles chegaram a um acordo fora do tribunal.
tip: An agreement that resolves a dispute without going to trial.

example: The dispute was resolved through mediation.
examplePt: O conflito foi resolvido por meio de mediação.
tip: A neutral third party helps both sides reach an agreement.

example: She received a subpoena to testify.
examplePt: Ela recebeu uma intimação para testemunhar.
tip: A legal order requiring someone to appear in court or provide evidence.

example: The police obtained a search warrant.
examplePt: A polícia obteve um mandado de busca.
tip: Official legal permission to make an arrest or conduct a search.

example: The grand jury issued an indictment.
examplePt: O grande júri emitiu uma denúncia formal.
tip: The 'c' is silent — pronounced 'in-DITE-ment'.

example: The trial ended in acquittal.
examplePt: O julgamento terminou em absolvição.
tip: A formal declaration that the defendant is not guilty.

example: He was released on parole.
examplePt: Ele foi solto em liberdade condicional.
tip: Early release from prison under supervision, with conditions attached.

example: She was sentenced to two years of probation.
examplePt: Ela foi sentenciada a dois anos em regime de suspensão condicional.
tip: A punishment served under supervision, instead of jail time.

example: He pays alimony every month.
examplePt: Ele paga pensão alimentícia todo mês.
tip: Financial support paid to a former spouse after divorce.

example: The lawyer took her deposition.
examplePt: O advogado colheu o depoimento dela.
tip: Sworn testimony given outside the courtroom, usually before a trial.

example: He signed an affidavit confirming the facts.
examplePt: Ele assinou uma declaração juramentada confirmando os fatos.
tip: A written statement made under oath.

example: You'll need the document notarized by a notary.
examplePt: Você vai precisar do documento reconhecido em cartório.
tip: An official who witnesses signatures and certifies documents.

example: The song is protected by copyright.
examplePt: A música é protegida por direito autoral.
tip: The legal right to control who can copy, sell, or use a creative work.

example: The company protects its intellectual property fiercely.
examplePt: A empresa protege sua propriedade intelectual com rigor.
tip: Legal ownership of ideas, inventions, and creative work — often abbreviated 'IP'.

example: Everyone has the right to due process.
examplePt: Todos têm direito ao devido processo legal.
tip: The guarantee that legal procedures will be fair and follow established rules.

example: The lawyer filed a writ of habeas corpus.
examplePt: O advogado apresentou um pedido de habeas corpus.
tip: Latin for 'you shall have the body' — protects against unlawful detention.

example: She obtained a restraining order against him.
examplePt: Ela obteve uma medida protetiva contra ele.
tip: A court order that legally prevents someone from approaching another person.

example: The professor teaches jurisprudence.
examplePt: O professor leciona jurisprudência.
tip: The theory and philosophy of law, or a body of legal decisions.

example: Both litigants presented their evidence.
examplePt: Ambos os litigantes apresentaram suas provas.
tip: A person involved in a lawsuit, either suing or being sued.

example: The case is awaiting adjudication.
examplePt: O caso aguarda julgamento formal.
tip: The formal, legal process of settling a dispute or claim.

example: His arraignment is scheduled for Monday.
examplePt: Sua audiência de acusação formal está marcada para segunda.
tip: The hearing where a defendant is formally charged and enters a plea.

example: Lying under oath is called perjury.
examplePt: Mentir sob juramento é chamado de perjúrio.
tip: The crime of lying while under oath in a legal setting.

example: The country requested his extradition.
examplePt: O país solicitou sua extradição.
tip: Sending a suspect back to another country to face trial there.

example: The government granted amnesty to the prisoners.
examplePt: O governo concedeu anistia aos prisioneiros.
tip: An official pardon for people convicted of certain crimes, often political.

example: The governor granted clemency to the inmate.
examplePt: O governador concedeu clemência ao detento.
tip: Mercy shown by reducing or forgiving a punishment.

example: The city passed a new noise ordinance.
examplePt: A cidade aprovou uma nova norma sobre ruído.
tip: A local law made by a city or town government.

example: The case was heard by an international tribunal.
examplePt: O caso foi julgado por um tribunal internacional.
tip: A special court set up to judge a specific type of case.

example: She is a talented young filmmaker.
examplePt: Ela é uma jovem cineasta talentosa.
tip: A general term for anyone who makes films, from director to producer.

example: The producer secured funding for the movie.
examplePt: O produtor conseguiu financiamento para o filme.
tip: Manages the business side of a film, unlike the director, who oversees creative choices.

example: The editor cut hours of footage.
examplePt: O editor cortou horas de material filmado.
tip: Shapes the final film by selecting and arranging the recorded scenes.

example: The movie's score won an award.
examplePt: A trilha sonora do filme ganhou um prêmio.
tip: Refers specifically to the original instrumental music, unlike a 'soundtrack', which can include songs.

example: The costume design won an Oscar.
examplePt: O figurino ganhou um Oscar.
tip: The art of creating the clothing worn by characters on screen.

example: The set design recreated the 1920s perfectly.
examplePt: A cenografia recriou os anos 1920 perfeitamente.
tip: The visual design and construction of a film's physical locations.

example: Casting for the new film starts next week.
examplePt: A escalação de elenco do novo filme começa semana que vem.
tip: The process of choosing actors for each role.

example: She did a screen test for the lead role.
examplePt: Ela fez um teste de tela para o papel principal.
tip: A filmed audition to see how an actor looks and performs on camera.

example: It's his first feature film as director.
examplePt: É seu primeiro longa-metragem como diretor.
tip: A full-length movie, usually over 40 minutes — the opposite of a 'short film'.

example: The short film won at the festival.
examplePt: O curta-metragem venceu no festival.
tip: A film shorter than a feature, often under 40 minutes.

example: The indie film became a surprise hit.
examplePt: O filme independente se tornou um sucesso surpresa.
tip: Short for 'independent film' — made outside the major movie studios.

example: Silent films relied heavily on music and gestures.
examplePt: Filmes mudos dependiam muito de música e gestos.
tip: Movies made before synchronized sound became standard in the late 1920s.

example: The film was shot in widescreen.
examplePt: O filme foi gravado em tela panorâmica.
tip: A wider aspect ratio than traditional television format.

example: The film uses a higher frame rate for action scenes.
examplePt: O filme usa uma taxa de quadros mais alta nas cenas de ação.
tip: How many individual images are shown per second — standard film is 24.

example: The camera zoomed in for a close-up.
examplePt: A câmera se aproximou para um close.
tip: A shot framed tightly on a subject's face or a small detail.

example: The wide shot revealed the whole city.
examplePt: O plano geral revelou a cidade inteira.
tip: A shot that shows a large area, the opposite of a close-up.

example: The documentary uses a calm voiceover.
examplePt: O documentário usa uma narração em off tranquila.
tip: Spoken narration that isn't part of the visible scene.

example: The narrator explains the backstory.
examplePt: O narrador explica a história de fundo.
tip: The voice that tells the story, whether seen on screen or not.

example: The antagonist is more interesting than the hero.
examplePt: O antagonista é mais interessante que o herói.
tip: The main character who opposes the protagonist.

example: The sidekick provides comic relief.
examplePt: O parceiro fornece o alívio cômico.
tip: A funny character or moment used to ease tension in a serious story.

example: The storm was foreshadowing disaster.
examplePt: A tempestade era um prenúncio do desastre.
tip: A hint early in the story about events that will happen later.

example: The training montage lasted two minutes.
examplePt: A montagem de treinamento durou dois minutos.
tip: A sequence of short clips edited together to show the passage of time.

example: The movie is an adaptation of the novel.
examplePt: O filme é uma adaptação do romance.
tip: A film based on a book, play, or other original source.

example: The show got its own spin-off series.
examplePt: A série ganhou seu próprio spin-off.
tip: A new story built around a secondary character from an existing one.

example: The film received an R rating.
examplePt: O filme recebeu uma classificação restrita.
tip: An official label showing the appropriate audience age for a film.

example: The studio held a test screening for the ending.
examplePt: O estúdio fez uma sessão de teste para o final.
tip: A private showing of an unfinished film to gauge audience reaction before release.

example: Stars walked the red carpet at the premiere.
examplePt: As estrelas desfilaram no tapete vermelho na estreia.
tip: The famous walkway where celebrities are photographed before an event.

example: The studio funded the entire production.
examplePt: A produtora financiou toda a produção.
tip: The company that finances and often owns a film.

example: The screenwriter adapted the true story.
examplePt: O roteirista adaptou a história real.
tip: The person who writes the script — dialogue, scenes, and structure.

example: The stunt required months of training.
examplePt: A cena de acrobacia exigiu meses de treinamento.
tip: A dangerous action scene, usually performed by a trained double.

example: The actor made a special appearance in the finale.
examplePt: O ator fez uma participação especial no final.
tip: A brief, notable role, often by a famous actor, in a limited scene.

example: Tickets sold out for opening night.
examplePt: Os ingressos esgotaram para a noite de estreia.
tip: The very first public showing of a film or play.

example: Stay for the scene after the end credits.
examplePt: Fique para a cena depois dos créditos finais.
tip: The list of names shown after a movie, crediting everyone who worked on it.

example: The singer performed a slow ballad.
examplePt: A cantora apresentou uma balada lenta.
tip: A slow, emotional song — different from 'balada', the Brazilian Portuguese word for a party.

example: The crowd sang the national anthem.
examplePt: A multidão cantou o hino nacional.
tip: Can be a national song, or any song that becomes a symbol for a group.

example: Everyone sang along to the chorus.
examplePt: Todo mundo cantou junto no refrão.
tip: The repeated part of a song, usually the most memorable section.

example: The second verse tells a different story.
examplePt: A segunda estrofe conta uma história diferente.
tip: A section of a song's lyrics that changes each time, unlike the chorus.

example: The musical bridge builds tension before the final chorus.
examplePt: A ponte da música cria tensão antes do refrão final.
tip: A contrasting section that connects two parts of a song, often near the end.

example: The guitar riff is instantly recognizable.
examplePt: O riff de guitarra é reconhecível na hora.
tip: A short, catchy, repeated musical phrase, usually played on guitar.

example: She practices scales every day.
examplePt: Ela pratica escalas todos os dias.
tip: A set of musical notes arranged in order of pitch.

example: The song is written in the key of C.
examplePt: A música é escrita na tonalidade de dó.
tip: The set of notes and chords a piece of music is built around.

example: Each instrument has a unique timbre.
examplePt: Cada instrumento tem um timbre único.
tip: The unique 'color' of a sound that lets you tell instruments apart, even at the same pitch.

example: The choir sang a cappella.
examplePt: O coral cantou a cappella.
tip: Italian for 'in the style of the chapel' — singing without instruments.

example: He hit an impressive falsetto note.
examplePt: Ele atingiu uma nota impressionante em falsete.
tip: A technique letting singers reach notes higher than their normal range.

example: They performed a beautiful duet.
examplePt: Eles fizeram um belo dueto.
tip: A performance by exactly two singers or musicians together.
