example: The jazz trio played until midnight.
examplePt: O trio de jazz tocou até meia-noite.
tip: A group of exactly three musicians or singers.

example: The string quartet performed Beethoven.
examplePt: O quarteto de cordas tocou Beethoven.
tip: A group of four musicians, common in classical string ensembles.

example: They formed a rock band in college.
examplePt: Eles formaram uma banda de rock na faculdade.
tip: A general term for a group of musicians playing together.

example: He works as a session musician in the studio.
examplePt: Ele trabalha como músico de sessão no estúdio.
tip: A professional hired to record or perform without being a permanent band member.

example: The backup singers harmonized perfectly.
examplePt: Os backing vocals fizeram uma harmonia perfeita.
tip: Singers who support the lead vocalist without taking the spotlight.

example: The frontman engaged the whole crowd.
examplePt: O vocalista líder envolveu toda a plateia.
tip: The lead singer and public face of a band — also 'frontwoman' for a woman.

example: The band shared their setlist online.
examplePt: A banda compartilhou a lista de músicas do show online.
tip: The planned order of songs to be played during a concert.

example: The band did a sound check before the show.
examplePt: A banda fez o teste de som antes do show.
tip: A rehearsal to adjust audio levels before a live performance.

example: He plugged his guitar into the amplifier.
examplePt: Ele conectou a guitarra no amplificador.
tip: Often shortened to 'amp' in everyday conversation.

example: She grabbed the microphone and started singing.
examplePt: Ela pegou o microfone e começou a cantar.
tip: Often shortened to 'mic' in casual speech.

example: The DJ scratched the record on the turntable.
examplePt: O DJ fez scratch no disco no toca-discos.
tip: The spinning platform used to play vinyl records.

example: The DJ mixed songs all night long.
examplePt: O DJ misturou músicas a noite toda.
tip: Short for 'disc jockey' — someone who plays and mixes recorded music.

example: The remix became more popular than the original.
examplePt: O remix ficou mais popular que o original.
tip: A reworked version of an existing song, often for dance floors.

example: She performed a cover of a classic song.
examplePt: Ela apresentou um cover de uma música clássica.
tip: A new performance of a song originally recorded by someone else.

example: He can't play without sheet music.
examplePt: Ele não consegue tocar sem partitura.
tip: The written notation musicians read to play a piece.

example: Practice with a metronome to keep the beat.
examplePt: Pratique com um metrônomo para manter o ritmo.
tip: A device that produces a steady, regular click to help keep time.

example: The hall has amazing acoustic resonance.
examplePt: O salão tem uma ressonância acústica incrível.
tip: The way sound vibrates and is amplified in a space or instrument.

example: The violinist added vibrato to the note.
examplePt: O violinista adicionou vibrato à nota.
tip: A slight, rapid variation in pitch that adds warmth to a sustained note.

example: The orchestra played a slow diminuendo.
examplePt: A orquestra tocou um diminuendo lento.
tip: An Italian musical term meaning to gradually get quieter — the opposite of crescendo.

example: The overture introduces the opera's main themes.
examplePt: A abertura apresenta os temas principais da ópera.
tip: An instrumental piece that opens an opera, musical, or orchestral work.

example: The jingle got stuck in my head.
examplePt: O jingle ficou grudado na minha cabeça.
tip: A short, catchy tune, usually written for advertising.

example: He's a seasoned traveler.
examplePt: Ele é um viajante experiente.
tip: American English spells it 'traveler'; British English uses 'traveller'.

example: Our tour guide spoke four languages.
examplePt: Nosso guia turístico falava quatro idiomas.
tip: The professional who leads and informs travelers during a tour.

example: Sightseers crowded the old town square.
examplePt: Turistas lotaram a praça do centro histórico.
tip: Comes from 'sightseeing' — visiting places just to look at them.

example: We're planning our summer vacation.
examplePt: Estamos planejando nossas férias de verão.
tip: American English word — British English usually says 'holiday'.

example: They took a weekend getaway to the mountains.
examplePt: Eles fizeram uma escapada de fim de semana para as montanhas.
tip: A short trip meant to relax or escape daily routine.

example: We took a road trip across the country.
examplePt: Fizemos uma viagem de carro pelo país.
tip: A long journey traveled by car, often stopping at multiple places.

example: We went camping by the lake.
examplePt: Fomos acampar perto do lago.
tip: Sleeping outdoors, usually in a tent, as a form of travel or leisure.

example: The hiking trail leads to a waterfall.
examplePt: A trilha para caminhada leva a uma cachoeira.
tip: A marked path made for walking through nature.

example: We reserved a campsite near the river.
examplePt: Reservamos uma área de acampamento perto do rio.
tip: A designated spot where people can set up tents or campers.

example: It took them ten minutes to set up the tent.
examplePt: Eles levaram dez minutos para montar a barraca.
tip: The portable shelter used when camping.

example: Check the trail map before hiking.
examplePt: Confira o mapa de trilha antes da caminhada.
tip: Shows the paths, distances, and landmarks along a hiking route.

example: The national park protects rare wildlife.
examplePt: O parque nacional protege animais raros.
tip: Land protected by the government for conservation and public visits.

example: The safari passes through a wildlife reserve.
examplePt: O safári passa por uma reserva de vida selvagem.
tip: A protected area specifically for wild animals and plants.

example: We took the scenic route along the coast.
examplePt: Pegamos a rota panorâmica ao longo da costa.
tip: A longer path chosen for its beautiful views rather than speed.

example: They stopped at a border checkpoint.
examplePt: Eles pararam em um posto de controle na fronteira.
tip: A location where travelers are stopped for inspection or verification.

example: The line at passport control was long.
examplePt: A fila no controle de passaporte estava longa.
tip: The airport checkpoint where officials verify travelers' identity.

example: She bought perfume at the duty-free shop.
examplePt: Ela comprou perfume na loja livre de impostos.
tip: Shops at airports where goods are sold without certain local taxes.

example: London and New York are in different time zones.
examplePt: Londres e Nova York estão em fusos horários diferentes.
tip: A region where everyone uses the same standard time.

example: He struggled with jet lag after the long flight.
examplePt: Ele sofreu com jet lag depois do voo longo.
tip: Tiredness and confusion caused by crossing multiple time zones quickly.

example: The flight was overbooked by ten seats.
examplePt: O voo estava com overbooking de dez assentos.
tip: When more tickets are sold than available seats, betting some people won't show up.

example: She bought a one-way ticket to Lisbon.
examplePt: Ela comprou uma passagem só de ida para Lisboa.
tip: A ticket for travel in only one direction, unlike a round trip.

example: A round trip is often cheaper than two one-way tickets.
examplePt: Uma viagem de ida e volta costuma ser mais barata que duas passagens só de ida.
tip: British English usually calls this a 'return trip'.

example: We have a two-hour connecting flight.
examplePt: Temos uma conexão de duas horas.
tip: A second flight taken to reach your final destination.

example: We booked a non-stop flight to save time.
examplePt: Reservamos um voo direto para economizar tempo.
tip: A flight with no stops or layovers along the way.

example: We flew economy class to save money.
examplePt: Voamos na classe econômica para economizar.
tip: The standard, most affordable seating class on an airplane.

example: He upgraded to first class.
examplePt: Ele fez upgrade para a primeira classe.
tip: The most luxurious and expensive class of travel.

example: The travel agency planned our whole trip.
examplePt: A agência de viagens planejou toda nossa viagem.
tip: A business that helps plan and book trips for customers.

example: Always buy travel insurance for international trips.
examplePt: Sempre compre seguro viagem para viagens internacionais.
tip: Protects travelers against medical emergencies, cancellations, and lost luggage.

example: The package tour includes flights and hotels.
examplePt: O pacote de viagem inclui voos e hotéis.
tip: A pre-arranged trip bundling flights, hotels, and activities together.

example: We tried the local cuisine at every stop.
examplePt: Provamos a culinária local em cada parada.
tip: The traditional food of a specific region or country.

example: The trip was a great cultural exchange.
examplePt: A viagem foi um ótimo intercâmbio cultural.
tip: The sharing of customs, language, and ideas between different cultures.

example: We faced a language barrier at the market.
examplePt: Enfrentamos uma barreira linguística no mercado.
tip: The difficulty of communicating when people don't share a common language.

example: Visiting Japan is on my bucket list.
examplePt: Visitar o Japão está na minha lista de desejos.
tip: A list of experiences or achievements someone wants before they die.

example: The restaurant serves gourmet burgers.
examplePt: O restaurante serve hambúrgueres gourmet.
tip: Borrowed from French — describes high-quality, refined food.

example: Add more seasoning to the chicken.
examplePt: Adicione mais tempero no frango.
tip: A general term for salt, herbs, and spices added to flavor food.

example: The soup starts with a chicken broth.
examplePt: A sopa começa com um caldo de galinha.
tip: A thin, savory liquid made by simmering meat, bones, or vegetables.

example: Use vegetable stock instead of water.
examplePt: Use caldo de legumes em vez de água.
tip: Similar to broth but usually made mainly from bones, used as a cooking base.

example: Dip the fish in batter before frying.
examplePt: Passe o peixe na massa líquida antes de fritar.
tip: A wet mixture of flour and liquid, used for pancakes, cakes, and fried foods.

example: The pie has a flaky crust.
examplePt: A torta tem uma massa crocante.
tip: The outer, often crispy layer of bread, pizza, or a pie.

example: The pie has an apple filling.
examplePt: A torta tem recheio de maçã.
tip: Whatever goes inside a pie, sandwich, or pastry.

example: Brush a honey glaze over the ham.
examplePt: Passe uma cobertura de mel sobre o presunto.
tip: A shiny, often sweet coating brushed onto food.

example: Blend the tomatoes into a puree.
examplePt: Bata os tomates até virar um purê.
tip: Food blended or mashed into a smooth, thick consistency.

example: Blend the fruits with some ice.
examplePt: Bata as frutas com um pouco de gelo.
tip: To mix ingredients thoroughly, often using a blender.

example: Mince the garlic finely.
examplePt: Pique o alho bem miudinho.
tip: To chop food into very small pieces, smaller than dicing.

example: Julienne the carrots for the salad.
examplePt: Corte as cenouras em tiras finas para a salada.
tip: A French culinary term for cutting vegetables into thin matchstick strips.

example: Caramelize the onions slowly over low heat.
examplePt: Caramelize as cebolas lentamente em fogo baixo.
tip: To cook sugar or food slowly until it turns golden brown and sweet.

example: Let the dough ferment overnight.
examplePt: Deixe a massa fermentar durante a noite.
tip: A chemical process, used to make bread, yogurt, wine, and kombucha.

example: Season the meat with salt and pepper.
examplePt: Tempere a carne com sal e pimenta.
tip: As a verb, it means to add flavor — as a noun, it means part of the year.

example: Poach the eggs in simmering water.
examplePt: Cozinhe os ovos em água em fervura leve.
tip: A gentle cooking method using barely simmering liquid, common for eggs and fish.

example: Sauté the vegetables in olive oil.
examplePt: Salteie os legumes em azeite.
tip: French for 'jumped' — quick cooking in a small amount of hot oil.

example: Put the meat on a skewer.
examplePt: Coloque a carne no espeto.
tip: A thin stick used to hold pieces of food together while grilling.

example: She made a chicken casserole for dinner.
examplePt: Ela fez um cozido de frango no forno para o jantar.
tip: A baked dish, or the deep dish it's cooked in.

example: The beef stew simmered for hours.
examplePt: O ensopado de carne cozinhou em fogo baixo por horas.
tip: A dish of meat and vegetables slow-cooked in liquid.

example: Broil the fish for five minutes.
examplePt: Grelhe o peixe por cinco minutos sob calor direto.
tip: American English term — British English calls this 'grill'.

example: The chicken is deep-fried until golden.
examplePt: O frango é frito por imersão até dourar.
tip: Fully submerging food in hot oil, unlike pan-frying with less oil.

example: We had vegetable stir-fry for dinner.
examplePt: Comemos um salteado de legumes no jantar.
tip: A fast cooking technique using high heat and constant stirring, common in Asian cuisine.

example: We're having a barbecue this weekend.
examplePt: Vamos fazer um churrasco neste fim de semana.
tip: Often shortened to 'BBQ' — cooking food over an open flame or coals.

example: Ketchup is a popular condiment.
examplePt: Ketchup é um condimento popular.
tip: A sauce or seasoning added to food at the table, like mustard or mayonnaise.

example: Drizzle vinaigrette over the salad.
examplePt: Regue a salada com molho vinagrete.
tip: A dressing made mainly of oil and vinegar.

example: Let the meat sit in the marinade overnight.
examplePt: Deixe a carne na marinada durante a noite.
tip: The seasoned liquid used to soak and flavor food before cooking.

example: Duck confit is a French classic.
examplePt: Confit de pato é um clássico francês.
tip: A French method of slowly cooking food, usually meat, submerged in its own fat.

example: She grilled a salmon fillet.
examplePt: Ela grelhou um filé de salmão.
tip: A boneless cut of meat or fish.

example: Tenderize the steak before cooking.
examplePt: Amacie o bife antes de cozinhar.
tip: To make meat softer and easier to chew, often by pounding it.

example: Blanch the broccoli before freezing it.
examplePt: Branqueie o brócolis antes de congelar.
tip: Briefly boiling then cooling food in ice water to preserve color and texture.

example: Add lemon zest to the cake batter.
examplePt: Adicione raspas de limão na massa do bolo.
tip: The flavorful outer peel of citrus fruits, grated finely.

example: Remove the rind before eating the cheese.
examplePt: Remova a casca antes de comer o queijo.
tip: The tough outer layer of certain cheeses and fruits.

example: Negative five is an integer.
examplePt: Menos cinco é um número inteiro.
tip: A whole number, positive, negative, or zero — no fractions or decimals.

example: Seven is a prime number.
examplePt: Sete é um número primo.
tip: A number divisible only by 1 and itself.

example: The coefficient of x is three.
examplePt: O coeficiente de x é três.
tip: The number multiplying a variable in an equation, like the 3 in '3x'.

example: This is a polynomial with three terms.
examplePt: Este é um polinômio com três termos.
tip: An expression combining variables and coefficients using addition and multiplication.

example: Multiply the two matrices together.
examplePt: Multiplique as duas matrizes.
tip: A rectangular grid of numbers, widely used in computer graphics and physics.

example: The vector points north.
examplePt: O vetor aponta para o norte.
tip: A quantity with both magnitude and direction, unlike a simple number.

example: Find the derivative of the function.
examplePt: Encontre a derivada da função.
tip: In calculus, it measures how fast something is changing.

example: Solve the integral of this curve.
examplePt: Resolva a integral dessa curva.
tip: The opposite operation of a derivative — often used to calculate area.

example: Use a logarithm to solve for x.
examplePt: Use um logaritmo para resolver x.
tip: Tells you what power a base number must be raised to, to get another number.

example: Trigonometry deals with triangles and angles.
examplePt: A trigonometria lida com triângulos e ângulos.
tip: From Greek: 'trigonon' (triangle) + 'metron' (measure).

example: The hypotenuse is the longest side of the triangle.
examplePt: A hipotenusa é o lado mais longo do triângulo.
tip: Only right triangles have one — it's always opposite the right angle.

example: Calculate the perimeter of the field.
examplePt: Calcule o perímetro do campo.
tip: The total distance around the outside edge of a shape.

example: The area of the room is 20 square meters.
examplePt: A área do quarto é de 20 metros quadrados.
tip: The amount of space inside a two-dimensional shape.

example: The vertex of the triangle is at the top.
examplePt: O vértice do triângulo está no topo.
tip: The point where two or more lines meet, like a corner.

example: These two lines are parallel.
examplePt: Essas duas linhas são paralelas.
tip: Lines that never meet, no matter how far they extend.

example: The walls meet at a perpendicular angle.
examplePt: As paredes se encontram em um ângulo perpendicular.
tip: Two lines that meet at exactly 90 degrees.

example: Find the next number in the sequence.
examplePt: Encontre o próximo número na sequência.
tip: An ordered list of numbers following a specific pattern.

example: The series converges to a finite value.
examplePt: A série converge para um valor finito.
tip: The sum of the terms of a sequence.

example: Set theory is the foundation of modern math.
examplePt: A teoria dos conjuntos é a base da matemática moderna.
tip: The branch of math that studies collections of objects, called sets.

example: This function has one input and one output.
examplePt: Essa função tem uma entrada e uma saída.
tip: A rule that assigns exactly one output to each input.

example: The domain of this function is all real numbers.
examplePt: O domínio dessa função é todos os números reais.
tip: The set of all possible input values a function can accept.

example: The range of the function is positive numbers only.
examplePt: A imagem da função é apenas números positivos.
tip: The set of all possible output values a function can produce.

example: The line has a steep slope.
examplePt: A reta tem uma inclinação acentuada.
tip: How steep a line is, calculated as 'rise over run'.

example: Mark the point using its coordinates.
examplePt: Marque o ponto usando suas coordenadas.
tip: A set of numbers that shows the exact position of a point on a graph.

example: The point is in the first quadrant.
examplePt: O ponto está no primeiro quadrante.
tip: One of the four sections a graph is divided into by its two axes.

example: Solve the inequality for x.
examplePt: Resolva a inequação para x.
tip: A mathematical statement using symbols like '<' or '>' instead of '='.

example: Five factorial equals 120.
examplePt: Cinco fatorial é igual a 120.
tip: Written with an exclamation mark: 5! means 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1.

example: Calculate the number of permutations.
examplePt: Calcule o número de permutações.
tip: An arrangement of items where the order matters.

example: How many combinations are possible?
examplePt: Quantas combinações são possíveis?
tip: Unlike permutations, order doesn't matter in a combination.

example: Find the median of this data set.
examplePt: Encontre a mediana desse conjunto de dados.
tip: The middle value in a sorted list of numbers.

example: The mode is the most frequent number.
examplePt: A moda é o número que mais se repete.
tip: The value that appears most often in a set of data.

example: The standard deviation shows how spread out the data is.
examplePt: O desvio padrão mostra o quanto os dados estão dispersos.
tip: A measure of how much values vary from the average.

example: In 3/4, three is the numerator.
examplePt: Em 3/4, três é o numerador.
tip: The top number in a fraction, above the line.

example: In 3/4, four is the denominator.
examplePt: Em 3/4, quatro é o denominador.
tip: The bottom number in a fraction, below the line.

example: Scientists discovered a new exoplanet.
examplePt: Cientistas descobriram um novo exoplaneta.
tip: A planet that orbits a star outside our solar system.

example: Pluto is classified as a dwarf planet.
examplePt: Plutão é classificado como um planeta-anão.
tip: A celestial body that orbits the sun but hasn't cleared its orbital path.

example: The pulsar emits beams of radiation.
examplePt: O pulsar emite feixes de radiação.
tip: A rapidly spinning neutron star that emits regular pulses of radiation.

example: The quasar is billions of light years away.
examplePt: O quasar está a bilhões de anos-luz de distância.
tip: An extremely bright, distant object powered by a supermassive black hole.

example: The movie explores travel through a wormhole.
examplePt: O filme explora viagens por um buraco de minhoca.
tip: A theoretical tunnel through space-time connecting distant points.

example: The universe began with the Big Bang.
examplePt: O universo começou com o Big Bang.
tip: The leading scientific theory for how the universe began, about 13.8 billion years ago.

example: Redshift shows that the galaxy is moving away.
examplePt: O desvio para o vermelho mostra que a galáxia está se afastando.
tip: A shift in light indicating an object is moving away from us.

example: They traveled to see the aurora.
examplePt: Eles viajaram para ver a aurora.
tip: Colorful lights in the sky caused by solar particles hitting the atmosphere.

example: The meteorite left a large crater.
examplePt: O meteorito deixou uma cratera grande.
tip: A meteor that survives its fall and lands on Earth's surface.

example: Day and night are equal during the equinox.
examplePt: O dia e a noite são iguais durante o equinócio.
tip: One of two days a year when day and night are nearly equal in length.

example: The summer solstice is the longest day of the year.
examplePt: O solstício de verão é o dia mais longo do ano.
tip: The day with the most or least daylight of the year.

example: The sun reached its zenith at noon.
examplePt: O sol atingiu seu zênite ao meio-dia.
tip: The point directly above an observer in the sky.

example: The satellite reached its apogee.
examplePt: O satélite atingiu seu apogeu.
tip: The point in orbit farthest from the Earth.

example: The moon looks bigger at perigee.
examplePt: A lua parece maior no perigeu.
tip: The opposite of apogee — the closest point in an orbit.

example: Earth's axial tilt causes the seasons.
examplePt: A inclinação axial da Terra causa as estações do ano.
tip: The angle between a planet's rotation axis and its orbital plane.

example: Sunspots can affect satellite communication.
examplePt: Manchas solares podem afetar a comunicação por satélite.
tip: A temporary dark, cooler patch on the sun's surface caused by magnetic activity.

example: We went stargazing in the desert.
examplePt: Fomos observar as estrelas no deserto.
tip: The hobby of watching the night sky, often with a telescope.

example: The planetarium shows a virtual night sky.
examplePt: O planetário mostra um céu noturno virtual.
tip: A building with a domed screen that projects a simulated night sky.

example: Spectroscopy reveals what stars are made of.
examplePt: A espectroscopia revela do que as estrelas são feitas.
tip: Analyzing light to determine the chemical makeup of distant objects.

example: Cosmic rays constantly hit Earth's atmosphere.
examplePt: Raios cósmicos atingem constantemente a atmosfera da Terra.
tip: High-energy particles traveling through space from distant sources.

example: Interplanetary travel remains a huge challenge.
examplePt: Viagens interplanetárias continuam sendo um grande desafio.
tip: Describes anything traveling or existing between planets.

example: The space probe reached Jupiter after six years.
examplePt: A sonda espacial chegou a Júpiter depois de seis anos.
tip: An unmanned spacecraft sent to explore space or other planets.

example: The space shuttle launched successfully.
examplePt: O ônibus espacial foi lançado com sucesso.
tip: A reusable spacecraft designed to travel between Earth and orbit.

example: Mission control tracked the rocket's path.
examplePt: O centro de controle de missão rastreou a trajetória do foguete.
tip: The ground team that manages and monitors a space mission.

example: Astronauts float in zero gravity.
examplePt: Astronautas flutuam em gravidade zero.
tip: The condition of weightlessness experienced in orbit.

example: She studies astrophysics at university.
examplePt: Ela estuda astrofísica na universidade.
tip: The branch of physics that deals with stars, galaxies, and the universe.

example: Our solar system is part of the Milky Way.
examplePt: Nosso sistema solar faz parte da Via Láctea.
tip: The name of our home galaxy, visible as a bright band on clear nights.

example: The telescope revealed a distant star cluster.
examplePt: O telescópio revelou um aglomerado de estrelas distante.
tip: A group of stars held together by gravity.

example: A binary star system has two suns.
examplePt: Um sistema de estrela binária tem dois sóis.
tip: Two stars orbiting a common center of mass.

example: Nothing can escape past the event horizon.
examplePt: Nada pode escapar além do horizonte de eventos.
tip: The boundary around a black hole beyond which nothing, not even light, can escape.

example: Scientists debate terraforming Mars.
examplePt: Cientistas debatem a terraformação de Marte.
tip: The theoretical process of making another planet habitable for humans.

example: The film is about extraterrestrial life.
examplePt: O filme é sobre vida extraterrestre.
tip: From Latin: 'extra' (outside) + 'terrestris' (of the Earth).

example: The nova brightened suddenly in the sky.
examplePt: A nova brilhou repentinamente no céu.
tip: A star that suddenly becomes much brighter, then fades — smaller than a supernova.

example: The environmentalist campaigns against pollution.
examplePt: O ambientalista faz campanha contra a poluição.
tip: Someone actively working to protect the environment.

example: They only use eco-friendly packaging.
examplePt: Eles só usam embalagens ecológicas.
tip: Describes products or actions that don't harm the environment.

example: The company aims to be carbon neutral by 2030.
examplePt: A empresa pretende ser carbono neutro até 2030.
tip: Balancing carbon emissions with an equal amount removed or offset.

example: Air quality worsens during the dry season.
examplePt: A qualidade do ar piora durante a estação seca.
tip: A measure of how clean or polluted the air is.

example: Water scarcity affects millions of people.
examplePt: A escassez de água afeta milhões de pessoas.
tip: A shortage of clean, accessible water resources.

example: Overfishing has reduced fish populations.
examplePt: A pesca predatória reduziu as populações de peixes.
tip: Catching fish faster than they can naturally reproduce.

example: Poaching threatens endangered elephants.
examplePt: A caça ilegal ameaça elefantes em extinção.
tip: Illegally hunting or capturing protected wildlife.

example: Reforestation efforts restored the hillside.
examplePt: Os esforços de reflorestamento restauraram a encosta.
tip: The process of replanting trees in an area that lost its forest.

example: The farm follows permaculture principles.
examplePt: A fazenda segue princípios de permacultura.
tip: A farming approach that works with natural ecosystems, not against them.

example: The bus runs on biofuel.
examplePt: O ônibus funciona com biocombustível.
tip: Fuel produced from plants or organic waste, instead of fossil sources.

example: Iceland relies heavily on geothermal energy.
examplePt: A Islândia depende muito de energia geotérmica.
tip: Energy generated from the natural heat inside the Earth.

example: The dam generates hydropower for the region.
examplePt: A barragem gera energia hidrelétrica para a região.
tip: Electricity generated from the movement of water.

example: Nuclear energy produces almost no carbon emissions.
examplePt: A energia nuclear produz quase nenhuma emissão de carbono.
tip: Energy released from splitting atoms, powerful but controversial.

example: Emission trading lets companies buy carbon credits.
examplePt: O comércio de emissões permite que empresas comprem créditos de carbono.
tip: A system where companies can buy and sell the right to emit pollution.

example: The ozone layer protects us from UV rays.
examplePt: A camada de ozônio nos protege dos raios UV.
tip: A layer of the atmosphere that blocks most of the sun's harmful radiation.

example: Acid rain damaged the forest.
examplePt: A chuva ácida danificou a floresta.
tip: Rain made acidic by pollution, harmful to plants, water, and buildings.

example: Melting ice caps raise sea levels.
examplePt: O derretimento das calotas polares eleva o nível do mar.
tip: A major consequence of global warming affecting the polar regions.

example: Sea level rise threatens coastal cities.
examplePt: A elevação do nível do mar ameaça cidades costeiras.
tip: The gradual increase in ocean height, largely caused by melting ice.

example: The region is prone to natural disasters.
examplePt: A região é propensa a desastres naturais.
tip: Any severe natural event that causes major damage, like floods or earthquakes.

example: The city switched to green energy sources.
examplePt: A cidade migrou para fontes de energia verde.
tip: Energy generated from renewable, low-impact sources like sun and wind.

example: The store sells plastic-free products.
examplePt: A loja vende produtos livres de plástico.
tip: Describes products or lifestyles avoiding plastic entirely.

example: She follows a zero waste lifestyle.
examplePt: Ela segue um estilo de vida de lixo zero.
tip: A goal of producing as little trash as possible.

example: Upcycling turns old furniture into something new.
examplePt: O reaproveitamento criativo transforma móveis velhos em algo novo.
tip: Reusing waste material to create something of higher value, unlike recycling.

example: These bags are fully biodegradable.
examplePt: Essas sacolas são totalmente biodegradáveis.
tip: Describes material that breaks down naturally over time.

example: Flying often increases your ecological footprint.
examplePt: Voar com frequência aumenta sua pegada ecológica.
tip: A measure of how much environmental impact a person or activity has.

example: The wetland is home to many bird species.
examplePt: A zona úmida abriga muitas espécies de aves.
tip: Land saturated with water, crucial for biodiversity and flood control.

example: The coral reef is dying due to warming waters.
examplePt: O recife de coral está morrendo por causa do aquecimento das águas.
tip: One of the most biodiverse ecosystems on the planet, but very sensitive to heat.

example: Ecotourism supports local conservation efforts.
examplePt: O ecoturismo apoia esforços locais de conservação.
tip: Tourism focused on responsibly visiting natural areas.

example: The wildlife sanctuary rescues injured animals.
examplePt: O santuário de vida selvagem resgata animais feridos.
tip: A protected place where animals or plants are kept safe from harm.

example: Birds begin their migration in autumn.
examplePt: As aves iniciam sua migração no outono.
tip: The seasonal movement of animals, often to find food or better weather.

example: Pesticides can harm bees and other pollinators.
examplePt: Pesticidas podem prejudicar abelhas e outros polinizadores.
tip: A chemical used to kill insects or pests, but often harmful to the environment too.

example: Too much fertilizer pollutes rivers.
examplePt: Fertilizante em excesso polui os rios.
tip: A substance added to soil to help plants grow, but can cause pollution if overused.

example: Groundwater supplies most of the town's water.
examplePt: A água subterrânea abastece a maior parte da cidade.
tip: Water stored underground in soil and rock, a major freshwater source.

example: She sees a psychologist every week.
examplePt: Ela consulta um psicólogo toda semana.
tip: A professional who studies the mind and behavior, but cannot prescribe medication.

example: Psychotherapy helped him process his grief.
examplePt: A psicoterapia o ajudou a processar seu luto.
tip: Talk-based treatment for emotional and mental health issues.

example: Confirmation bias is a common cognitive bias.
examplePt: O viés de confirmação é um viés cognitivo comum.
tip: A systematic error in thinking that affects judgment and decisions.

example: Neuroscience studies how the brain works.
examplePt: A neurociência estuda como o cérebro funciona.
tip: The scientific study of the nervous system, especially the brain.

example: Children form strong attachments to their parents.
examplePt: Crianças formam apegos fortes aos pais.
tip: The emotional bond formed between people, especially early in life.

example: Babies show different temperaments from birth.
examplePt: Bebês mostram temperamentos diferentes desde o nascimento.
tip: A person's natural, innate personality traits present from an early age.

example: Self-awareness is key to personal growth.
examplePt: A autoconsciência é essencial para o crescimento pessoal.
tip: The ability to recognize and understand your own emotions and behavior.

example: It takes willpower to quit smoking.
examplePt: É preciso força de vontade para parar de fumar.
tip: The mental strength to control your own actions and impulses.

example: Procrastination is his biggest challenge at work.
examplePt: A procrastinação é seu maior desafio no trabalho.
tip: The habit of delaying tasks, even when you know it's not a good idea.

example: He used rationalization to justify the mistake.
examplePt: Ele usou racionalização para justificar o erro.
tip: A defense mechanism where people create logical excuses for their behavior.

example: Her anger was really a projection of her own fear.
examplePt: A raiva dela era, na verdade, uma projeção do próprio medo.
tip: Attributing your own feelings or flaws to someone else.

example: Repression can lead to emotional problems later.
examplePt: A repressão pode causar problemas emocionais mais tarde.
tip: Unconsciously pushing painful thoughts or memories out of awareness.

example: He accused her of gaslighting him during the argument.
examplePt: Ele a acusou de gaslighting durante a discussão.
tip: Manipulating someone into doubting their own memory or perception of reality.

example: Sometimes people just need validation, not advice.
examplePt: Às vezes as pessoas só precisam de validação, não de conselhos.
tip: Acknowledging that someone's feelings are real and understandable.

example: She spends time on introspection every night.
examplePt: Ela passa um tempo em introspecção toda noite.
tip: The act of examining your own thoughts and feelings closely.

example: Assertiveness training helped her speak up at work.
examplePt: O treinamento de assertividade a ajudou a se posicionar no trabalho.
tip: The ability to express your needs confidently, without being aggressive.

example: Their relationship shows signs of codependency.
examplePt: O relacionamento deles mostra sinais de codependência.
tip: An unhealthy reliance on another person for emotional validation.

example: Trauma can trigger dissociation.
examplePt: O trauma pode desencadear dissociação.
tip: A feeling of being disconnected from your thoughts, feelings, or surroundings.

example: Crying gave her a sense of catharsis.
examplePt: Chorar deu a ela uma sensação de catarse.
tip: The emotional relief that comes from releasing strong feelings.

example: Half the group received a placebo.
examplePt: Metade do grupo recebeu um placebo.
tip: A fake treatment used in studies — sometimes even it produces real results.

example: Pavlov's experiment demonstrated classical conditioning.
examplePt: O experimento de Pavlov demonstrou o condicionamento clássico.
tip: Learning a behavior through repeated association or reinforcement.

example: Positive reinforcement encourages good behavior.
examplePt: O reforço positivo incentiva o bom comportamento.
tip: A reward used to increase the likelihood of a behavior repeating.

example: The bell was a stimulus for the dog to salivate.
examplePt: O sino era um estímulo para o cachorro salivar.
tip: Anything that triggers a response — plural is 'stimuli'.

example: Fear triggers a fight-or-flight response.
examplePt: O medo dispara uma resposta de luta ou fuga.
tip: The reaction that follows a stimulus.

example: The hero is a common archetype in stories.
examplePt: O herói é um arquétipo comum nas histórias.
tip: A universal, recurring pattern or symbol, a concept popularized by Carl Jung.

example: Freud wrote extensively about neurosis.
examplePt: Freud escreveu bastante sobre neurose.
tip: An older psychological term for mild anxiety-related conditions.

example: She has a phobia of spiders.
examplePt: Ela tem fobia de aranhas.
tip: An intense, irrational fear of a specific object or situation.

example: He felt a compulsion to check the door twice.
examplePt: Ele sentia uma compulsão de checar a porta duas vezes.
tip: An irresistible urge to do something, often repeatedly.

example: His obsession with cleanliness became a problem.
examplePt: A obsessão dele com limpeza se tornou um problema.
tip: A persistent, intrusive thought that's hard to stop thinking about.

example: The patient experienced delusions during the episode.
examplePt: O paciente teve delírios durante a crise.
tip: A false belief held firmly despite clear evidence against it.

example: The fever caused hallucinations.
examplePt: A febre causou alucinações.
tip: Perceiving something (seeing, hearing) that isn't actually there.

example: Her therapist helped her manage anxiety.
examplePt: A terapeuta dela a ajudou a controlar a ansiedade.
tip: A broader term than 'psychologist' — covers many kinds of mental health professionals.

example: The company invests in employee wellness.
examplePt: A empresa investe no bem-estar dos funcionários.
tip: A broad concept covering physical, mental, and emotional health.

example: The archaeologist found ancient pottery.
examplePt: O arqueólogo encontrou cerâmica antiga.
tip: A scientist who studies human history through physical remains.

example: The pyramids of Egypt are thousands of years old.
examplePt: As pirâmides do Egito têm milhares de anos.
tip: Massive stone structures, most famously built as tombs for Egyptian pharaohs.

example: Hieroglyphs cover the tomb's walls.
examplePt: Hieróglifos cobrem as paredes da tumba.
tip: Ancient Egyptian writing that used pictures to represent words and sounds.

example: Ancient Egyptians wrote on papyrus.
examplePt: Os egípcios antigos escreviam em papiro.
tip: An early form of paper made from a Nile River plant.

example: The gladiator fought in the Roman arena.
examplePt: O gladiador lutava na arena romana.
tip: A trained fighter who battled for entertainment in ancient Rome.

example: The Crusades lasted for nearly two centuries.
examplePt: As Cruzadas duraram quase dois séculos.
tip: A series of medieval religious military campaigns.

example: Feudalism structured medieval European society.
examplePt: O feudalismo estruturou a sociedade medieval europeia.
tip: A medieval system where land was exchanged for loyalty and labor.

example: A serf worked the lord's land.
examplePt: Um servo trabalhava a terra do senhor.
tip: A peasant bound to work the land under feudalism, without full freedom.

example: The vassal pledged loyalty to the king.
examplePt: O vassalo jurou lealdade ao rei.
tip: A person granted land in exchange for military service and loyalty.

example: The conquistador arrived in the New World.
examplePt: O conquistador chegou ao Novo Mundo.
tip: Spanish for 'conqueror' — used for the Spanish explorers of the Americas.

example: European colonization changed the continent forever.
examplePt: A colonização europeia mudou o continente para sempre.
tip: The act of settling and controlling territory occupied by other peoples.

example: Imperialism expanded European control worldwide.
examplePt: O imperialismo expandiu o controle europeu pelo mundo.
tip: A policy of extending a country's power through territory or influence.

example: The Industrial Revolution transformed manufacturing.
examplePt: A Revolução Industrial transformou a manufatura.
tip: A period of rapid technological and economic change starting in the 1700s.

example: Millions died in the World Wars.
examplePt: Milhões morreram nas Guerras Mundiais.
tip: There have been two so far, in the 20th century, involving most of the world's nations.

example: The Cold War lasted for decades without direct combat.
examplePt: A Guerra Fria durou décadas sem combate direto.
tip: The tense standoff between the US and USSR, never a direct military conflict.

example: The armistice ended the fighting.
examplePt: O armistício encerrou os combates.
tip: An official agreement to stop fighting, before a full peace treaty.

example: The tribunal investigated the genocide.
examplePt: O tribunal investigou o genocídio.
tip: The deliberate, systematic killing of a large group, usually ethnic or national.

example: Museums preserve the memory of the Holocaust.
examplePt: Museus preservam a memória do Holocausto.
tip: The Nazi genocide of six million Jews during World War II.

example: The diaspora kept its traditions alive abroad.
examplePt: A diáspora manteve suas tradições vivas no exterior.
tip: A large group of people spread across the world, away from their original homeland.

example: The war caused a mass exodus of refugees.
examplePt: A guerra causou um êxodo em massa de refugiados.
tip: A mass departure of people, often to escape war or hardship.

example: The uprising was crushed within weeks.
examplePt: O levante foi esmagado em poucas semanas.
tip: An organized rebellion against those in power.

example: The military staged a coup.
examplePt: Os militares deram um golpe de estado.
tip: The 'p' is silent — pronounced 'coo', short for 'coup d'état'.

example: The annexation sparked international protest.
examplePt: A anexação gerou protestos internacionais.
tip: When one country formally takes control of another territory.

example: The partition split the country in two.
examplePt: A partição dividiu o país em dois.
tip: The division of a territory into separate parts, often creating new borders.

example: The Enlightenment promoted reason over tradition.
examplePt: O Iluminismo promoveu a razão sobre a tradição.
tip: An 18th-century movement emphasizing reason, science, and individual rights.

example: The Reformation split the Christian church.
examplePt: A Reforma dividiu a igreja cristã.
tip: The 16th-century religious movement that led to the creation of Protestantism.

example: The Inquisition persecuted those it deemed heretics.
examplePt: A Inquisição perseguiu quem considerava herege.
tip: A church-led institution that investigated and punished religious dissent.

example: The explorer mapped uncharted coastlines.
examplePt: O explorador mapeou litorais desconhecidos.
tip: Someone who travels to discover unfamiliar lands.

example: Their journey home became a decade-long odyssey.
examplePt: A viagem de volta para casa virou uma odisseia de uma década.
tip: A long, adventurous journey — named after Homer's ancient Greek epic poem.

example: The trade route connected two continents.
examplePt: A rota comercial conectava dois continentes.
tip: A path historically used to transport goods between regions.

example: The Silk Road connected China to Europe.
examplePt: A Rota da Seda conectava a China à Europa.
tip: An ancient network of trade routes linking East and West for centuries.

example: Historians call this period the golden age of the empire.
examplePt: Historiadores chamam esse período de idade de ouro do império.
tip: A period of great prosperity, culture, or achievement in a civilization's history.

example: The term 'dark ages' is now considered outdated by many historians.
examplePt: O termo 'Idade das Trevas' hoje é considerado ultrapassado por muitos historiadores.
tip: An older, less accurate term once used for the early medieval period in Europe.

example: The politician promised new reforms.
examplePt: O político prometeu novas reformas.
tip: Someone actively involved in government or elected office.

example: He is remembered as a great statesman.
examplePt: Ele é lembrado como um grande estadista.
tip: A respected, experienced political leader, often used with a positive connotation.

example: The electorate rejected the proposal.
examplePt: O eleitorado rejeitou a proposta.
tip: The entire body of people entitled to vote in an election.

example: She represents a rural constituency.
examplePt: Ela representa uma circunscrição eleitoral rural.
tip: A specific geographic area represented by an elected official.

example: The company spent millions on lobbying.
examplePt: A empresa gastou milhões em lobby.
tip: Trying to influence lawmakers on behalf of a group or cause.

example: The campaign started as a grassroots movement.
examplePt: A campanha começou como um movimento de base.
tip: A movement driven by ordinary people, not organized from the top down.

example: The bill received bipartisan support.
examplePt: O projeto de lei recebeu apoio bipartidário.
tip: Supported by both major political parties.

example: The debate turned overly partisan.
examplePt: O debate ficou excessivamente partidário.
tip: Strongly favoring one political party or side over impartial analysis.

example: The country slid toward autocracy.
examplePt: O país deslizou rumo à autocracia.
tip: A system of government where one person holds absolute power.

example: Critics claim the country is really an oligarchy.
examplePt: Críticos afirmam que o país é, na verdade, uma oligarquia.
tip: Rule by a small group of powerful people, often wealthy elites.

example: The nation is governed as a theocracy.
examplePt: A nação é governada como uma teocracia.
tip: A government ruled by religious leaders or law.

example: The federation includes ten member states.
examplePt: A federação inclui dez estados-membros.
tip: A union of states or regions with a shared central government.

example: The confederation gave states more independence.
examplePt: A confederação deu mais independência aos estados.
tip: Unlike a federation, member states keep more independent power.

example: The region voted for secession.
examplePt: A região votou pela secessão.
tip: The act of formally withdrawing from a larger political union.

example: A plebiscite decided the territory's future.
examplePt: Um plebiscito decidiu o futuro do território.
tip: A direct public vote on a specific, important question.

example: The party whip ensured everyone voted together.
examplePt: O líder de bancada garantiu que todos votassem juntos.
tip: A legislator responsible for keeping party members in line during votes.

example: The senator used a filibuster to delay the vote.
examplePt: O senador usou uma obstrução parlamentar para atrasar a votação.
tip: A tactic of speaking for a very long time to delay a legislative vote.

example: The meeting couldn't start without a quorum.
examplePt: A reunião não pôde começar sem quórum.
tip: The minimum number of members needed to hold a valid vote.

example: The incumbent won re-election easily.
examplePt: O titular do cargo venceu a reeleição com facilidade.
tip: The person currently holding a political office.

example: The president is restricted by a term limit.
examplePt: O presidente é restrito por um limite de mandato.
tip: A legal restriction on how many terms someone can serve in office.

example: The electoral college determines the winner.
examplePt: O colégio eleitoral determina o vencedor.
tip: A group of representatives who formally elect a country's leader, notably in the US.

example: Candidates focus heavily on swing states.
examplePt: Os candidatos focam bastante nos estados indecisos.
tip: A region that could reasonably vote for either major party.

example: Gerrymandering distorts election results.
examplePt: A manipulação de distritos eleitorais distorce resultados eleitorais.
tip: Redrawing voting districts unfairly to favor one political party.

example: The think tank published a new policy report.
examplePt: O grupo de estudos publicou um novo relatório de políticas.
tip: An organization that researches and advises on political or social issues.

example: She has worked in civil service for twenty years.
examplePt: Ela trabalha no serviço público há vinte anos.
tip: The body of government employees who aren't elected or military.

example: The queen serves as head of state.
examplePt: A rainha atua como chefe de Estado.
tip: The official who symbolically represents a country, distinct from the head of government.

example: The prime minister addressed parliament.
examplePt: O primeiro-ministro discursou no parlamento.
tip: The head of government in many parliamentary systems.

example: The law was declared unconstitutional.
examplePt: A lei foi declarada inconstitucional.
tip: Related to or consistent with a country's constitution.

example: The legislature passed the new budget.
examplePt: O Poder Legislativo aprovou o novo orçamento.
tip: The branch of government responsible for making laws.

example: The judiciary remains independent of politics.
examplePt: O Poder Judiciário permanece independente da política.
tip: The branch of government responsible for interpreting laws.

example: The executive branch enforces the laws.
examplePt: O Poder Executivo aplica as leis.
tip: The branch of government responsible for carrying out and enforcing laws.

example: Checks and balances prevent any branch from gaining too much power.
examplePt: Os freios e contrapesos impedem que qualquer poder ganhe força demais.
tip: A system where each branch of government limits the power of the others.

example: The linguist studies dying languages.
examplePt: O linguista estuda idiomas em extinção.
tip: A scientist who studies language, not necessarily someone who speaks many.

example: Morphology studies how words are formed.
examplePt: A morfologia estuda como as palavras são formadas.
tip: The study of the internal structure and formation of words.

example: Pragmatics looks at meaning in context.
examplePt: A pragmática estuda o significado no contexto.
tip: The study of how context influences the meaning of language.

example: English has around 44 phonemes.
examplePt: O inglês tem cerca de 44 fonemas.
tip: The smallest unit of sound that can change the meaning of a word.

example: 'Unhappy' has two morphemes: 'un' and 'happy'.
examplePt: 'Unhappy' tem dois morfemas: 'un' e 'happy'.
tip: The smallest unit of language that carries meaning.

example: The lexicon of this field is very technical.
examplePt: O léxico dessa área é bem técnico.
tip: The complete vocabulary of a language or a specific field.

example: She switches register between formal and casual speech.
examplePt: Ela alterna o registro entre fala formal e casual.
tip: The style or tone of language used, adjusted for the situation.

example: The country shows classic diglossia between two dialects.
examplePt: O país mostra uma diglossia clássica entre dois dialetos.
tip: When two varieties of a language are used in different social situations.

example: Haitian Creole developed from French and African languages.
examplePt: O crioulo haitiano se desenvolveu a partir do francês e de línguas africanas.
tip: A stable language that develops from a mix of different languages over generations.

example: A pidgin formed between traders who spoke different languages.
examplePt: Um pidgin se formou entre comerciantes que falavam idiomas diferentes.
tip: A simplified language used between groups without a common tongue — becomes a creole if passed to children as a first language.

example: 'Karaoke' is a loanword from Japanese.
examplePt: 'Karaokê' é um empréstimo linguístico do japonês.
tip: A word borrowed from another language and adopted into everyday use.

example: 'Family' and 'família' are cognates.
examplePt: 'Family' e 'família' são cognatos.
tip: Words in different languages that share the same origin and look similar.

example: 'Actually' is a false friend for Portuguese speakers.
examplePt: 'Actually' é um falso cognato para falantes de português.
tip: Words that look similar across languages but have different meanings.

example: 'Meat' and 'meet' are homophones.
examplePt: 'Meat' e 'meet' são homófonos.
tip: Words that sound the same but have different meanings and often spellings.

example: 'Bow' (ribbon) and 'bow' (to bend) are homographs.
examplePt: 'Bow' (laço) e 'bow' (curvar-se) são homógrafos.
tip: Words spelled the same but with different meanings and sometimes pronunciations.

example: 'Buzz' and 'sizzle' are examples of onomatopoeia.
examplePt: 'Buzz' e 'sizzle' são exemplos de onomatopeia.
tip: A word that imitates the sound it describes.

example: 'Peter Piper picked' is a classic alliteration.
examplePt: 'Peter Piper picked' é uma aliteração clássica.
tip: The repetition of the same initial sound in nearby words.

example: 'Level' is a palindrome.
examplePt: 'Level' é um palíndromo.
tip: A word or phrase that reads the same forwards and backwards.

example: 'NASA' is a famous acronym.
examplePt: 'NASA' é uma sigla famosa.
tip: A word formed from the first letters of a longer phrase.

example: 'Selfie' was once a neologism.
examplePt: 'Selfie' já foi um neologismo.
tip: A newly coined word or expression, not yet fully established in a language.

example: 'Thou' is an archaism in modern English.
examplePt: 'Thou' é um arcaísmo no inglês moderno.
tip: An old word or expression no longer used in everyday modern speech.

example: 'Passed away' is a euphemism for 'died'.
examplePt: 'Passed away' é um eufemismo para 'morreu'.
tip: A milder, softer way of expressing something unpleasant or blunt.

example: 'I've told you a million times' is hyperbole.
examplePt: 'Eu já te falei um milhão de vezes' é hipérbole.
tip: Exaggeration used for emphasis, not meant to be taken literally.

example: 'Deafening silence' is a classic oxymoron.
examplePt: 'Silêncio ensurdecedor' é um oxímoro clássico.
tip: A phrase that combines two contradictory terms for effect.

example: 'Free gift' is often criticized as a tautology.
examplePt: 'Presente grátis' é frequentemente criticado como tautologia.
tip: Needless repetition of an idea using different words.

example: Saying 'for all intensive purposes' is a malapropism.
examplePt: Dizer 'for all intensive purposes' é um malapropismo.
tip: Mistakenly using a similar-sounding word in place of the correct one, often comically.

example: Bilingual speakers often use code-switching in conversation.
examplePt: Falantes bilíngues costumam usar alternância de código na conversa.
tip: Switching between two or more languages within a single conversation.

example: Her mother tongue is Portuguese.
examplePt: A língua materna dela é o português.
tip: The first language a person learns, usually from their family.

example: English is his second language.
examplePt: O inglês é a segunda língua dele.
tip: Any language learned after the mother tongue.

example: She sounds like a native speaker.
examplePt: Ela fala como uma falante nativa.
tip: Someone who learned a language from birth, as their first language.

example: The interpreter translated the speech live.
examplePt: O intérprete traduziu o discurso ao vivo.
tip: Someone who translates spoken language in real time, unlike a written translator.

example: The interview transcription took hours.
examplePt: A transcrição da entrevista levou horas.
tip: Writing down spoken words exactly as they were said.

example: The dictionary includes a pronunciation guide.
examplePt: O dicionário inclui um guia de pronúncia.
tip: A tool showing how to say a word correctly, often using phonetic symbols.

example: The professor published a new paper.
examplePt: O professor publicou um novo artigo.
tip: Reserved for university-level teachers in English, unlike Portuguese, where it applies to all teachers.

example: She works as an adjunct at two universities.
examplePt: Ela trabalha como professora adjunta em duas universidades.
tip: A part-time or contract professor, without the full status of a tenured one.

example: He received tenure after ten years.
examplePt: Ele conquistou a estabilidade acadêmica depois de dez anos.
tip: A permanent academic position that protects a professor from being easily dismissed.

example: He is a proud alumnus of the university.
examplePt: Ele é um ex-aluno orgulhoso da universidade.
tip: Singular masculine form — 'alumna' is feminine, 'alumni' is plural.

example: The alumni funded the new library.
examplePt: Os ex-alunos financiaram a nova biblioteca.
tip: The plural form of 'alumnus' or 'alumna'.

example: This cohort graduates next spring.
examplePt: Essa turma se forma na próxima primavera.
tip: A group of students who start and progress through a program together.

example: Check the syllabus for the exam dates.
examplePt: Confira a ementa para as datas das provas.
tip: A document outlining the topics, readings, and rules of a course.

example: Her coursework includes weekly essays.
examplePt: O trabalho do curso dela inclui redações semanais.
tip: The assignments and projects completed as part of a course, as opposed to exams.

example: She chose photography as her elective.
examplePt: Ela escolheu fotografia como disciplina eletiva.
tip: An optional course, unlike a required one.

example: Calculus is a prerequisite for this course.
examplePt: Cálculo é pré-requisito para esse curso.
tip: Something you must complete before taking a more advanced course.

example: The program received full accreditation.
examplePt: O programa recebeu credenciamento total.
tip: Official recognition that an institution meets certain quality standards.

example: The professor is on sabbatical this year.
examplePt: O professor está em ano sabático este ano.
tip: A paid break from teaching, often used for research or writing.

example: She received a research fellowship.
examplePt: Ela recebeu uma bolsa de pesquisa avançada.
tip: Funding awarded to support advanced research or study, often after graduation.

example: The lab received a large grant.
examplePt: O laboratório recebeu uma verba considerável.
tip: Money awarded, usually by a government or foundation, to fund research.

example: Researchers gathered at the symposium.
examplePt: Pesquisadores se reuniram no simpósio.
tip: A formal meeting where experts discuss a particular topic.

example: The department hosts a weekly colloquium.
examplePt: O departamento realiza um colóquio semanal.
tip: An academic seminar or discussion, usually less formal than a conference.

example: The journal accepted her manuscript.
examplePt: A revista aceitou o manuscrito dela.
tip: A written work submitted for publication, before it's formally printed.

example: The study was published in a top journal.
examplePt: O estudo foi publicado em uma revista acadêmica de destaque.
tip: A regularly published academic publication featuring research articles.

example: The footnote cites the original source.
examplePt: A nota de rodapé cita a fonte original.
tip: A small note at the bottom of a page, adding detail or a citation.

example: The raw data is in the appendix.
examplePt: Os dados brutos estão no apêndice.
tip: Extra material at the end of a document, supporting the main text.

example: The data set includes ten thousand entries.
examplePt: O conjunto de dados inclui dez mil entradas.
tip: A structured collection of information used for analysis or research.

example: A larger sample size gives more reliable results.
examplePt: Uma amostra maior gera resultados mais confiáveis.
tip: The number of participants or items included in a study.

example: The control group received no treatment.
examplePt: O grupo de controle não recebeu tratamento.
tip: The group in an experiment used as a baseline, receiving no intervention.

example: There's a strong correlation between the two variables.
examplePt: Há uma forte correlação entre as duas variáveis.
tip: A statistical relationship — but remember, correlation doesn't always mean causation.

example: Correlation does not always imply causation.
examplePt: Correlação nem sempre implica causalidade.
tip: When one thing directly causes another, a stronger claim than mere correlation.

example: The study's validity was questioned by critics.
examplePt: A validade do estudo foi questionada por críticos.
tip: Whether a study actually measures what it claims to measure.

example: The test showed high reliability across trials.
examplePt: O teste mostrou alta confiabilidade entre as tentativas.
tip: Whether a study produces consistent results if repeated.

example: Be careful making generalizations from a small sample.
examplePt: Cuidado ao fazer generalizações a partir de uma amostra pequena.
tip: Applying findings from a specific study to a broader population.

example: The program is highly interdisciplinary.
examplePt: O programa é altamente interdisciplinar.
tip: Combining knowledge and methods from more than one academic field.

example: She's doing postdoctoral research in Germany.
examplePt: Ela está fazendo pesquisa pós-doutoral na Alemanha.
tip: Refers to research or study done after completing a doctorate (PhD).

example: The capstone project took an entire semester.
examplePt: O projeto final de curso levou um semestre inteiro.
tip: A culminating project that showcases everything learned in a program.

example: The teacher shared the grading rubric.
examplePt: O professor compartilhou a rubrica de avaliação.
tip: A guide listing the specific criteria used to grade an assignment.
